$x \equiv a - b \pmod{v}$ for exactly one ordered pair $(a, b)$ of elements of $B$.

articles.title: The weak form of Erdős Problem 707 is false
articles.statement:
It is not the case that every finite Sidon set
$A \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ is contained in a perfect difference set modulo $m^2 + m + 1$ for some
natural number $m \ge 1$: there is a finite Sidon set $A \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ such that for every
$m \ge 1$, no set $B \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ with $A \subseteq B$ is a perfect difference set modulo
$m^2 + m + 1$. Here $A$ is Sidon when $w + x = y + z$ with $w, x, y, z \in A$ forces
$\{w, x\} = \{y, z\}$, and $B$ is a perfect difference set modulo $v$ when every nonzero residue
$r$ modulo $v$ satisfies $r \equiv a - b \pmod{v}$ for exactly one ordered pair $(a, b)$ of
elements of $B$.

Alexeev and Mixon proved that the Sidon set $\{1, 2, 4, 8, 13\}$ is contained in no perfect
difference set, and Hall (1947) proved the same for $\{1, 3, 9, 10, 13\}$.

## Sources

- T. F. Bloom, Erdős Problems, Problem #707, https://www.erdosproblems.com/707 (status DISPROVED (LEAN)); resolution: B. Alexeev and D. G. Mixon, Forbidden Sidon subsets of perfect difference sets, featuring a human-assisted proof, arXiv:2510.19804 (2025); M. Hall, Jr., Cyclic projective planes, Duke Math. J. 14 (1947), 1079-1090, abstract of arXiv:2510.19804: {1, 2, 4, 8, 13} is a finite Sidon set contained in no finite perfect difference set; erdosproblems.com/707: {1, 2, 4, 8} cannot be extended to a perfect difference set modulo p² + p + 1 for any prime p, and Hall's {1, 3, 9, 10, 13} cannot be extended to any perfect difference set, https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.19804.

articles.title: Erdős Problem 707, weak form
articles.statement:
The proposition that for every finite Sidon set
$A \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ there are a natural number $m \ge 1$ and a set $B \subseteq \mathbb{N}$
with $A \subseteq B$ such that $B$ is a perfect difference set modulo $m^2 + m + 1$.

This weakens Erdős Problem 707 by allowing any $m \ge 1$ in place of a prime $p$.

articles.title: Erdős Problem 707 is false
articles.statement:
It is not the case that every finite Sidon set
$A \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ is contained in a perfect difference set modulo $p^2 + p + 1$ for some
prime $p$: there is a finite Sidon set $A \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ such that for every prime $p$, no
set $B \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ with $A \subseteq B$ is a perfect difference set modulo
$p^2 + p + 1$. Here $A$ is Sidon when $w + x = y + z$ with $w, x, y, z \in A$ forces
$\{w, x\} = \{y, z\}$, and $B$ is a perfect difference set modulo $v$ when every nonzero residue
$r$ modulo $v$ satisfies $r \equiv a - b \pmod{v}$ for exactly one ordered pair $(a, b)$ of
elements of $B$.

Alexeev and Mixon proved that the Sidon set $\{1, 2, 4, 8\}$ is such a set (their proof is
formalized in Lean); erdosproblems.com/707 lists the problem as disproved.

## Sources

- T. F. Bloom, Erdős Problems, Problem #707, https://www.erdosproblems.com/707 (status DISPROVED (LEAN)); resolution: B. Alexeev and D. G. Mixon, Forbidden Sidon subsets of perfect difference sets, featuring a human-assisted proof, arXiv:2510.19804 (2025); M. Hall, Jr., Cyclic projective planes, Duke Math. J. 14 (1947), 1079-1090, abstract of arXiv:2510.19804: {1, 2, 4, 8, 13} is a finite Sidon set contained in no finite perfect difference set; erdosproblems.com/707: {1, 2, 4, 8} cannot be extended to a perfect difference set modulo p² + p + 1 for any prime p, and Hall's {1, 3, 9, 10, 13} cannot be extended to any perfect difference set, https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.19804.

articles.title: Erdős Problem 707
articles.statement:
The proposition that for every finite Sidon set $A \subseteq \mathbb{N}$
there are a prime $p$ and a set $B \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ with $A \subseteq B$ such that $B$ is a
perfect difference set modulo $p^2 + p + 1$.

articles.title: Erdős Problem 198 is false
articles.statement:
It is not the case that the complement of every Sidon set
$A \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ contains an infinite arithmetic progression: there is a Sidon set
$A \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ such that for all natural numbers $a$ and $d \ge 1$ some term $a + kd$,
$k \in \mathbb{N}$, lies in $A$. Here $A$ is Sidon when $w + x = y + z$ with $w, x, y, z \in A$
forces $\{w, x\} = \{y, z\}$.

To construct such a set, enumerate the infinite progressions $P_1, P_2, \ldots$ and pick
$a_n \in P_n$ with $a_n > 2 a_{n-1}$; the resulting lacunary set is Sidon and meets every infinite
progression. erdosproblems.com/198 records this construction (implicit in Baumgartner's paper) and
the explicit example $\{(n + 1)! + n : n \ge 0\}$.

## Sources

- T. F. Bloom, Erdős Problems, Problem #198, https://www.erdosproblems.com/198 (status DISPROVED (LEAN)); resolution: J. E. Baumgartner, Partitioning vector spaces, J. Combin. Theory Ser. A 18 (1975), 231-233; construction recorded on erdosproblems.com/198, erdosproblems.com/198: answered no; a lacunary set with one element in each infinite progression (implicit in [Ba75]), or explicitly A = {(n + 1)! + n : n ≥ 0}, https://www.erdosproblems.com/198.

articles.title: Erdős Problem 198
articles.statement:
The proposition that the complement of every Sidon set
$A \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ contains an infinite arithmetic progression: for every Sidon set
$A \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ there are natural numbers $a$ and $d \ge 1$ such that $a + kd \notin A$
for every natural number $k$.

articles.title: Large Sidon sets have many isolated sums
articles.statement:
For every natural number $M \ge 1$ there is a
natural number $K$ such that every finite Sidon set $A$ of natural numbers with at least $K$
elements has at least $M$ isolated elements in its sumset $A + A = \{x + y : x, y \in A\}$. Here
$A$ is a Sidon set when $a + b = c + d$ with $a, b, c, d \in A$ implies $\{a, b\} = \{c, d\}$,
and an element $s$ of $A + A$ is isolated when $s + 1 \notin A + A$ and either $s = 0$ or
$s - 1 \notin A + A$.

This answers Erdős Problem 152 affirmatively: Tsoukalas et al. show, with a Lean proof, that
every Sidon set $A$ of $n$ natural numbers has at least $(n^2 - 100n - 16)/16$ isolated elements
in $A + A$.

## Sources

- George Tsoukalas et al., Advancing Mathematics Research with AI-Driven Formal Proof Search, arXiv preprint (2026), arXiv:2605.22763, https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.22763.

articles.title: Erdős Problem 152 on isolated sums of Sidon sets
articles.statement:
A finite set $A$ of natural numbers is
a Sidon set when $a + b = c + d$ with $a, b, c, d \in A$ implies $\{a, b\} = \{c, d\}$, and its
sumset is $A + A = \{x + y : x, y \in A\}$. An element $s$ of a finite set $S$ of natural numbers
is isolated in $S$ when $s + 1 \notin S$ and either $s = 0$ or $s - 1 \notin S$. The proposition
asserts that for every natural number $M \ge 1$ there is a natural number $K$ such that every
finite Sidon set $A$ of natural numbers with at least $K$ elements has at least $M$ isolated
elements in $A + A$.

articles.title: Isolated elements of a set of natural numbers
articles.statement:
Let $S$ be a finite set of natural numbers.
A natural number $a$ is isolated in $S$ when $a \in S$, $a + 1 \notin S$, and either $a = 0$ or
$a - 1 \notin S$.

For $a = 0$ the condition on the predecessor is vacuous, since $0$ has no predecessor among the
natural numbers.

articles.title: Finite Sidon sets of natural numbers
articles.statement:
A finite set $A$ of natural numbers is a Sidon set
when every equality $a + b = c + d$ with $a, b, c, d \in A$ is trivial, that is, $a = c$ and
$b = d$, or $a = d$ and $b = c$.

articles.title: Sidon set
articles.statement:
A set in an additive commutative monoid is Sidon when every equality of
two pairwise sums is trivial up to swapping the summands. Repeated summands
are included.

articles.title: Number of isolated elements
articles.statement:
For a finite set $S$ of natural numbers, the isolated count
of $S$ is the number of elements $a \in S$ with $a + 1 \notin S$ and either $a = 0$ or
$a - 1 \notin S$.

articles.title: Sumset of a finite set of natural numbers
articles.statement:
For a finite set $A$ of natural numbers, the
sumset $A + A$ is the finite set of all sums $x + y$ with $x, y \in A$.

articles.title: Singer's difference set theorem
articles.statement:
For every prime power $q$, there is a subset $D$ of the
cyclic group $\mathbb{Z}/(q^2 + q + 1)\mathbb{Z}$ with $q + 1$ elements such that every nonzero
element $x$ of this group can be written as $x = a - b$ for exactly one ordered pair $(a, b)$ of
elements of $D$.

articles.title: Largest Sidon subset of $\{1, \dots, N\}$ (Green's Problem 31)
articles.statement:
For a natural number
$N$, $F(N)$ is the largest cardinality of a Sidon subset of $[N] = \{1, \dots, N\}$.

articles.title: Lindström's upper bound for Sidon sets can be improved
articles.statement:
Let $F(N)$ be the largest size of a
Sidon subset of $\{1, \dots, N\}$. There are a real constant $c < 1$ and a natural number $N_0$
such that $F(N) \le \sqrt{N} + c N^{1/4}$ for all $N \ge N_0$.

Balogh, Füredi and Roy proved this with $c = 0.998$; Carter, Hunter and O'Bryant later lowered
the constant to $0.98183$.

## Sources

- B. Green, 100 open problems, Problem 31 (manuscript, update of December 2025), https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/open-problems.pdf; resolution: J. Balogh, Z. Füredi and S. Roy, An upper bound on the size of Sidon sets, Amer. Math. Monthly 130 (2023), 437-445, doi:10.1080/00029890.2023.2176667; arXiv:2103.15850, abstract: the maximum size of a Sidon set of {1, ..., n} is at most √n + 0.998 n^{1/4} for sufficiently large n; Green, Problem 31, 'Update 2021' records this bound and its 2023 improvement to 0.98183 (D. Carter, Z. Hunter and K. O'Bryant, Acta Math. Hungar. 175 (2025), 108-126), https://doi.org/10.1080/00029890.2023.2176667.

articles.title: Green's Problem 31: improving Lindström's upper bound
articles.statement:
Let $F(N)$ be the largest
size of a Sidon subset of $\{1, \dots, N\}$. The statement is that there are a real constant
$c < 1$ and a natural number $N_0$ such that $F(N) \le \sqrt{N} + c N^{1/4}$ for all $N \ge N_0$.

Lindström's bound is $F(N) \le N^{1/2} + N^{1/4} + O(1)$; the statement asks for a constant
below $1$ in the second term.

articles.title: Erdős Problem 131 has a negative answer
articles.statement:
It is not true that for every real
$\varepsilon > 0$ there is a natural number $N_0$ such that for every natural number $N \ge 1$ with
$N \ge N_0$ there is a set $S \subseteq \{1, \dots, N\}$ with $|S| > N^{1/2 - \varepsilon}$ that is
divisor-sum-free, meaning that no element $x \in S$ divides the sum of the elements of any nonempty
subset of $S \setminus \{x\}$.

Let $F(N)$ be the largest size of a divisor-sum-free subset of $\{1, \dots, N\}$. Every
divisor-sum-free set is non-averaging, that is, none of its elements is the average of other
elements of the set (an element equal to the average of $k$ others divides their sum), and Pham
and Zakharov (arXiv:2410.14624) prove that the largest non-averaging subset of $\{1, \dots, N\}$
has size $N^{1/4 + o(1)}$, so $F(N) \le N^{1/4 + o(1)}$; erdosproblems.com/131 (checked
2026-10-22) records that this answers the question negatively. The page also links a formal proof
of $F(N) \le N^{1/5 + o(1)}$, which with Csaba's $F(N) \gg N^{1/5}$ would give the order of growth.

## Sources

- H. T. Pham and D. Zakharov, Sharp bound for the Erdős-Straus non-averaging set problem, arXiv:2410.14624 (2024), https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.14624.

articles.title: Erdős Problem 131: large divisor-sum-free sets
articles.statement:
The proposition that for every real
$\varepsilon > 0$ there is a natural number $N_0$ such that for every natural number $N \ge 1$ with
$N \ge N_0$ there is a set $S \subseteq \{1, \dots, N\}$ with $|S| > N^{1/2 - \varepsilon}$ that is
divisor-sum-free: no element $x \in S$ divides the sum of the elements of any nonempty subset of
$S \setminus \{x\}$.

articles.title: Divisor-sum-free sets
articles.statement:
A finite set $S$ of natural numbers is divisor-sum-free if no
element $x \in S$ divides the sum of the elements of any nonempty subset of $S \setminus \{x\}$.

articles.title: Product-free set
articles.statement:
A set $S$ in a type $M$ with a multiplication is product-free if
$xy \notin S$ for all $x, y \in S$, where $x$ and $y$ need not be distinct.

articles.title: Bedert's theorem on large sum-free subsets
articles.statement:
There is a function $\omega$ from the natural
numbers to the real numbers with $\omega(n) \to \infty$ as $n \to \infty$ such that every finite
set $A$ of positive integers contains a subset $B \subseteq A$ with $x + y \notin B$ for all
$x, y \in B$ (a sum-free subset) and $|B| \ge |A|/3 + \omega(|A|)$.

Bedert proves more: every $n$-element set of integers contains a sum-free subset of size at least
$n/3 + c \log \log n$ for an absolute constant $c > 0$. This answers Green's Problem 1.

## Sources

- Benjamin Bedert, Large sum-free subsets of sets of integers via L¹-estimates for trigonometric series, arXiv:2502.08624v1, https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.08624v1.

articles.title: Green's Problem 1 on large sum-free subsets
articles.statement:
The statement that there is a function
$\omega$ from the natural numbers to the real numbers with $\omega(n) \to \infty$ as
$n \to \infty$ such that every finite set $A$ of positive integers contains a sum-free subset
$B \subseteq A$ with $|B| \ge |A|/3 + \omega(|A|)$.

## Sources

- Ben Green, Problem 1 [GREEN-001].

articles.title: Sum-free sets of natural numbers
articles.statement:
A finite set $S$ of natural numbers is sum-free if
$x + y \notin S$ for all $x, y \in S$, where $x = y$ is allowed.

## Sources

- [GREEN-001].

articles.title: Non-averaging sets
articles.statement:
A finite set $A$ of natural numbers is non-averaging if no $a \in A$ is
the arithmetic mean of a nonempty set $S \subseteq A \setminus \{a\}$, that is,
$\sum_{s \in S} s \ne |S| \cdot a$ for every $a \in A$ and every nonempty
$S \subseteq A \setminus \{a\}$.

Equivalently, no element of $A$ is the arithmetic mean of at least two distinct elements of $A$.

articles.title: Pham–Zakharov theorem on non-averaging sets
articles.statement:
For every $\varepsilon > 0$ and every
sufficiently large $N$, some non-averaging subset of $\{1, \dots, N\}$ has at least
$N^{1/4 - \varepsilon}$ elements, and every non-averaging subset of $\{1, \dots, N\}$ has at most
$N^{1/4 + \varepsilon}$ elements. Thus the largest non-averaging subset of $\{1, \dots, N\}$ has
size $N^{1/4 + o(1)}$.

Bosznay constructed non-averaging subsets of $\{1, \dots, N\}$ of size $\gg N^{1/4}$, and Pham and
Zakharov proved the matching upper bound $N^{1/4 + o(1)}$.

## Sources

- T. F. Bloom, Erdős Problems, Problem #186, https://www.erdosproblems.com/186 (status SOLVED); resolution: H. T. Pham and D. Zakharov, Sharp bound for the Erdős-Straus non-averaging set problem, Geom. Funct. Anal. 35 (2025), 1712-1738, arXiv:2410.14624 (upper bound); Á. P. Bosznay, On the lower estimation of non-averaging sets, Acta Math. Hungar. 53 (1989), 155-157 (lower bound), Pham-Zakharov main theorem: the largest non-averaging subset of {1, …, n} has size n^{1/4 + o(1)}; erdosproblems.com/186: N^{1/4} ≪ F(N) ≪ N^{1/4 + o(1)}, https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.14624.

articles.title: Erdős Problem 186 on non-averaging sets
articles.statement:
For every $\varepsilon > 0$ and every sufficiently
large $N$, the largest non-averaging subset of $\{1, \dots, N\}$ has size between
$N^{1/4 - \varepsilon}$ and $N^{1/4 + \varepsilon}$: some non-averaging subset of
$\{1, \dots, N\}$ has at least $N^{1/4 - \varepsilon}$ elements, and every non-averaging subset
of $\{1, \dots, N\}$ has at most $N^{1/4 + \varepsilon}$ elements. In short, the largest
non-averaging subset of $\{1, \dots, N\}$ has size $N^{1/4 + o(1)}$.

articles.title: Maximal sum-free subsets of $\{1, \dots, n\}$ number $o(2^{n/2})$
articles.statement:
Let $f_m(n)$ be the
number of maximal sum-free subsets of $\{1, \dots, n\}$. Then $f_m(n) / 2^{n/2} \to 0$ as
$n \to \infty$, that is, $f_m(n) = o(2^{n/2})$.

## Sources

- T. F. Bloom, Erdős Problems, Problem #877, https://www.erdosproblems.com/877 (status PROVED); resolution: T. Łuczak and T. Schoen, On the number of maximal sum-free sets, Proc. Amer. Math. Soc. 129 (2001), 2205-2207, abstract: {1, 2, …, n} contains at most 2^{n/2 - 2^{-28} n} maximal sum-free subsets, provided n is large enough; erdosproblems.com/877: this resolves the question, and Balogh, Liu, Sharifzadeh and Treglown later proved f_m(n) = 2^{(1/4 + o(1)) n}, https://doi.org/10.1090/S0002-9939-00-05815-9.

articles.title: Erdős Problem 877 on maximal sum-free sets
articles.statement:
Let $f_m(n)$ be the number of maximal
sum-free subsets of $\{1, \dots, n\}$. This is the statement, asked by Cameron and Erdős, that
$f_m(n) / 2^{n/2} \to 0$ as $n \to \infty$, that is, $f_m(n) = o(2^{n/2})$.

articles.title: Number of maximal sum-free subsets of $\{1, \dots, n\}$
articles.statement:
For a natural number $n$,
$f_m(n)$ is the number of sets $A \subseteq \{1, \dots, n\}$ that are sum-free, meaning
$x + y \notin A$ for all $x, y \in A$ (including $x = y$), and maximal with this property:
every sum-free set $B$ with $A \subseteq B \subseteq \{1, \dots, n\}$ equals $A$.

articles.title: Sum-free subsets of $\{1, \dots, n\}$ number $2^{(1 + o(1)) n / 2}$
articles.statement:
Let $f(n)$ be the
number of sum-free subsets of $\{1, \dots, n\}$, that is, of sets $A \subseteq \{1, \dots, n\}$
with no $a, b, c \in A$ satisfying $a = b + c$ (the case $b = c$ included). Then
$\log_2 f(n) / n \to 1/2$ as $n \to \infty$, that is, $f(n) = 2^{(1 + o(1)) n / 2}$.

## Sources

- T. F. Bloom, Erdős Problems, Problem #748, https://www.erdosproblems.com/748 (status PROVED); resolution: B. Green, The Cameron-Erdős conjecture, Bull. London Math. Soc. 36 (2004), 769-778; A. A. Sapozhenko, The Cameron-Erdős conjecture, Dokl. Akad. Nauk 393 (2003), 749-752, abstract of arXiv:math/0304058 (Green): the number of sum-free subsets of {1, …, N} is O(2^{N/2}); erdosproblems.com/748: true, in fact f(n) ≪ 2^{n/2} (Green; Sapozhenko), with the trivial lower bound from subsets of the upper half, https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0304058.

articles.title: Erdős Problem 748 on the number of sum-free sets
articles.statement:
Let $f(n)$ be the number of sum-free
subsets of $\{1, \dots, n\}$. This is the statement that $\log_2 f(n) / n \to 1/2$ as
$n \to \infty$, that is, $f(n) = 2^{(1 + o(1)) n / 2}$.

articles.title: Number of sum-free subsets of $\{1, \dots, n\}$
articles.statement:
For a natural number $n$, $f(n)$ is the
number of sets $A \subseteq \{1, \dots, n\}$ that are sum-free, meaning that there are no
$a, b, c \in A$ with $a = b + c$ (the case $b = c$ included). The empty set is counted.

articles.title: Square-sum-free sets
articles.statement:
A finite set $A$ of natural numbers is square-sum-free if for all
$a, b \in A$, not necessarily distinct, the sum $a + b$ is not a perfect square.

articles.title: Maximal density of square-sum-free sets (Erdős Problem 438)
articles.statement:
For a natural number $N$, let
$M(N)$ be the largest size of a set $A \subseteq \{1, \dots, N\}$ such that no sum $a + b$ with
$a, b \in A$, not necessarily distinct, is a perfect square. Then $M(N) / N \to 11/32$ as
$N \to \infty$.

Khalfalah, Lodha and Szemerédi proved $M(N) \le (11/32 + o(1)) N$, and Massias's example (the
integers congruent to one of $1, 5, 9, 13, 14, 17, 21, 25, 26, 29, 30$ modulo $32$) gives
$M(N) \ge 11N/32 + O(1)$.

## Sources

- T. F. Bloom, Erdős Problems, Problem #438, https://www.erdosproblems.com/438 (status SOLVED); resolution: A. Khalfalah, S. Lodha and E. Szemerédi, Tight bound for the density of sequence of integers the sum of no two of which is a perfect square, Discrete Math. (2002), 243-255, max |A| ≤ (11/32 + o(1)) N; Massias's residues mod 32 give the lower bound (erdosproblems.com/438).

articles.title: Erdős Problem 438 (statement)
articles.statement:
For a natural number $N$, let $M(N)$ be the largest size of
a set $A \subseteq \{1, \dots, N\}$ such that no sum $a + b$ with $a, b \in A$, not necessarily
distinct, is a perfect square. This is the statement that $M(N) / N \to 11/32$ as
$N \to \infty$.

articles.title: Maximum size of a square-sum-free set
articles.statement:
For a natural number $N$, the largest size of a set
$A \subseteq \{1, \dots, N\}$ such that no sum $a + b$ with $a, b \in A$, not necessarily distinct,
is a perfect square.

articles.title: Edges of the distinct link graph
articles.statement:
Let $G$ be a set with an addition and $S \subseteq G$.
Two elements $x, y \in G$ are adjacent in the distinct link graph of $S$ if $x \ne y$ and there
is some $s \in S$, different from both $x$ and $y$, with $x + y = s$, $x + s = y$ or $y + s = x$.
In an abelian group this says exactly that $\{x, y, s\}$ is a distinct Schur triple for some
$s \in S$. In the paper's graph $L^*_S[B]$ with vertex set $B$, these are the edges between
distinct vertices; the relation itself does not depend on $B$.

## Sources

- Nathanaël Hassler and Andrew Treglown, *Notes on Sum-Free Sets in Abelian Groups*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A97, Definition 2 (i).

articles.title: Loops of the distinct link graph
articles.statement:
Let $G$ be a set with an addition and $S \subseteq G$.
An element $x \in G$ carries a loop in the distinct link graph of $S$ if there are distinct
$s, s' \in S$, both different from $x$, with $s + s' = x$, $x + s = s'$ or $x + s' = s$. In an
abelian group this says exactly that $\{x, s, s'\}$ is a distinct Schur triple for some distinct
$s, s' \in S$.

## Sources

- Nathanaël Hassler and Andrew Treglown, *Notes on Sum-Free Sets in Abelian Groups*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A97, Definition 2 (ii).

articles.title: Number of distinct Schur triples
articles.statement:
For a subset $F$ of a set $G$ with an addition, this is
the number of ordered pairs $(x, y)$ with $x, y \in F$ such that $x$, $y$ and $x + y$ are pairwise
distinct and $x + y \in F$, that is, the number of ordered distinct Schur triples $(x, y, x + y)$
in $F$. If there are infinitely many such pairs, the value is $0$ by convention.

## Sources

- Nathanaël Hassler and Andrew Treglown, *Notes on Sum-Free Sets in Abelian Groups*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A97, introduction and Lemma 1.

articles.title: Green–Ruzsa structure lemma
articles.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite abelian group of type $\mathrm{I}(p)$ and
let $k$ be a natural number with $p = 3k + 2$. If $A \subseteq G$ is sum-free and
$|A| > \left(\frac{1}{3} + \frac{1}{3(p + 1)}\right)|G|$, then there is a group homomorphism
$\psi : G \to \mathbb{Z}_p$ with $\psi(a) \in \{k + 1, \dots, 2k + 1\}$ for every $a \in A$,
where $\mathbb{Z}_p$ is identified with $\{0, 1, \dots, p - 1\}$.

## Sources

- Nathanaël Hassler and Andrew Treglown, *Notes on Sum-Free Sets in Abelian Groups*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A97, Lemma 2.

articles.title: Container lemma
articles.statement:
For every real $\delta > 0$ there is a natural number $n_0$ such that
every finite abelian group $G$ of order $n \ge n_0$ has a family $\mathcal{F}$ of subsets of $G$
with the following properties: (i) each $F \in \mathcal{F}$ contains at most $\delta n^2$ ordered
distinct Schur triples $(x, y, x + y)$; (ii) every distinct sum-free subset of $G$ is contained
in some $F \in \mathcal{F}$; (iii) $|\mathcal{F}| \le 2^{\delta n}$; (iv) every
$F \in \mathcal{F}$ is of the form $A \cup B$ with $A$ sum-free and $|B| \le \delta n$.

## Sources

- Nathanaël Hassler and Andrew Treglown, *Notes on Sum-Free Sets in Abelian Groups*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A97, Lemma 1.

articles.title: The empty set is independent in the distinct link graph
articles.statement:
For every set $G$ with an
addition and all $S, B \subseteq G$, the empty set is an independent set of the distinct link
graph $L^*_S[B]$.

## Sources

- Nathanaël Hassler and Andrew Treglown, *Notes on Sum-Free Sets in Abelian Groups*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A97, Definition 2.

articles.title: Independent sets of the distinct link graph
articles.statement:
Let $G$ be a set with an addition and let
$S, B, I \subseteq G$. The set $I$ is an independent set of the distinct link graph $L^*_S[B]$
(the graph on vertex set $B$ given by the edges and loops of the distinct link graph of $S$) if
$I \subseteq B$, no element of $I$ carries a loop, and no two elements of $I$ are adjacent.

## Sources

- Nathanaël Hassler and Andrew Treglown, *Notes on Sum-Free Sets in Abelian Groups*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A97, Definition 2.

articles.title: Sum-free sets are distinct sum-free
articles.statement:
For every set $G$ with an addition, every sum-free
subset of $G$ is distinct sum-free.

## Sources

- Nathanaël Hassler and Andrew Treglown, *Notes on Sum-Free Sets in Abelian Groups*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A97, introduction.

articles.title: Distinct sum-free sets
articles.statement:
Let $G$ be a set with an addition. A subset $S \subseteq G$ is
distinct sum-free if there are no pairwise distinct $x, y, z \in S$ with $x + y = z$, that is, if
$S$ contains no distinct Schur triple.

## Sources

- Nathanaël Hassler and Andrew Treglown, *Notes on Sum-Free Sets in Abelian Groups*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A97, introduction.

articles.title: The empty set is sum-free
articles.statement:
For every set $G$ with an addition, the empty subset of $G$ is
sum-free.

## Sources

- Nathanaël Hassler and Andrew Treglown, *Notes on Sum-Free Sets in Abelian Groups*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A97, introduction.

articles.title: Sum-free set
articles.statement:
Let $G$ be a set with an addition. A subset $S \subseteq G$ is sum-free if
$x + y \notin S$ for all $x, y \in S$, where $x = y$ is allowed; that is, $S$ contains no Schur
triple $x + y = z$ with $x, y, z \in S$.

## Sources

- Nathanaël Hassler and Andrew Treglown, *Notes on Sum-Free Sets in Abelian Groups*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A97, introduction.

articles.title: Characterization of type I(p)
articles.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite set and $p$ a natural number. Then $G$
is of type $\mathrm{I}(p)$ if and only if $p$ is prime, $p \equiv 2 \pmod 3$, $p$ divides $|G|$,
and $p \le q$ for every prime $q$ with $q \equiv 2 \pmod 3$ that divides $|G|$.

## Sources

- Nathanaël Hassler and Andrew Treglown, *Notes on Sum-Free Sets in Abelian Groups*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A97, Definition 1.

articles.title: Groups of type I(p)
articles.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite set and $p$ a natural number. $G$ is of type
$\mathrm{I}(p)$ if $p$ is the smallest prime with $p \equiv 2 \pmod 3$ dividing $|G|$: that is,
$p$ is prime, $p \equiv 2 \pmod 3$, $p$ divides $|G|$, and $p \le q$ for every prime $q$ with
$q \equiv 2 \pmod 3$ that divides $|G|$.

Only the order of $G$ is used; in the paper $G$ is a finite abelian group.

## Sources

- Nathanaël Hassler and Andrew Treglown, *Notes on Sum-Free Sets in Abelian Groups*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A97, Definition 1.

articles.title: Trivial bound on sum-free subsets
articles.statement:
Let $G$ be a set with an addition. For every finite
subset $S \subseteq G$, the largest size of a sum-free subset of $S$ is at most $|S|$.

## Sources

- Nathanaël Hassler and Andrew Treglown, *Notes on Sum-Free Sets in Abelian Groups*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A97, introduction.

articles.title: Diananda–Yap and Green–Ruzsa theorem
articles.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite abelian group of order $n$, and
let $\mu(G)$ be the largest size of a sum-free subset of $G$. If $G$ is of type $\mathrm{I}(p)$
for a natural number $p$, then $\mu(G) = n\left(\frac{1}{3} + \frac{1}{3p}\right)$. If no prime
$q \equiv 2 \pmod 3$ divides $n$ and $3 \mid n$ (type $\mathrm{II}$), then $\mu(G) = n/3$. If no
prime $q \equiv 2 \pmod 3$ divides $n$ and $3 \nmid n$ (type $\mathrm{III}$), then
$\mu(G) = n\left(\frac{1}{3} - \frac{1}{3m}\right)$, where $m$ is the exponent of $G$.

The paper quotes this result from Diananda–Yap and Green–Ruzsa.

## Sources

- Nathanaël Hassler and Andrew Treglown, *Notes on Sum-Free Sets in Abelian Groups*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A97, Theorem 1, with Definition 1.

articles.title: Size of a largest sum-free subset
articles.statement:
Let $G$ be a set with an addition and $S \subseteq G$.
Write $\mu(S)$ for the supremum in $\mathbb{N}$ of the sizes of the finite sum-free subsets of
$S$ (sets $T$ with $x + y \notin T$ for all $x, y \in T$), taken to be $0$ if these sizes are
unbounded. For finite $S$ this is the largest size of a sum-free subset of $S$, and $\mu(G)$ is
the value for $S = G$.

## Sources

- Nathanaël Hassler and Andrew Treglown, *Notes on Sum-Free Sets in Abelian Groups*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A97, introduction (`μ(G)`) and Theorem 2.

articles.title: Sharp lower bound on maximal distinct sum-free sets
articles.statement:
Write $f^*_{\max}(G)$ for the number
of maximal distinct sum-free subsets of an abelian group $G$. There is a natural number $C$ such
that for every real $\eta > 0$ there is $n_0$ with the following property. Let $r_1, r_2 \ge 0$
with $r = r_1 + r_2 \ge 1$, let $\alpha_1, \dots, \alpha_{r_1} \ge 2$, let $K$ be a finite
abelian group of odd order, and let
$G = \mathbb{Z}_{2^{\alpha_1}} \oplus \dots \oplus \mathbb{Z}_{2^{\alpha_{r_1}}} \oplus
\mathbb{Z}_2^{r_2} \oplus K$ have order $n$. If $n \ge n_0$ and $n / 2^r \ge C$, then

$$(2^{2r-1} + 2^{r+r_1-1} - 2^{r+1} + 2^{r_1})\, 2^{n/4} +
(2^r - 2^{r_1} - \eta)\, 2^{n/4 - 2^{r-2}} \le f^*_{\max}(G).$$

## Sources

- Nathanaël Hassler and Andrew Treglown, *Notes on Sum-Free Sets in Abelian Groups*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A97, Theorem 6.

articles.title: Maximal distinct sum-free sets in groups of even order
articles.statement:
Write $f^*_{\max}(G)$ for the
number of maximal distinct sum-free subsets of an abelian group $G$. There is a natural number
$C$ such that for every real $\varepsilon > 0$ there is $n_0$ with the following property. Let
$r \ge 1$, let $\alpha_1, \dots, \alpha_r \ge 1$, let $K$ be a finite abelian group of odd order,
and let $G = \mathbb{Z}_{2^{\alpha_1}} \oplus \dots \oplus \mathbb{Z}_{2^{\alpha_r}} \oplus K$
have order $n$. If $n \ge n_0$ and $n / 2^r \ge C$, then
$2^{(1/4 - \varepsilon) n} \le f^*_{\max}(G) \le 2^{(1/4 + \varepsilon) n}$.

## Sources

- Nathanaël Hassler and Andrew Treglown, *Notes on Sum-Free Sets in Abelian Groups*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A97, Theorem 4.

articles.title: Sharp upper bound on maximal distinct sum-free sets
articles.statement:
Write $f^*_{\max}(G)$ for the number
of maximal distinct sum-free subsets of an abelian group $G$. There is a natural number $C$ such
that for every real $\eta > 0$ there is $n_0$ with the following property. Let $r_1, r_2 \ge 0$
with $r = r_1 + r_2 \ge 1$, let $\alpha_1, \dots, \alpha_{r_1} \ge 2$, let $K$ be a finite
abelian group of odd order, and let
$G = \mathbb{Z}_{2^{\alpha_1}} \oplus \dots \oplus \mathbb{Z}_{2^{\alpha_{r_1}}} \oplus
\mathbb{Z}_2^{r_2} \oplus K$ have order $n$. If $n \ge n_0$ and $n / 2^r \ge C$, then

$$f^*_{\max}(G) \le (2^{2r-1} + 2^{r+r_1-1} - 2^{r+1} + 2^{r_1})\, 2^{n/4} +
(2^r - 2^{r_1} + \eta)\, 2^{n/4 - 2^{r-2}}.$$

## Sources

- Nathanaël Hassler and Andrew Treglown, *Notes on Sum-Free Sets in Abelian Groups*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A97, Theorem 5.

articles.title: Number of maximal distinct sum-free sets
articles.statement:
Let $G$ be a set with an addition. The number
$f^*_{\max}(G)$ is the number of subsets of $G$ that are maximal, with respect to inclusion, among
the distinct sum-free subsets of $G$, and it is $0$ if there are infinitely many such subsets.
Here $S \subseteq G$ is distinct sum-free if $x + y \notin S$ for all $x, y \in S$ such that $x$,
$y$ and $x + y$ are pairwise distinct.

## Sources

- Nathanaël Hassler and Andrew Treglown, *Notes on Sum-Free Sets in Abelian Groups*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A97, section "Maximal distinct sum-free subsets".

articles.title: Almost triangle-free bound
articles.statement:
Let $\Gamma$ be a finite graph, let $T$ be a set of vertices
of $\Gamma$, let $n \ge 1$ and $D \ge 1$ be integers, and let $k$ be a real number. Suppose
that the graph $\Gamma'$ obtained from $\Gamma$ by deleting $T$ is triangle-free, has $n$
vertices and has at least $n/2 + k$ edges, and that $\Gamma$ has maximum degree
$\Delta(\Gamma) \le D$. Then the number $\mathrm{mis}(\Gamma)$ of maximal independent sets of
$\Gamma$ satisfies $\mathrm{mis}(\Gamma) \le 2^{n/2 - k/(100D^2) + 2|T|}$.

## Sources

- Nathanaël Hassler and Andrew Treglown, *Notes on Sum-Free Sets in Abelian Groups*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A97, Lemma 6.

articles.title: Liu–Sharifzadeh stability bound
articles.statement:
Let $\Gamma$ be a graph with $n$ vertices, $n + k$
edges for an integer $k$, and maximum degree $\Delta \ge 1$. Then the number
$\mathrm{mis}(\Gamma)$ of maximal independent sets of $\Gamma$ satisfies
$\mathrm{mis}(\Gamma) \le 3^{\Delta/13} \cdot 3^{n/3 - k/(13\Delta)}$.

## Sources

- Nathanaël Hassler and Andrew Treglown, *Notes on Sum-Free Sets in Abelian Groups*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A97, Lemma 7.

articles.title: Balogh–Liu–Sharifzadeh–Treglown bound
articles.statement:
Let $k \ge 1$ be a real number and let $\Gamma$
be a finite graph with $n$ vertices, minimum degree $\delta(\Gamma)$ and maximum degree
$\Delta(\Gamma) \le k\,\delta(\Gamma)$, and put $b = \sqrt{\delta(\Gamma)}$. Then the number
$\mathrm{mis}(\Gamma)$ of maximal independent sets of $\Gamma$ satisfies
$\mathrm{mis}(\Gamma) \le \bigl(\sum_{0 \le i \le n/b} \binom{n}{i}\bigr) \cdot
3^{\frac{k}{k+1} \cdot \frac{n}{3} + \frac{2n}{3b}}$, where $n/b$ and $2n/(3b)$ are read as $0$
when $\delta(\Gamma) = 0$.

## Sources

- Nathanaël Hassler and Andrew Treglown, *Notes on Sum-Free Sets in Abelian Groups*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A97, Lemma 5.

articles.title: Number of maximal independent sets
articles.statement:
For a graph $\Gamma$, $\mathrm{mis}(\Gamma)$ is the
number of maximal independent sets of $\Gamma$, that is, of sets of pairwise non-adjacent
vertices that are not properly contained in another such set; it is $0$ if there are
infinitely many.

## Sources

- Nathanaël Hassler and Andrew Treglown, *Notes on Sum-Free Sets in Abelian Groups*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A97, subsection "Maximal independent sets in graphs".

articles.title: Counting maximal sum-free sets in elementary abelian 2- and 3-groups
articles.statement:
Let $f_{\max}(G)$
be the number of maximal sum-free subsets of $G$. As $k \to \infty$, with $n = 2^k$,
$f_{\max}(\mathbb{Z}_2^k) = \bigl(\binom{n-1}{2} + o(1)\bigr) 2^{n/4}$, and with $n = 3^k$,
$f_{\max}(\mathbb{Z}_3^k) = \bigl((n-3)(n-1)/3 + o(1)\bigr) 3^{n/9}$; that is,
$f_{\max}(\mathbb{Z}_2^k)/2^{n/4} - \binom{n-1}{2} \to 0$ and
$f_{\max}(\mathbb{Z}_3^k)/3^{n/9} - (n-3)(n-1)/3 \to 0$.

## Sources

- Nathanaël Hassler and Andrew Treglown, *Notes on Sum-Free Sets in Abelian Groups*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A97, Theorem 3.

articles.title: Number of maximal sum-free sets
articles.statement:
For a set $G$ with an addition, $f_{\max}(G)$ is the
number of maximal sum-free subsets of $G$, that is, of sets $S \subseteq G$ with $x + y \notin S$
for all $x, y \in S$ (including $x = y$) that are not properly contained in another such set;
it is $0$ if there are infinitely many.

## Sources

- Nathanaël Hassler and Andrew Treglown, *Notes on Sum-Free Sets in Abelian Groups*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A97, introduction.

articles.title: Link-graph extension lemma
articles.statement:
Let $G$ be an abelian group and let $B, S \subseteq G$ be
disjoint distinct sum-free sets. If $I \subseteq B$ and $S \cup I$ is a maximal distinct
sum-free subset of $G$, then $I$ is a maximal independent set of the distinct link graph
$L^*_S[B]$: a subset of $B$ with no looped vertex and no two adjacent vertices that is not
properly contained in another such set.

Disjointness of $B$ and $S$ is needed: for $G = \mathbb{Z}_2$, $S = G$, $B = \{0\}$ and
$I = \emptyset$ the conclusion fails.

## Sources

- Nathanaël Hassler and Andrew Treglown, *Notes on Sum-Free Sets in Abelian Groups*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A97, Lemma 8.

articles.title: Counting subgroups by order and by index
articles.statement:
In a finite abelian group $G$, for every
natural number $k$ the number of subgroups of order $k$ equals the number of subgroups of
index $k$.

## Sources

- Nathanaël Hassler and Andrew Treglown, *Notes on Sum-Free Sets in Abelian Groups*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A97, Lemma 3.

articles.title: Ranks of the index-two subgroups of a finite abelian 2-group
articles.statement:
Let $r_1, r_2$ be natural
numbers with $r = r_1 + r_2 \ge 1$, let $\alpha_1, \dots, \alpha_{r_1} \ge 2$, and let
$G = \mathbb{Z}_{2^{\alpha_1}} \oplus \dots \oplus \mathbb{Z}_{2^{\alpha_{r_1}}} \oplus
\mathbb{Z}_2^{r_2}$. Then exactly $2^{r_1} - 1$ subgroups of $G$ of index $2$ have rank $r$,
and exactly $2^r - 2^{r_1}$ subgroups of $G$ of index $2$ have rank $r - 1$, where the rank
of a group is the minimal number of its generators.

## Sources

- Nathanaël Hassler and Andrew Treglown, *Notes on Sum-Free Sets in Abelian Groups*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A97, Lemma 4.

articles.title: Random sum-free sets
articles.statement:
For a finite abelian group $G$ let $\mu(G)$ be the size of a
largest sum-free subset of $G$. Let $(G_n)_{n \ge 0}$ be finite abelian groups with
$|G_i| < |G_j|$ and $\mu(G_i)/|G_i| = \mu(G_j)/|G_j|$ whenever $i < j$. Then for every
$\varepsilon > 0$ there is $C > 0$ such that for every real sequence $(p_n)$ with
$C |G_n|^{-1/2} \le p_n \le 1$ for all $n$, the probability that the largest sum-free subset
of the binomial random subset $G_{n,p_n}$ has size within $\varepsilon \mu(G_n) p_n$ of
$\mu(G_n) p_n$ tends to $1$ as $n \to \infty$. Here $G_{n,p}$ contains each element of $G_n$
independently with probability $p$, so this probability is
$\sum_S p_n^{|S|} (1-p_n)^{|G_n|-|S|}$ over the subsets $S \subseteq G_n$ with that property.

## Sources

- Nathanaël Hassler and Andrew Treglown, *Notes on Sum-Free Sets in Abelian Groups*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A97, Theorem 2.

articles.title: Maximal distinct sum-free sets in groups of type $I(p)$
articles.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite abelian
group and let $p \ge 5$ be such that $G$ is of type $I(p)$, that is, $p$ is the smallest prime
with $p \equiv 2 \pmod 3$ that divides $|G|$. Call $S \subseteq G$ sum-free if $x + y \notin S$
for all $x, y \in S$, and distinct sum-free if $x + y \notin S$ for all $x, y \in S$ such that
$x$, $y$ and $x + y$ are pairwise distinct. Let $\mu(G)$ be the size of a largest sum-free subset
of $G$, and let $f^*_{\max}(G)$ be the number of maximal distinct sum-free subsets of $G$. Then
$f^*_{\max}(G) \ge 2^{\mu(G)/2}$.

## Sources

- Nathanaël Hassler and Andrew Treglown, *Notes on Sum-Free Sets in Abelian Groups*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A97, Proposition 1.

articles.title: Cauchy–Davenport–Chowla theorem
articles.statement:
Let $q$ be a positive integer and let $A$ and $B$ be
nonempty subsets of $\mathbb{Z}/q\mathbb{Z}$ such that $0 \in B$ and every nonzero element of $B$
is a unit of $\mathbb{Z}/q\mathbb{Z}$. Then $|A + B| \ge \min(q, |A| + |B| - 1)$, where
$A + B = \{a + b : a \in A, b \in B\}$.

## Sources

- R. C. Vaughan, *The Hardy–Littlewood Method*, 2nd ed., Cambridge Tracts in Mathematics 125, Cambridge University Press, 1997, Lemma 2.14; also stated as Lemma 3.5 in H. Wang and S. Tian, arXiv:2608.12397v1. Mathlib's `ZMod.cauchy_davenport` covers the prime-modulus special case.

articles.title: Full-dimensional sets in $\mathbb{Z}^d$
articles.statement:
A finite set $A \subseteq \mathbb{Z}^d$ is
full-dimensional when it is not contained in an affine hyperplane: for every real vector
$a \in \mathbb{R}^d$ and every real number $c$, if $\sum_i a_i x_i = c$ for all $x \in A$, then
$a = 0$.

articles.title: Conlon–Lim theorem: Stanchescu's difference set bound holds
articles.statement:
For every integer $d \ge 2$ there
is a natural number $N$ such that every finite set $A \subseteq \mathbb{Z}^d$ with $|A| \ge N$ that
is not contained in an affine hyperplane (no nonzero real linear functional is constant on $A$)
satisfies $|A - A| \ge \left(2d - 2 + \frac{1}{d - 1}\right)|A| - (2d^2 - 4d + 3)$, where
$A - A = \{a - b : a, b \in A\}$ is the difference set of $A$.

## Sources

- Problems presented at the workshop on recent trends in additive combinatorics, collected by E. Croot and V. F. Lev, AIM workshop problem list, Problem 2.6 (Y. Stanchescu), https://aimath.org/WWN/additivecomb/additivecomb.pdf; resolution: D. Conlon and J. Lim, Difference sets in ℝ^d, Israel J. Math. 267 (2025) 729-748, arXiv:2110.09053, abstract and main theorem, https://arxiv.org/abs/2110.09053.

articles.title: Statement of Stanchescu's difference set bound
articles.statement:
The proposition that for every integer
$d \ge 2$ there is a natural number $N$ such that every full-dimensional finite set
$A \subseteq \mathbb{Z}^d$ (one not contained in an affine hyperplane) with $|A| \ge N$ satisfies
$|A - A| \ge \left(2d - 2 + \frac{1}{d - 1}\right)|A| - (2d^2 - 4d + 3)$, where
$A - A = \{a - b : a, b \in A\}$ is the difference set of $A$.

articles.title: Consecutive sums
articles.statement:
Let $k \in \mathbb{N}$ and let $a_0, \dots, a_{k-1}$ be natural
numbers. The consecutive sums of $a$ form the finite set of natural numbers
$a_u + a_{u+1} + \dots + a_v$ for indices $0 \le u \le v \le k - 1$.

articles.title: Erdős Problem 356 has a positive answer
articles.statement:
There is a real number $c > 0$ such that for all
sufficiently large $n \in \mathbb{N}$ there exist $k \in \mathbb{N}$ and natural numbers
$a_0 < a_1 < \dots < a_{k-1}$ with $1 \le a_i \le n$ for every $i$, whose set of consecutive sums
$a_u + a_{u+1} + \dots + a_v$ (for $u \le v$) has at least $c n^2$ elements.

## Sources

- T. F. Bloom, Erdős Problems, Problem #356, https://www.erdosproblems.com/356 (status PROVED (LEAN)); resolution: A. Beker, On a problem of Erdős and Graham about consecutive sums in strictly increasing sequences, arXiv:2311.10087 (2023), erdosproblems.com/356: the original problem was solved in the affirmative by Beker, https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.10087.

articles.title: Erdős Problem 356
articles.statement:
The proposition that there is a real number $c > 0$ such that for all
sufficiently large $n \in \mathbb{N}$ there exist $k \in \mathbb{N}$ and natural numbers
$a_0 < a_1 < \dots < a_{k-1}$ with $1 \le a_i \le n$ for every $i$, whose set of consecutive sums
$a_u + a_{u+1} + \dots + a_v$ (for $u \le v$) has at least $c n^2$ elements.

articles.title: x² + xy is an explicit expander over prime fields
articles.statement:
Bourgain's expander property for
$f(x, y) = x^2 + xy$ holds: there is a real $\varepsilon > 0$ such that for every real $C \ge 1$
there are a real $c > 0$ and a natural number $p_0$ such that for every prime $p \ge p_0$ and all
sets $A, B \subseteq \mathbb{F}_p$ with $\sqrt{p}/C \le |A| \le C\sqrt{p}$ and
$\sqrt{p}/C \le |B| \le C\sqrt{p}$, the set
$f(A, B) = \{a^2 + ab : a \in A,\ b \in B\}$ has at least $c\, p^{1/2 + \varepsilon}$ elements.

Bourgain proved that $|f(A, B)| \gtrsim p^{\eta}$ for some $\eta > \delta$ whenever
$|A| \sim |B| \sim p^{\delta}$ with $0 < \delta < 1$ (as Shen recalls; $\delta = 1/2$ is the AIM
question). Stevens and de Zeeuw (Corollary 12) later gave an explicit exponent:
$|f(A, B)| \gg \min\{|A|^{1/2} |B|^{3/4}, |B|^2\}$ for $A \ne \{0\}$ and $|A|^2 |B| \ll p^2$,
which for $|A|, |B|$ between $p^{1/2}/C$ and $C p^{1/2}$ is $\gg_C p^{5/8}$, so
$\varepsilon = 1/8$ works for every $C$.

## Sources

- AIM workshop Recent trends in additive combinatorics (2004), problem list collected by E. Croot and V. F. Lev, https://aimath.org/WWN/additivecomb/additivecomb.pdf, Problem 3.1 (J. Bourgain); resolution: J. Bourgain, More on the sum-product phenomenon in prime fields and its applications, Int. J. Number Theory 1 (2005), 1-32; explicit exponent: S. Stevens and F. de Zeeuw, An improved point-line incidence bound over arbitrary fields, Bull. Lond. Math. Soc. 49 (2017), 842-858, arXiv:1609.06284; C.-Y. Shen, On the sum product estimates and two variables expanders, Publ. Mat. 54 (2010), 149-157, Shen, Section 1, recalling Bourgain: F(x, y) = x² + xy satisfies |F(A, B)| ≳ p^ε for some ε > δ whenever |A| ∼ |B| ∼ p^δ, 0 < δ < 1 (δ = 1/2 is the AIM question); Stevens-de Zeeuw, Section 4 and Corollary 12: for f(x, y) = x² + xy and finite A, B ⊂ F with A ≠ {0} (if char F = p > 0, assuming |A|²|B| ≪ p²), |f(A, B)| ≫ min{|A|^{1/2}|B|^{3/4}, |B|²}; they recall Bourgain's theorem that |f(A, B)| ≫ N^{1+δ} when |A| = |B| = N ≈ p^ε, https://doi.org/10.1112/blms.12077.

articles.title: Bourgain's expander property for x² + xy
articles.statement:
The statement that there is a real
$\varepsilon > 0$ such that for every real $C \ge 1$ there are a real $c > 0$ and a natural number
$p_0$ such that for every prime $p \ge p_0$ and all sets $A, B \subseteq \mathbb{F}_p$ with
$\sqrt{p}/C \le |A| \le C\sqrt{p}$ and $\sqrt{p}/C \le |B| \le C\sqrt{p}$, the set
$\{a^2 + ab : a \in A,\ b \in B\}$ has at least $c\, p^{1/2 + \varepsilon}$ elements.

This says that $f(x, y) = x^2 + xy$ answers Bourgain's question (AIM, Recent trends in additive
combinatorics, Problem 3.1).

articles.title: A subspace almost inside $A + A$ (Kelley–Meka)
articles.statement:
There are real constants $C > 0$ and
$E > 0$ such that for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$, every set $A \subseteq \mathbb{F}_2^n$ and all real
numbers $\alpha$ and $\varepsilon$ with $\alpha > 0$, $0 < \varepsilon < 1$ and
$|A| / 2^n = \alpha$, there is an additive subgroup $V$ of $\mathbb{F}_2^n$ whose codimension
$\log_2(2^n / |V|)$ is at most $C \, (\log(\varepsilon^{-1} \alpha^{-1}) + 1)^E$ and which
satisfies $|V \cap (A + A)| \ge (1 - \varepsilon) |V|$. Here $A + A = \{a + b : a, b \in A\}$ and
$\log$ is the natural logarithm.

Kelley and Meka (Lemma 1.5 of arXiv:2302.05537) show that, over a finite field $\mathbb{F}_q$,
every set $A \subseteq \mathbb{F}_q^n$ of density at least $2^{-d}$ and every error parameter
$\tau$ admit a set $A' \subseteq A$ whose affine span $V + \theta$ has codimension
$O(d^5 \log(1/\tau)^4)$ and $|A' + A'| \ge (1 - \tau)|V + \theta|$, answering the question of
Hatami, Hosseini and Lovett. Over $\mathbb{F}_2$ the sumset $A' + A'$ lies in the subspace $V$,
which gives the statement. Bloom and Sisask improve this codimension bound (arXiv:2309.02353,
Theorem 3).

## Sources

- Zander Kelley and Raghu Meka, Strong bounds for 3-progressions, FOCS 2023, arXiv:2302.05537, https://arxiv.org/abs/2302.05537.

articles.title: Almost-subspace-in-$A + A$ conjecture
articles.statement:
The statement that there are real constants $C > 0$
and $E > 0$ such that for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$, every set $A \subseteq \mathbb{F}_2^n$ and all
real numbers $\alpha$ and $\varepsilon$ with $\alpha > 0$, $0 < \varepsilon < 1$ and
$|A| / 2^n = \alpha$, there is an additive subgroup $V$ of $\mathbb{F}_2^n$ whose codimension
$\log_2(2^n / |V|)$ is at most $C \, (\log(\varepsilon^{-1} \alpha^{-1}) + 1)^E$ and which
satisfies $|V \cap (A + A)| \ge (1 - \varepsilon) |V|$. Here $A + A = \{a + b : a, b \in A\}$ and
$\log$ is the natural logarithm; the constants $C$ and $E$ express the source's codimension bound
$\log^{O(1)}(\varepsilon^{-1} \alpha^{-1})$.

## Sources

- cites [AIM-COMBINATORICS-0031], aim-combinatorics-notes.json notes[30].

articles.title: Counting Boolean factor pairs with a small sumset
articles.statement:
Let $n$ and $k$ be natural numbers with
$0 < k \le n$, and let $d > 0$ be a real number. Then the number of pairs $(A, B)$ of finite sets
of natural numbers such that $0 \in A$, the largest element of $A$ is $k$, the largest element of
$B$ is $n - k$, and $|A + B| \le |A| + |B| + d$, where $A + B = \{a + b : a \in A, b \in B\}$ is
the sumset, is at most $n^{2d+2} 2^k$.

This is Lemma 19 for Boolean polynomials $f$ and $g$ recorded by their supports $A$ and $B$: the
conditions say that $f$ has nonzero constant term, $\deg f = k$ and $\deg g = n - k$, and the
support of their max-min product $f \otimes g$ is $A + B$.

## Sources

- Baily, Dell, Fleischmann, Jackson, Pesikoff, Miller and Reifenberg, *Indecomposability Over the Max-Min Semiring*, Journal of Integer Sequences 28 (2025), Article 25.2.7, Lemma 19 (`jis-2025-25.2.7-lem-19`).

articles.title: Monotone digit maps are lunar homomorphisms
articles.statement:
Let $d : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ be
nondecreasing, and for a coefficient sequence $f : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ write $d(f)$ for the
sequence $k \mapsto d(f_k)$. Write $f \oplus g$ for the pointwise maximum and $f \otimes g$ for the
max-min product of coefficient sequences $f$ and $g$. Then for all $f$ and $g$,
$d(f) \oplus d(g) = d(f \oplus g)$ and $d(f) \otimes d(g) = d(f \otimes g)$.

This is Theorem 15 (Applegate, LeBrun and Sloane, prime promotion), stated for every nondecreasing
map on $\mathbb{N}$; a base-$b$ digit map, a nondecreasing map on the digits, extends to such a map.

## Sources

- Baily, Dell, Fleischmann, Jackson, Pesikoff, Miller and Reifenberg, *Indecomposability Over the Max-Min Semiring*, Journal of Integer Sequences 28 (2025), Article 25.2.7, Theorem 15 (`jis-2025-25.2.7-thm-15`).

articles.title: A digit string has no coefficients beyond its length
articles.statement:
Let $n$ and $b$ be natural numbers
and let $a = (a_0, \dots, a_{n-1})$ be a digit string with digits in $\{0, \dots, b - 1\}$. Then
for every $k \ge n$, the $k$-th term of the coefficient sequence of $a$ is $0$.

## Sources

- Baily, Dell, Fleischmann, Jackson, Pesikoff, Miller and Reifenberg, *Indecomposability Over the Max-Min Semiring*, Journal of Integer Sequences 28 (2025), Article 25.2.7, Section 2 (lunar numbers `ℒ_b` as polynomials over `ℬ_b = {0, …, b - 1}`).

articles.title: Coefficient sequence of a digit string
articles.statement:
Let $n$ and $b$ be natural numbers. The
coefficient sequence of a digit string $a = (a_0, \dots, a_{n-1})$ with digits in
$\{0, \dots, b - 1\}$ is the sequence $\mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ whose $k$-th term is $a_k$ for
$k < n$ and $0$ for $k \ge n$.

## Sources

- Baily, Dell, Fleischmann, Jackson, Pesikoff, Miller and Reifenberg, *Indecomposability Over the Max-Min Semiring*, Journal of Integer Sequences 28 (2025), Article 25.2.7, Section 2 (lunar numbers `ℒ_b` as polynomials over `ℬ_b = {0, …, b - 1}`).

articles.title: The lunar unit is a prime candidate
articles.statement:
For every natural number $b \ge 2$, the lunar unit
of base $b$, the sequence with constant term $b - 1$ and all other terms $0$, is a prime candidate
in base $b$: its constant term is nonzero and one of its terms equals $b - 1$.

## Sources

- Baily, Dell, Fleischmann, Jackson, Pesikoff, Miller and Reifenberg, *Indecomposability Over the Max-Min Semiring*, Journal of Integer Sequences 28 (2025), Article 25.2.7, Section 2 (definition of prime candidate).

articles.title: Lunar prime candidates
articles.statement:
Let $b$ be a natural number. A coefficient sequence
$f : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ is a prime candidate in base $b$ when its constant term $f_0$ is
nonzero and some term $f_i$ equals $b - 1$, where the subtraction is truncated, so that
$b - 1 = 0$ when $b = 0$. For $f$ with all terms less than $b$, the second condition says that
the largest coefficient of $f$ is $b - 1$.

## Sources

- Baily, Dell, Fleischmann, Jackson, Pesikoff, Miller and Reifenberg, *Indecomposability Over the Max-Min Semiring*, Journal of Integer Sequences 28 (2025), Article 25.2.7, Section 2 (definition of prime candidate).

articles.title: Indecomposable prime candidates are lunar primes
articles.statement:
Let $n$ and $b \ge 2$ be natural
numbers, let $a = (a_0, \dots, a_{n-1})$ be a digit string with digits in $\{0, \dots, b - 1\}$,
and let $f$ be its coefficient sequence. If $f$ is a prime candidate in base $b$ and $f$ is
max-min indecomposable, then $f$ is a lunar prime of base $b$.

This is Lemma 30 (Applegate, LeBrun and Sloane).

## Sources

- Baily, Dell, Fleischmann, Jackson, Pesikoff, Miller and Reifenberg, *Indecomposability Over the Max-Min Semiring*, Journal of Integer Sequences 28 (2025), Article 25.2.7, Lemma 30 (`jis-2025-25.2.7-lem-30`).

articles.title: Lunar primes
articles.statement:
Let $b$ be a natural number. The lunar unit of base $b$ is the constant
polynomial $b - 1$, the sequence with constant term $b - 1$ and all other terms $0$. A coefficient
sequence $f : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ is a lunar prime of base $b$ (Applegate, LeBrun and
Sloane) when for all sequences $g, h : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ with all terms less than $b$ and
$g \otimes h = f$, where $\otimes$ is the max-min product, $g$ or $h$ is the lunar unit.

## Sources

- Baily, Dell, Fleischmann, Jackson, Pesikoff, Miller and Reifenberg, *Indecomposability Over the Max-Min Semiring*, Journal of Integer Sequences 28 (2025), Article 25.2.7, Section 2 (definition of prime lunar numbers).

articles.title: Max-min indecomposable sequences
articles.statement:
A coefficient sequence $f : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$
is indecomposable (in the arXiv version: irreducible) when for all sequences
$g, h : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ with $g \otimes h = f$, where $\otimes$ is the max-min product,
$g$ or $h$ is a max-min monomial, that is, a sequence with exactly one nonzero term.

Factors range over all sequences $\mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$; for a natural number $b$ and $f$
with all terms less than $b$, this is equivalent to factoring over $\{0, \dots, b - 1\}$, by
applying the digit map $x \mapsto \min(x, b - 1)$.

## Sources

- Baily, Dell, Fleischmann, Jackson, Pesikoff, Miller and Reifenberg, *Indecomposability Over the Max-Min Semiring*, Journal of Integer Sequences 28 (2025), Article 25.2.7, Section 1 (definition of indecomposable).

articles.title: The lunar unit is a monomial
articles.statement:
For every natural number $b \ge 2$, the lunar unit of base
$b$, the sequence with constant term $b - 1$ and all other terms $0$, is a max-min monomial: it
has exactly one nonzero term.

## Sources

- Baily, Dell, Fleischmann, Jackson, Pesikoff, Miller and Reifenberg, *Indecomposability Over the Max-Min Semiring*, Journal of Integer Sequences 28 (2025), Article 25.2.7, Section 2 (definition of prime lunar numbers).

articles.title: Monomials over the max-min semiring
articles.statement:
A coefficient sequence
$g : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ over the max-min semiring is a monomial when exactly one of its
entries is nonzero, that is, when it is $c x^i$ for some index $i$ and some coefficient $c \neq 0$.

## Sources

- Baily, Dell, Fleischmann, Jackson, Pesikoff, Miller and Reifenberg, *Indecomposability Over the Max-Min Semiring*, Journal of Integer Sequences 28 (2025), Article 25.2.7, Section 1 (definition of indecomposable).

articles.title: Upper bound on the number of decomposable lunar numbers
articles.statement:
Fix an integer $b \ge 2$. There
is a constant $C > 0$ such that for every integer $n \ge 2$ and all reals $d > 0$ and $v > 0$, the
set $\Sigma_b^n$ of decomposable lunar numbers of base $b$ and degree at most $n$ satisfies

$$|\Sigma_b^n| \le C b^{n+1} \Big(n^2 e^{-d^2/(4(n+2))} + n^{2d+4} 2^{d/2-(n+1)/3} +
v n^{2d+2} 2^v b^{d/2-n/b} + n^2 2^{-v}\Big).$$

## Sources

- Baily, Dell, Fleischmann, Jackson, Pesikoff, Miller and Reifenberg, *Indecomposability Over the Max-Min Semiring*, Journal of Integer Sequences 28 (2025), Article 25.2.7, Proposition 21 (`jis-2025-25.2.7-prop-21`).

articles.title: Decomposable lunar numbers
articles.statement:
For natural numbers $b$ and $n$, let $\mathcal{L}_b^n$ be the
set of lunar numbers of base $b$ and degree at most $n$, that is, polynomials
$c_0 \oplus c_1 x \oplus \dots \oplus c_n x^n$ with digits $c_k \in \{0, \dots, b - 1\}$. The set
$\Sigma_b^n$ of decomposable lunar numbers consists of the $h \in \mathcal{L}_b^n$ that factor as
$h = f \otimes g$ under the max-min product, with $f, g \in \mathcal{L}_b^n$ each having at least
two nonzero digits.

A monomial is $t x^m$ with $t \in \{0, \dots, b - 1\}$, so the factors are exactly the
non-monomials. Every factor of a nonzero lunar number of degree at most $n$ lies in
$\mathcal{L}_b^n$.

## Sources

- Baily, Dell, Fleischmann, Jackson, Pesikoff, Miller and Reifenberg, *Indecomposability Over the Max-Min Semiring*, Journal of Integer Sequences 28 (2025), Article 25.2.7, Section 2, before Proposition 21.

articles.title: Bound on the number of Hoeffding extremal lunar numbers
articles.statement:
Fix an integer $b \ge 2$. There is
a constant $C > 0$ such that for every integer $n \ge 1$ and every real $d > 0$, the set
$\mathcal{H}_b^n(d)$ of $d$-Hoeffding extremal lunar numbers of base $b$ and degree at most $n$
has at most $C n^2 e^{-d^2/(4(n+2))} b^n$ elements.

## Sources

- Baily, Dell, Fleischmann, Jackson, Pesikoff, Miller and Reifenberg, *Indecomposability Over the Max-Min Semiring*, Journal of Integer Sequences 28 (2025), Article 25.2.7, Lemma 24 (`jis-2025-25.2.7-lem-24`).

articles.title: Hoeffding extremal lunar numbers
articles.statement:
Let $b$ and $n$ be natural numbers and $d$ a real
number. Let $\mathcal{L}_b^n$ be the set of lunar numbers of base $b$ and degree at most $n$
(digit strings $c_0, \dots, c_n$ with digits in $\{0, \dots, b - 1\}$), with the max-min product
$\otimes$, and for $f \in \mathcal{L}_b^n$ let $|f_i|$ be the number of its digits that are at
least $i$. The set $\mathcal{H}_b^n(d)$ of $d$-Hoeffding extremal lunar numbers consists of the
$h \in \mathcal{L}_b^n$ for which there is an index $i$ with $1 \le i \le b - 1$ such that either
$\bigl||h_i| - (b - i)n/b\bigr| > d/2$, or $h = f \otimes g$ for some $f, g \in \mathcal{L}_b^n$
with $\bigl||f_i| + |g_i| - (b - i)(n + 1)/b\bigr| > d/2$.

## Sources

- Baily, Dell, Fleischmann, Jackson, Pesikoff, Miller and Reifenberg, *Indecomposability Over the Max-Min Semiring*, Journal of Integer Sequences 28 (2025), Article 25.2.7, Definition 23.

articles.title: Bound on decomposable lunar numbers neither level decomposable nor extremal
articles.statement:
Fix an integer
$b \ge 2$. For a natural number $n$ let $\mathcal{I}_b^n = \Sigma_b^n \setminus \mathcal{D}_b^n$,
where $\Sigma_b^n$ is the set of decomposable lunar numbers of base $b$ and degree at most $n$ and
$\mathcal{D}_b^n$ the set of level-decomposable ones, and for a real $d$ let $\mathcal{H}_b^n(d)$
be the set of $d$-Hoeffding extremal ones. There is a constant $C > 0$ such that for every natural
number $n$ and all reals $d > 0$ and $v > 0$,

$$|\mathcal{I}_b^n \setminus \mathcal{H}_b^n(d)| \le
C \Big(v n^{2d+2} 2^v b^{(b-1)n/b + d/2} + n^2 2^{-v} b^{n+1}\Big).$$

## Sources

- Baily, Dell, Fleischmann, Jackson, Pesikoff, Miller and Reifenberg, *Indecomposability Over the Max-Min Semiring*, Journal of Integer Sequences 28 (2025), Article 25.2.7, Lemma 28 (`jis-2025-25.2.7-lem-28`).

articles.title: Level counts of $1 \oplus 2x^2$ in base $3$
articles.statement:
For the base-$3$ lunar number
$f = 1 \oplus 2x^2$ of degree at most $2$, with digits $1, 0, 2$, exactly two digits are at least
$1$ and exactly one digit is at least $2$: $|f_1| = 2$ and $|f_2| = 1$.

## Sources

- Baily, Dell, Fleischmann, Jackson, Pesikoff, Miller and Reifenberg, *Indecomposability Over the Max-Min Semiring*, Journal of Integer Sequences 28 (2025), Article 25.2.7, Section 2, Definitions 13 and 16.

articles.title: Level counts of a product that is not Hoeffding extremal
articles.statement:
Let $b$ and $n$ be natural
numbers, $d$ a real number and $f, g, h$ lunar numbers of base $b$ and degree at most $n$ with
$h = f \otimes g$ under the max-min product. For a natural number $i$ write $|f_i|$, $|g_i|$ and
$|h_i|$ for the numbers of digits of $f$, $g$ and $h$ that are at least $i$. If $h$ is not in the
set $\mathcal{H}_b^n(d)$ of $d$-Hoeffding extremal lunar numbers of base $b$ and degree at most
$n$, then $|h_i| \le |f_i| + |g_i| + d$ for every $i$ with $1 \le i \le b - 1$.

The source also assumes that $h$ lies in the set $\Sigma_b^n$ of decomposable lunar numbers of
base $b$ and degree at most $n$, which is not needed, and prints $|b_i|$ for $|g_i|$.

## Sources

- Baily, Dell, Fleischmann, Jackson, Pesikoff, Miller and Reifenberg, *Indecomposability Over the Max-Min Semiring*, Journal of Integer Sequences 28 (2025), Article 25.2.7, Lemma 25 (`jis-2025-25.2.7-lem-25`).

articles.title: Level counts of a lunar number
articles.statement:
Let $f$ be a lunar number of base $b$ and degree at most
$n$, with digits $c_0, \dots, c_n \in \{0, \dots, b - 1\}$, and let $i$ be a natural number. The
level count $|f_i|$ is the number of indices $k \le n$ with $c_k \ge i$, that is, the number of
nonzero coefficients of the $i$-level support $f_i = s_i(f)$, the Boolean polynomial with
coefficient $1$ at $x^k$ when $c_k \ge i$ and $0$ otherwise.

A lunar number $f$ is not a monomial $t x^m$ (with $t = 0$ allowed) if and only if $|f_1| \ge 2$,
and $f_i$ is not a monomial if and only if $|f_i| \ge 2$.

## Sources

- Baily, Dell, Fleischmann, Jackson, Pesikoff, Miller and Reifenberg, *Indecomposability Over the Max-Min Semiring*, Journal of Integer Sequences 28 (2025), Article 25.2.7, Section 2, Definitions 13 and 16.

articles.title: Bound on level-decomposable lunar numbers that are not Hoeffding extremal
articles.statement:
Let $b \ge 2$
and $n$ be natural numbers and $d > 0$ a real number. The number of elements of
$\mathcal{D}_b^n \setminus \mathcal{H}_b^n(d)$ is at most $n^{2d+4} 2^{d/2-n/3} b^{n+1}$, where
$\mathcal{D}_b^n$ is the set of level-decomposable lunar numbers of base $b$ and degree at most
$n$ and $\mathcal{H}_b^n(d)$ is the set of $d$-Hoeffding extremal ones.

## Sources

- Baily, Dell, Fleischmann, Jackson, Pesikoff, Miller and Reifenberg, *Indecomposability Over the Max-Min Semiring*, Journal of Integer Sequences 28 (2025), Article 25.2.7, Lemma 26 (`jis-2025-25.2.7-lem-26`).

articles.title: Level-decomposable lunar numbers
articles.statement:
Let $b$ and $n$ be natural numbers and
$a = \lfloor b/2 \rfloor$. For a lunar number $f$ of base $b$ and degree at most $n$, given by its
digits $f_0, \dots, f_n \in \{0, \dots, b - 1\}$, write $|f_a|$ for the number of indices $k \le n$
with $f_k \ge a$. The set $\mathcal{D}_b^n$ consists of the lunar numbers $h$ of base $b$ and
degree at most $n$ such that $h = f \otimes g$ for some lunar numbers $f$ and $g$ of base $b$ and
degree at most $n$ with $|f_a| \ge 2$ and $|g_a| \ge 2$, where $\otimes$ is the max-min product of
coefficient sequences.

For $b \ge 2$ we have $a \ge 1$, so $|f_a| \ge 2$ implies that $f$ has at least two nonzero
digits; hence $\mathcal{D}_b^n$ is contained in the set $\Sigma_b^n$ of decomposable lunar numbers
of degree at most $n$, and one writes $\mathcal{I}_b^n = \Sigma_b^n \setminus \mathcal{D}_b^n$.

## Sources

- Baily, Dell, Fleischmann, Jackson, Pesikoff, Miller and Reifenberg, *Indecomposability Over the Max-Min Semiring*, Journal of Integer Sequences 28 (2025), Article 25.2.7, Section 2, before Remark 22.

articles.title: Decomposable lunar numbers with a low-degree factor
articles.statement:
Let $b \ge 2$ and $n$ be natural
numbers and let $d > 0$ and $v > 0$ be reals. Count the lunar numbers $h$ of base $b$ and degree at
most $n$ that lie in $\Sigma_b^n \setminus \mathcal{H}_b^n(d)$ (decomposable but not $d$-Hoeffding
extremal) and can be written as $h = f \otimes g$, with $\otimes$ the max-min product, where $f$
and $g$ are lunar numbers of base $b$ and degree at most $n$, each with at least two nonzero
digits, and every digit $f_k$ with $k > v$ is zero. Their number is at most
$v \, n^{2d+3} \, 2^v \, (b - 1)^{(b-1)n/b + d/2}$.

The factorization is required to be nontrivial, as in the source's proof; if trivial
factorizations $h = (b - 1) \otimes h$ counted, the claim would fail at $b = 2$, $n = 2$, $d = 5$,
$v = 10^{-4}$: the lunar number with digit string $(1, 1, 1)$, that is $1 \oplus x \oplus x^2$
with $\oplus$ the lunar sum (digitwise maximum), lies in $\Sigma_2^2 \setminus \mathcal{H}_2^2(5)$,
but the bound is $8192 \cdot 10^{-4} \cdot 2^{10^{-4}} < 1$.

## Sources

- Baily, Dell, Fleischmann, Jackson, Pesikoff, Miller and Reifenberg, *Indecomposability Over the Max-Min Semiring*, Journal of Integer Sequences 28 (2025), Article 25.2.7, Lemma 27 (`jis-2025-25.2.7-lem-27`).

articles.title: Asymptotic count of lunar primes
articles.statement:
Fix an integer $b \ge 2$. For $n \ge 1$ let $\pi_b(n)$
be the number of digit strings $(a_0, \dots, a_{n-1})$ with $a_k \in \{0, \dots, b - 1\}$ and
leading digit $a_{n-1} \ne 0$ whose coefficient sequence $(a_0, \dots, a_{n-1}, 0, 0, \dots)$ is a
lunar prime of base $b$; these are the prime lunar numbers of base $b$ with $n$ digits. Then
$\pi_b(n) \sim (b - 1)^2 b^{n-2}$ as $n \to \infty$, as conjectured by Applegate, LeBrun and
Sloane.

## Sources

- Baily, Dell, Fleischmann, Jackson, Pesikoff, Miller and Reifenberg, *Indecomposability Over the Max-Min Semiring*, Journal of Integer Sequences 28 (2025), Article 25.2.7, Corollary 12 (`jis-2025-25.2.7-cor-12`).

articles.title: Lunar unit
articles.statement:
For a natural number $b$, the lunar unit of base $b$ is the coefficient sequence
$\mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ whose constant term is $b - 1$ and whose other terms are all $0$, that
is, the constant polynomial $b - 1$ over the max-min semiring. The subtraction is truncated, so
the lunar unit of base $0$ is the zero sequence.

For sequences with all terms less than $b$, the lunar unit is the identity of the max-min product.

## Sources

- Baily, Dell, Fleischmann, Jackson, Pesikoff, Miller and Reifenberg, *Indecomposability Over the Max-Min Semiring*, Journal of Integer Sequences 28 (2025), Article 25.2.7, Section 2 (definition of prime lunar numbers).

articles.title: Almost all max-min polynomials are indecomposable
articles.statement:
Fix an integer $b \ge 2$. For each
$n$, among the polynomials of degree $n$ with coefficients in $\mathcal{B}_b = \{0, \dots, b - 1\}$,
that is, coefficient strings $(a_0, \dots, a_n)$ with $a_n \ne 0$, the proportion of those that
are indecomposable over the max-min semiring tends to $1$ as $n \to \infty$.

## Sources

- Baily, Dell, Fleischmann, Jackson, Pesikoff, Miller and Reifenberg, *Indecomposability Over the Max-Min Semiring*, Journal of Integer Sequences 28 (2025), Article 25.2.7, Theorem 11 (`jis-2025-25.2.7-thm-11`).

articles.title: Linear coefficient of a max-min product
articles.statement:
For all sequences
$g, h \colon \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$, the max-min product satisfies
$(g \otimes h)_1 = \max(\min(g_0, h_1), \min(g_1, h_0))$.

## Sources

- Baily, Dell, Fleischmann, Jackson, Pesikoff, Miller and Reifenberg, *Indecomposability Over the Max-Min Semiring*, Journal of Integer Sequences 28 (2025), Article 25.2.7, Section 1 (the max-min semiring and its polynomials).

articles.title: Constant coefficient of a max-min product
articles.statement:
For all sequences
$g, h \colon \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$, the max-min product satisfies
$(g \otimes h)_0 = \min(g_0, h_0)$.

## Sources

- Baily, Dell, Fleischmann, Jackson, Pesikoff, Miller and Reifenberg, *Indecomposability Over the Max-Min Semiring*, Journal of Integer Sequences 28 (2025), Article 25.2.7, Section 1 (the max-min semiring and its polynomials).

articles.title: Max-min product
articles.statement:
The max-min product of sequences $g, h \colon \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$
is the sequence $g \otimes h$ with $(g \otimes h)_k = \max_{i + j = k} \min(g_i, h_j)$ for every
$k \in \mathbb{N}$, the maximum running over pairs of natural numbers $(i, j)$. This is the product
of the max-min semiring $(\mathbb{N}, \max, \min)$ on coefficient sequences.

## Sources

- Baily, Dell, Fleischmann, Jackson, Pesikoff, Miller and Reifenberg, *Indecomposability Over the Max-Min Semiring*, Journal of Integer Sequences 28 (2025), Article 25.2.7, Section 1 (the max-min semiring and its polynomials).

articles.title: A decomposable lunar number in base 2
articles.statement:
In base $2$, the lunar number with digit string
$(1, 1, 1)$, that is $1 \oplus x \oplus x^2$ with $\oplus$ the lunar sum (digitwise maximum), lies
both in the set $\Sigma_2^2$ of decomposable lunar numbers of degree at most $2$ and in the set
$\mathcal{D}_2^2$ of level-decomposable lunar numbers of degree at most $2$.

A factorization witnessing both is $1 \oplus x \oplus x^2 = (1 \oplus x) \otimes (1 \oplus x)$,
where $\otimes$ is the max-min product and $1 \oplus x$ has digit string $(1, 1, 0)$.

## Sources

- Baily, Dell, Fleischmann, Jackson, Pesikoff, Miller and Reifenberg, *Indecomposability Over the Max-Min Semiring*, Journal of Integer Sequences 28 (2025), Article 25.2.7, Section 2, before Proposition 21 and Remark 22.

articles.title: Zero is not a lunar prime
articles.statement:
For every integer $b \ge 2$, the zero sequence is not a lunar
prime of base $b$: $0 = 0 \otimes 0$, where $\otimes$ is the max-min product, and $0$ is not the
lunar unit, the constant polynomial $b - 1$ with coefficient sequence $(b - 1, 0, 0, \dots)$.

## Sources

- Baily, Dell, Fleischmann, Jackson, Pesikoff, Miller and Reifenberg, *Indecomposability Over the Max-Min Semiring*, Journal of Integer Sequences 28 (2025), Article 25.2.7, Section 2 (definition of prime lunar numbers).

articles.title: The zero sequence is decomposable
articles.statement:
The zero coefficient sequence
$\mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ is not indecomposable over the max-min semiring: it factors as
$0 = 0 \otimes 0$, where $\otimes$ is the max-min product, and the zero sequence is not a
monomial.

## Sources

- Baily, Dell, Fleischmann, Jackson, Pesikoff, Miller and Reifenberg, *Indecomposability Over the Max-Min Semiring*, Journal of Integer Sequences 28 (2025), Article 25.2.7, Section 1 (definition of indecomposable).

articles.title: The zero sequence is not a monomial
articles.statement:
The zero coefficient sequence
$\mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ is not a max-min monomial: a monomial has exactly one nonzero
entry, and the zero sequence has none.

## Sources

- Baily, Dell, Fleischmann, Jackson, Pesikoff, Miller and Reifenberg, *Indecomposability Over the Max-Min Semiring*, Journal of Integer Sequences 28 (2025), Article 25.2.7, Section 1 (definition of indecomposable).

articles.title: Shitov's theorem: almost all Boolean polynomials with nonzero constant term are prime
articles.statement:
For $n \in \mathbb{N}$, consider the Boolean polynomials of degree exactly $n$ with nonzero
constant term, that is, the base-$2$ lunar numbers given by digit strings
$(a_0, \dots, a_n) \in \{0, 1\}^{n+1}$ with $a_0 \ne 0$ and $a_n \ne 0$. The proportion of
these which are lunar primes in base $2$ tends to $1$ as $n \to \infty$.

## Sources

- Baily, Dell, Fleischmann, Jackson, Pesikoff, Miller and Reifenberg, *Indecomposability Over the Max-Min Semiring*, Journal of Integer Sequences 28 (2025), Article 25.2.7, Theorem 10 (`jis-2025-25.2.7-thm-10`), quoting Shitov (2014), Theorem 2.5.

articles.title: An example of a Hoeffding extremal lunar number
articles.statement:
In base $2$, the zero lunar number of
degree at most $2$ (the digit string $(0, 0, 0)$) lies in the $1$-Hoeffding extremal set
$\mathcal{H}_2^2(1)$: for the level $i = 1$, the number $|0_1|$ of its digits that are at least
$1$ is $0$, and $\left|0 - (2 - 1) \cdot 2 / 2\right| = 1 > 1/2$.

## Sources

- Baily, Dell, Fleischmann, Jackson, Pesikoff, Miller and Reifenberg, *Indecomposability Over the Max-Min Semiring*, Journal of Integer Sequences 28 (2025), Article 25.2.7, Definition 23.

articles.title: The set of admissible coset-cover exponents
articles.statement:
This is the set of all real numbers $C$
that are admissible asymptotic coset-cover exponents: for every real $\varepsilon > 0$ there is a
real $K_0 \ge 1$ such that for every real $K \ge K_0$, every $n \in \mathbb{N}$ and every
nonempty finite set $A \subseteq \mathbb{F}_2^n$ with $|A + A| \le K|A|$, there are an
$\mathbb{F}_2$-linear subspace $H$ of $\mathbb{F}_2^n$ with $|H| \le |A|$ and a finite set
$F \subseteq \mathbb{F}_2^n$ with $|F| \le K^{C + \varepsilon}$ and $A \subseteq F + H$.

## Sources

- Optimization Problems constant 18a.

articles.title: Basis-vector lower bound for coset-cover exponents
articles.statement:
Every admissible asymptotic
coset-cover exponent $C$ satisfies $C \ge 1$.

The obstruction comes from sets of basis vectors.

## Sources

- Optimization Problems constant 18a.

articles.title: Statement of the basis-vector lower bound
articles.statement:
The proposition that every admissible
asymptotic coset-cover exponent $C$ satisfies $C \ge 1$.

The obstruction comes from sets of basis vectors.

## Sources

- Optimization Problems constant 18a.

articles.title: The binary vector space $\mathbb{F}_2^n$
articles.statement:
For a natural number $n$, the ambient space
$\mathbb{F}_2^n$ of all functions from $\{0, 1, \dots, n - 1\}$ to the two-element field
$\mathbb{F}_2 = \mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}$.

## Sources

- Optimization Problems constant 18a.

articles.title: Gowers–Green–Manners–Tao theorem (polynomial Freiman–Ruzsa over $\mathbb{F}_2$)
articles.statement:
The
polynomial Freiman–Ruzsa conjecture over $\mathbb{F}_2$ holds: there are real polynomials $P$ and
$Q$, with $P(K) > 0$ and $Q(K) > 0$ for every real $K \ge 1$, such that for every
$n \in \mathbb{N}$, every nonempty finite set $A \subseteq \mathbb{F}_2^n$ and every real $K \ge 1$
with $|A + A| \le K|A|$, there is a subset $A' \subseteq A$ with $|A| / P(K) \le |A'|$ and
$|\operatorname{span}(A')| \le Q(K)\,|A'|$, where $\operatorname{span}(A')$ is the
$\mathbb{F}_2$-linear span of $A'$.

Gowers, Green, Manners and Tao prove that such a set $A$ is covered by polynomially many (in $K$)
cosets of a subspace of size at most $|A|$; the densest of these cosets gives the subset $A'$.

## Sources

- W. T. Gowers, B. Green, F. Manners, T. Tao, On a conjecture of Marton, arXiv:2311.05762 (November 2023), https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.05762.

articles.title: Polynomial Freiman–Ruzsa conjecture over $\mathbb{F}_2$
articles.statement:
There are real polynomials $P$
and $Q$, with $P(K) > 0$ and $Q(K) > 0$ for every real $K \ge 1$, such that for every
$n \in \mathbb{N}$, every nonempty finite set $A \subseteq \mathbb{F}_2^n$ and every real $K \ge 1$
with $|A + A| \le K|A|$, there is a subset $A' \subseteq A$ with $|A| / P(K) \le |A'|$ and
$|\operatorname{span}(A')| \le Q(K)\,|A'|$, where $\operatorname{span}(A')$ is the
$\mathbb{F}_2$-linear span of $A'$.

The problem is recorded as OWR-12177-008. It was proved by Gowers, Green, Manners and Tao
(arXiv:2311.05762).

articles.title: The vector space $\mathbb{F}_2^n$
articles.statement:
For a natural number $n$, $\mathbb{F}_2^n$ is the
space of functions from $\{0, \dots, n - 1\}$ to the field $\mathbb{F}_2 = \mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}$
with two elements, the $n$-dimensional vector space over $\mathbb{F}_2$.

articles.title: Gowers–Green–Manners–Tao exponent $7 + \sqrt{17}$
articles.statement:
The number $7 + \sqrt{17}$ is an
admissible asymptotic coset-cover exponent.

## Sources

- GGMT, arXiv:2311.05762, and Optimization Problems constant 18a.

articles.title: Statement of the Gowers–Green–Manners–Tao exponent $7 + \sqrt{17}$
articles.statement:
The proposition that
$7 + \sqrt{17}$ is an admissible asymptotic coset-cover exponent.

## Sources

- GGMT, arXiv:2311.05762, and Optimization Problems constant 18a.

articles.title: Admissible asymptotic coset-cover exponents
articles.statement:
A real number $C$ is an admissible asymptotic
coset-cover exponent if for every real $\varepsilon > 0$ there is a real $K_0 \ge 1$ such that
for every real $K \ge K_0$, every $n \in \mathbb{N}$ and every nonempty finite set
$A \subseteq \mathbb{F}_2^n$ with $|A + A| \le K|A|$, there is an $\mathbb{F}_2$-linear subspace
$H$ of $\mathbb{F}_2^n$ with $|H| \le |A|$ such that $A$ is covered by at most $K^{C + \varepsilon}$
translates of $H$: there is a finite set $F \subseteq \mathbb{F}_2^n$ with
$|F| \le K^{C + \varepsilon}$ and $A \subseteq F + H$.

This makes the source's bound of $K^{C + o(1)}$ translates uniform: once $K$ is large enough,
the same bound works in every dimension and for every nonempty set of doubling at most $K$.

## Sources

- Optimization Problems constant 18a, with the uniform asymptotic quantifiers made explicit.

articles.title: The least coset-cover exponent is attained
articles.statement:
The set of admissible asymptotic coset-cover
exponents has a least element, namely its infimum $C^*$ (the Marton cover exponent): $C^*$ is
itself admissible, and $C^* \le C$ for every admissible asymptotic coset-cover exponent $C$.

## Sources

- Optimization Problems constant 18a.

articles.title: Statement that the Marton coset-cover exponent is attained
articles.statement:
The proposition that the
Marton coset-cover exponent $C^*$, the infimum of the admissible asymptotic coset-cover exponents,
is the least admissible exponent: $C^*$ is itself an admissible asymptotic coset-cover exponent,
and $C^* \le C$ for every admissible asymptotic coset-cover exponent $C$.

## Sources

- Optimization Problems constant 18a.

articles.title: Liao's simplified coset-cover bound with exponent 11
articles.statement:
The number $11$ is an admissible
asymptotic coset-cover exponent: for every $\varepsilon > 0$ there is $K_0 \ge 1$ such that for
every real $K \ge K_0$, every $n \in \mathbb{N}$ and every nonempty finite set
$A \subseteq \mathbb{F}_2^n$ with $|A + A| \le K|A|$, there is a subspace $H$ of $\mathbb{F}_2^n$
with $|H| \le |A|$ such that $A$ is covered by at most $K^{11 + \varepsilon}$ translates
of $H$.

## Sources

- J.-J. Liao, arXiv:2404.09639, Theorem 1.2 and the implication `C ≤ C' + 1`.

articles.title: Statement of Liao's simplified exponent-11 coset-cover bound
articles.statement:
The proposition that $11$
is an admissible asymptotic coset-cover exponent: for every $\varepsilon > 0$ there is $K_0 \ge 1$
such that for every real $K \ge K_0$, every $n \in \mathbb{N}$ and every nonempty finite set
$A \subseteq \mathbb{F}_2^n$ with $|A + A| \le K|A|$, there is a subspace $H$ of $\mathbb{F}_2^n$
with $|H| \le |A|$ such that $A$ is covered by at most $K^{11 + \varepsilon}$ translates of $H$.

## Sources

- J.-J. Liao, arXiv:2404.09639, Theorem 1.2 and the implication `C ≤ C' + 1`.

articles.title: Liao's coset-cover bound with exponent 9
articles.statement:
The number $9$ is an admissible
asymptotic coset-cover exponent: for every $\varepsilon > 0$ there is $K_0 \ge 1$ such that for
every real $K \ge K_0$, every $n \in \mathbb{N}$ and every nonempty finite set
$A \subseteq \mathbb{F}_2^n$ with $|A + A| \le K|A|$, there is a subspace $H$ of $\mathbb{F}_2^n$
with $|H| \le |A|$ such that $A$ is covered by at most $K^{9 + \varepsilon}$ translates
of $H$.

## Sources

- J.-J. Liao, arXiv:2404.09639, Theorem 1.1.

articles.title: Statement of Liao's exponent-9 coset-cover bound
articles.statement:
The proposition that $9$ is an admissible
asymptotic coset-cover exponent: for every $\varepsilon > 0$ there is $K_0 \ge 1$ such that for
every real $K \ge K_0$, every $n \in \mathbb{N}$ and every nonempty finite set
$A \subseteq \mathbb{F}_2^n$ with $|A + A| \le K|A|$, there is a subspace $H$ of $\mathbb{F}_2^n$
with $|H| \le |A|$ such that $A$ is covered by at most $K^{9 + \varepsilon}$ translates
of $H$.

## Sources

- J.-J. Liao, arXiv:2404.09639, Theorem 1.1.

articles.title: The Marton coset-cover exponent
articles.statement:
Call a real number $C$ an admissible asymptotic
coset-cover exponent if for every $\varepsilon > 0$ there is $K_0 \ge 1$ such that for every real
$K \ge K_0$, every $n \in \mathbb{N}$ and every nonempty finite set $A \subseteq \mathbb{F}_2^n$
