$H$ with the edge $e$ removed, Li proved that a $3$-uniform hypergraph $H$ with $\tau(H) = 3$ and
$\tau(H - e) = 2$ for every edge $e$ has at most $10$ edges, so some vertex has degree at most $6$.

## Sources

- T. F. Bloom, Erdős Problems, Problem #834, https://www.erdosproblems.com/834 (status SOLVED); resolution: R. Li, On an Erdős-Lovász problem: 3-critical 3-graphs of minimum degree 7, arXiv:2512.24850 (2025; unrefereed, accepted on erdosproblems.com/834), abstract and main theorem for the transversal interpretation: a 3-uniform hypergraph H with τ(H) = 3 and τ(H - e) = 2 for every edge e has at most 10 edges, in particular δ(H) ≤ 6, sharp for K₅⁽³⁾; erdosproblems.com/834: 'In the first formulation ... Li proves that a 3-critical 3-uniform hypergraph must have a vertex of degree ≤ 6', https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.24850.

articles.title: Erdős Problem 834 for transversal-critical triple systems
articles.statement:
There exist $n \in \mathbb{N}$
and a $3$-uniform hypergraph $H$ on the vertex set $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ such that some set of at
most $3$ vertices meets every edge of $H$, no set of at most $2$ vertices meets every edge of $H$,
for every edge $e$ of $H$ some set of at most $2$ vertices meets every edge of $H$ other than $e$,
and every vertex lies in at least $7$ edges of $H$.

Writing $\tau$ for the least size of a vertex set meeting every edge and $H - e$ for $H$ with the
edge $e$ removed, this asks for $\tau(H) = 3$ and $\tau(H - e) \le 2$ for every edge $e$, with
every vertex of degree at least $7$.

articles.title: Refutation of Erdős Problem 794
articles.statement:
It is not true that for every natural number $n$ and every
family $H$ of $3$-element subsets of $\{0, 1, \dots, 3n - 1\}$ with at least $n^3 + 1$ members,
there is a $4$-element set $S$ such that at least $3$ members of $H$ are subsets of $S$, or there
is a $5$-element set $S$ such that at least $7$ members of $H$ are subsets of $S$.

Phillip Harris gave an explicit counterexample on $9$ vertices.

## Sources

- Phillip Harris counterexample, formalized by Aristotle, ChatGPT, and Boris Alexeev at plby/lean-proofs, https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/8822f7ddef30fadbd92e1c6ab4ed897af356af5e/src/v4.29.1/ErdosProblems/Erdos794.lean.

articles.title: Erdős Problem 794 on dense 3-uniform hypergraphs
articles.statement:
The proposition asserts that for every
natural number $n$ and every family $H$ of $3$-element subsets of $\{0, 1, \dots, 3n - 1\}$ with
at least $n^3 + 1$ members, there is a $4$-element set $S$ such that at least $3$ members of $H$
are subsets of $S$, or there is a $5$-element set $S$ such that at least $7$ members of $H$ are
subsets of $S$.

This is Erdős's original question in its positive form; it is known to be false.

articles.title: Extremal number for $k$ vertices spanning $k - 2$ triples
articles.statement:
For $k, n \in \mathbb{N}$ let
$\mathcal{F}_k$ be the family of all $3$-uniform hypergraphs with $k$ vertices and $k - 2$ edges.
Then $\mathrm{ex}_3(n, \mathcal{F}_k)$ is the largest number of triples in a $3$-uniform
hypergraph $E$ on the vertex set $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ that contains no member of $\mathcal{F}_k$,
meaning that no set of exactly $k$ vertices contains $k - 2$ or more triples of $E$ (a member may
have isolated vertices, and extra triples can be dropped). Here $k - 2$ is read as $0$ when
$k < 2$, and $\mathrm{ex}_3(n, \mathcal{F}_k) = 0$ when no such hypergraph exists, which happens
exactly when $k \le 2$ and $k \le n$.

articles.title: Erdős Problem 1076 fails as worded
articles.statement:
For $k, n \in \mathbb{N}$ let $\mathcal{F}_k$ be the family
of $3$-graphs with $k$ vertices and $k - 2$ edges, and let $\mathrm{ex}_3(n, \mathcal{F}_k)$ be the
largest number of triples in a $3$-uniform hypergraph on $n$ vertices that contains no member of
$\mathcal{F}_k$, that is, in which no $k$ vertices span $k - 2$ or more triples. It is not true
that for every $k \ge 5$, $\mathrm{ex}_3(n, \mathcal{F}_k) / n^2 \to 1/6$ as $n \to \infty$.

Already $k = 5$ fails: Glock proved that the largest triple system on $n$ vertices with no five
vertices spanning three triples has $(1 + o(1)) n^2 / 5$ triples, so
$\mathrm{ex}_3(n, \mathcal{F}_5) / n^2 \to 1/5$; his §1 states this as the answer to whether $1/6$
is sharp for every $k$.

## Sources

- T. F. Bloom, Erdős Problems, Problem #1076, https://www.erdosproblems.com/1076 (status PROVED); resolution: S. Glock, Triple systems with no three triples spanning at most five points, Bull. Lond. Math. Soc. 51 (2019), 230-236, abstract and Theorem 2: lim n⁻² f⁽³⁾(n; 5, 3) = 1/5, where f⁽³⁾(n; k, s) is the largest number of triples on n points containing no k points spanning s triples; §1 poses the question whether the lower bound lim inf n⁻² f⁽³⁾(n; k, k - 2) ≥ 1/6 is sharp in general, and Theorem 2 shows it is not for k = 5 (arXiv:1809.02100), https://arxiv.org/abs/1809.02100.

articles.title: Erdős Problem 1076 as worded
articles.statement:
For $k, n \in \mathbb{N}$ let
$\mathrm{ex}_3(n, \mathcal{F}_k)$ be the largest number of triples in a $3$-uniform hypergraph on
$n$ vertices in which no $k$ vertices span $k - 2$ or more triples, that is, which contains no
member of the family $\mathcal{F}_k$ of $3$-graphs with $k$ vertices and $k - 2$ edges. This is
the statement that for every $k \ge 5$, $\mathrm{ex}_3(n, \mathcal{F}_k) / n^2 \to 1/6$ as
$n \to \infty$, that is, $\mathrm{ex}_3(n, \mathcal{F}_k) \sim n^2 / 6$.

articles.title: The Ruzsa–Szemerédi (6, 3) theorem
articles.statement:
For $n \in \mathbb{N}$ let $\mathrm{ex}_3(n)$ be the
largest number of $3$-element subsets of $\{1, \dots, n\}$ such that every set of at most $6$ of
these points contains at most $2$ of the chosen subsets. Then $\mathrm{ex}_3(n) / n^2 \to 0$ as
$n \to \infty$, that is, $\mathrm{ex}_3(n) = o(n^2)$.

## Sources

- T. F. Bloom, Erdős Problems, Problem #716, https://www.erdosproblems.com/716 (status PROVED (LEAN)); resolution: I. Z. Ruzsa and E. Szemerédi, Triple systems with no six points carrying three triangles, Combinatorics (Proc. Fifth Hungarian Colloq., Keszthely, 1976), Vol. II (1978), 939-945, erdosproblems.com/716: 'The answer is yes, proved by Ruzsa and Szemerédi' (the Ruzsa-Szemerédi problem), https://www.erdosproblems.com/716.

articles.title: The Brown–Erdős–Sós (6, 3) conjecture
articles.statement:
For $n \in \mathbb{N}$ let $\mathrm{ex}_3(n)$ be
the largest number of $3$-element subsets of $\{1, \dots, n\}$ such that every set of at most $6$
of these points contains at most $2$ of the chosen subsets. The conjecture (Erdős Problem 716) is
the proposition that $\mathrm{ex}_3(n) / n^2 \to 0$ as $n \to \infty$, that is,
$\mathrm{ex}_3(n) = o(n^2)$.

articles.title: The (6, 3) extremal number
articles.statement:
For $n \in \mathbb{N}$, $\mathrm{ex}_3(n)$ is the largest
number of $3$-element subsets of $\{1, \dots, n\}$ such that every set of at most $6$ of these
points contains at most $2$ of the chosen subsets.

For $n \ge 6$ this is the extremal number $\mathrm{ex}_3(n, \mathcal{F})$ of the family
$\mathcal{F}$ of $3$-uniform hypergraphs with $6$ vertices and $3$ edges, since a set of triples
contains a member of $\mathcal{F}$ exactly when some $6$ points carry $3$ of the triples.

articles.title: Edges of the complete uniform hypergraph
articles.statement:
For natural numbers $k$ and $m$, the edge
family of the complete $k$-uniform hypergraph on the vertex set $\{0, 1, \dots, m-1\}$ is the
family of all $k$-element subsets of $\{0, 1, \dots, m-1\}$.

## Sources

- [AIM-COMBINATORICS-0149], aim-combinatorics-notes.json notes[148], Source item 11.3, Section Complete hypergraphs, Workshop Hypergraph Turan problem, Source URL http://aimpl.org/hypergraphturan/1/.

articles.title: De Caen's conjecture is false
articles.statement:
It is not the case that $k \, (1 - \pi(K_{k+1}^{(k)}))$
tends to $\infty$ as $k \to \infty$, where $\pi(K_{k+1}^{(k)})$ is the Turán density of the
complete $k$-uniform hypergraph $K_{k+1}^{(k)}$ on $k+1$ vertices.

Pikhurko (Adv. Math. 464 (2025) 110148, Theorem 1.1) proves
$T(n, k+1, k) \le \frac{6.239}{k+1} \binom{n}{k}$ for all $n > k \ge 1$, where $T(n, k+1, k)$
is the least number of $k$-element subsets of an $n$-element set such that every
$(k+1)$-element subset contains one of them; hence $k \, (1 - \pi(K_{k+1}^{(k)})) \le 6.239$
for every $k \ge 1$, and the paper states that this disproves de Caen's conjecture.

## Sources

- O. Pikhurko, Constructions of Turán systems that are tight up to a multiplicative constant, Advances in Mathematics 464 (2025), 110148, https://pikhurko.github.io/E/Pikhurko25am.pdf.

articles.title: De Caen's conjecture on Turán densities of complete hypergraphs
articles.statement:
For a natural number
$k$, let $\pi(K_{k+1}^{(k)})$ be the Turán density of the complete $k$-uniform hypergraph on
$k+1$ vertices. De Caen's conjecture asserts that $k \, (1 - \pi(K_{k+1}^{(k)})) \to \infty$
as $k \to \infty$.

## Sources

- [AIM-COMBINATORICS-0149], aim-combinatorics-notes.json notes[148], Source item 11.3, Section Complete hypergraphs, Workshop Hypergraph Turan problem, Source URL http://aimpl.org/hypergraphturan/1/.

articles.title: Turán density of the complete $k$-graph on $k+1$ vertices
articles.statement:
For a natural number $k$,
the Turán density $\pi(K_{k+1}^{(k)})$ of the complete $k$-uniform hypergraph $K_{k+1}^{(k)}$
on $k+1$ vertices is the limit superior, as $n \to \infty$, of the Turán density ratios
$\mathrm{ex}(n, K_{k+1}^{(k)}) / \binom{n}{k}$, where $\mathrm{ex}(n, K_{k+1}^{(k)})$ is the
Turán number of $K_{k+1}^{(k)}$ and the ratio is taken to be $0$ when $\binom{n}{k} = 0$.

## Sources

- [AIM-COMBINATORICS-0149], aim-combinatorics-notes.json notes[148], Source item 11.3, Section Complete hypergraphs, Workshop Hypergraph Turan problem, Source URL http://aimpl.org/hypergraphturan/1/.

articles.title: Turán density ratio
articles.statement:
For natural numbers $k$ and $n$, the Turán density ratio is the
real number $\mathrm{ex}(n, K_{k+1}^{(k)}) / \binom{n}{k}$, where
$\mathrm{ex}(n, K_{k+1}^{(k)})$ is the Turán number of the complete $k$-uniform hypergraph
$K_{k+1}^{(k)}$ on $k+1$ vertices, the largest number of $k$-element subsets of an $n$-element
set containing no copy of $K_{k+1}^{(k)}$. The ratio is defined to be $0$ when
$\binom{n}{k} = 0$, that is, when $n < k$.

## Sources

- [AIM-COMBINATORICS-0149], aim-combinatorics-notes.json notes[148], Source item 11.3, Section Complete hypergraphs, Workshop Hypergraph Turan problem, Source URL http://aimpl.org/hypergraphturan/1/.

articles.title: Turán number of the complete $k$-graph on $k+1$ vertices
articles.statement:
For natural numbers $k$ and
$n$, let $K_{k+1}^{(k)}$ be the complete $k$-uniform hypergraph on the vertex set
$\{0, 1, \dots, k\}$, whose edges are all $k$-element subsets of that set. The Turán number
$\mathrm{ex}(n, K_{k+1}^{(k)})$ is the largest size of a family $E$ of $k$-element subsets of
$\{0, 1, \dots, n-1\}$ that contains no copy of $K_{k+1}^{(k)}$, that is, for which there is no
injective map $f \colon \{0, 1, \dots, k\} \to \{0, 1, \dots, n-1\}$ such that the image under
$f$ of every edge of $K_{k+1}^{(k)}$ belongs to $E$.

## Sources

- [AIM-COMBINATORICS-0149], aim-combinatorics-notes.json notes[148], Source item 11.3, Section Complete hypergraphs, Workshop Hypergraph Turan problem, Source URL http://aimpl.org/hypergraphturan/1/.

articles.title: Blow-up of a hypergraph along a map
articles.statement:
Let $D$ be a family of subsets of
$\{0, \dots, m-1\}$, let $r \in \mathbb{N}$ and let $\varphi : \{0, \dots, n-1\} \to
\{0, \dots, m-1\}$. The $r$-uniform blow-up of $D$ along $\varphi$ is the family of $r$-element
subsets $e \subseteq \{0, \dots, n-1\}$ such that $\varphi$ is injective on $e$ and the image
$\varphi(e)$ is a block of $D$.

articles.title: Generalized triangle $\mathcal{T}_r$
articles.statement:
Let $r, n \in \mathbb{N}$ and let $G$ be a family of
subsets of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$, typically an $r$-uniform hypergraph. Then $G$ contains a
generalized triangle $\mathcal{T}_r$ (the book $B_{r,2}$) when there are edges
$D_1, D_2, D_3 \in G$, not necessarily distinct, with $|D_1 \cap D_2| + 1 = r$,
$D_1 \triangle D_2 \subseteq D_3$ and $D_3 \cap D_1 \cap D_2 = \emptyset$.

articles.title: Norin–Yepremyan theorem for $\mathcal{T}_5$
articles.statement:
There exist a Steiner system $D$ of type
$S(4, 5, 11)$ on $\{0, \dots, 10\}$ and an $n_0 \in \mathbb{N}$ such that for every $n \ge n_0$,
the Turán number $\mathrm{ex}(n, \mathcal{T}_5)$ of the generalized triangle $\mathcal{T}_5$ (the
book $B_{5,2}$) equals the largest number of edges of a $5$-uniform blow-up of $D$ along a map
$\{0, \dots, n-1\} \to \{0, \dots, 10\}$.

Norin and Yepremyan proved more: for all large $n$, every extremal $\mathcal{T}_5$-free
$5$-uniform hypergraph on $n$ vertices is a blow-up of $S(4, 5, 11)$ (the Frankl–Füredi
construction).

## Sources

- AimPL: Hypergraph Turán problem, Problem 2.1 (Frankl-Füredi), http://aimpl.org/hypergraphturan/2/; resolution: S. Norin and L. Yepremyan, Turán number of generalized triangles, J. Combin. Theory Ser. A 146 (2017), 312-343, arXiv:1501.01913, Theorem 1.1: there is n0 such that for all n ≥ n0, ex(n, 𝒯_r) = ex(n, Σ_r) for r = 5, 6, and the extremal graphs are blow-ups of the unique (11, 5, 4) and (12, 6, 5) Steiner systems; the blow-ups are the Frankl-Füredi lower-bound constructions named in the AimPL problem, https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jcta.2016.09.003.

articles.title: Turán number of $\mathcal{T}_5$ via blow-ups of $S(4, 5, 11)$
articles.statement:
There exist a Steiner system
$D$ of type $S(4, 5, 11)$ on $\{0, \dots, 10\}$ and an $n_0 \in \mathbb{N}$ such that for every
$n \ge n_0$, the Turán number $\mathrm{ex}(n, \mathcal{T}_5)$ of the generalized triangle
$\mathcal{T}_5$ (the book $B_{5,2}$) equals the largest number of edges of a $5$-uniform blow-up
of $D$ along a map $\{0, \dots, n-1\} \to \{0, \dots, 10\}$.

## Sources

- AimPL Problem 2.1 (Hypergraph Turán problem), case `k = 5`.

articles.title: Norin–Yepremyan theorem for $\mathcal{T}_6$
articles.statement:
There exist a Steiner system $D$ of type
$S(5, 6, 12)$ on $\{0, \dots, 11\}$ and an $n_0 \in \mathbb{N}$ such that for every $n \ge n_0$,
the Turán number $\mathrm{ex}(n, \mathcal{T}_6)$ of the generalized triangle $\mathcal{T}_6$ (the
book $B_{6,2}$) equals the largest number of edges of a $6$-uniform blow-up of $D$ along a map
$\{0, \dots, n-1\} \to \{0, \dots, 11\}$.

Norin and Yepremyan proved more: for all large $n$, every extremal $\mathcal{T}_6$-free
$6$-uniform hypergraph on $n$ vertices is a blow-up of $S(5, 6, 12)$ (the Frankl–Füredi
construction).

Theory Ser. A 146 (2017), 312-343, arXiv:1501.01913, Theorem 1.1: there is n0 such that for all n ≥ n0, ex(n, 𝒯_r) = ex(n, Σ_r) for r = 5, 6, and the extremal graphs are blow-ups of the unique (11, 5, 4) and (12, 6, 5) Steiner systems; the blow-ups are the Frankl-Füredi lower-bound constructions named in the AimPL problem, https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jcta.2016.09.003.

articles.title: Turán number of $\mathcal{T}_6$ via blow-ups of $S(5, 6, 12)$
articles.statement:
There exist a Steiner system
$D$ of type $S(5, 6, 12)$ on $\{0, \dots, 11\}$ and an $n_0 \in \mathbb{N}$ such that for every
$n \ge n_0$, the Turán number $\mathrm{ex}(n, \mathcal{T}_6)$ of the generalized triangle
$\mathcal{T}_6$ (the book $B_{6,2}$) equals the largest number of edges of a $6$-uniform blow-up
of $D$ along a map $\{0, \dots, n-1\} \to \{0, \dots, 11\}$.

## Sources

- AimPL Problem 2.1 (Hypergraph Turán problem), case `k = 6`.

articles.title: Turán number of the generalized triangle
articles.statement:
For $r, n \in \mathbb{N}$, the Turán number
$\mathrm{ex}(n, \mathcal{T}_r)$ is the largest number of edges of an $r$-uniform hypergraph on the
vertex set $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ that contains no generalized triangle $\mathcal{T}_r$.

articles.title: Steiner system $S(t, r, m)$
articles.statement:
Let $t, r, m \in \mathbb{N}$ and let $D$ be a family of
subsets of $\{0, \dots, m-1\}$. Then $D$ is a Steiner system $S(t, r, m)$ when every block of $D$
has exactly $r$ elements and every $t$-element subset of $\{0, \dots, m-1\}$ is contained in
exactly one block of $D$.

articles.title: Largest blow-up of a hypergraph
articles.statement:
Let $D$ be a family of subsets of $\{0, \dots, m-1\}$
and let $r, n \in \mathbb{N}$. The largest blow-up size of $D$ is the maximum, over all maps
$\varphi : \{0, \dots, n-1\} \to \{0, \dots, m-1\}$, of the number of edges of the $r$-uniform
blow-up of $D$ along $\varphi$; it is $0$ when there is no such map.

articles.title: The complete $r$-graph is a Turán system
articles.statement:
Let $n$, $s$, $r$ be natural numbers with
$0 < r < s \le n$. Then the complete $r$-graph on $\{0, 1, \dots, n-1\}$ (the family of all its
$r$-element subsets) is a Turán $(n, s, r)$-system.

articles.title: The complete $r$-graph is $r$-uniform
articles.statement:
For all natural numbers $n$ and $r$, every member
of the complete $r$-graph on $\{0, 1, \dots, n-1\}$ has exactly $r$ elements.

articles.title: The complete $r$-graph
articles.statement:
For natural numbers $n$ and $r$, the complete $r$-graph on $n$
vertices is the family of all $r$-element subsets of $\{0, 1, \dots, n-1\}$.

articles.title: Turán systems cover every $s$-set
articles.statement:
Let $n$, $s$, $r$ be natural numbers and let $H$ be a
Turán $(n, s, r)$-system. Then every $s$-element subset $T$ of $\{0, 1, \dots, n-1\}$ contains
some member $e$ of $H$.

articles.title: Turán systems exist
articles.statement:
For all natural numbers $n$, $s$, $r$ with $0 < r < s \le n$, there
is a Turán $(n, s, r)$-system.

articles.title: Turán system
articles.statement:
Let $n$, $s$, $r$ be natural numbers. A family $H$ of subsets of
$\{0, 1, \dots, n-1\}$ is a Turán $(n, s, r)$-system when $0 < r < s \le n$, $H$ is
$r$-uniform (every member of $H$ has exactly $r$ elements), and every $s$-element subset of
$\{0, 1, \dots, n-1\}$ contains some member of $H$.

articles.title: A Turán system has $s \le n$
articles.statement:
Let $n$, $s$, $r$ be natural numbers and let $H$ be a
Turán $(n, s, r)$-system. Then $s \le n$.

articles.title: Lower bounds on the Turán number
articles.statement:
Let $n$, $s$, $r$, $b$ be natural numbers with
$0 < r < s \le n$. If $b \le k$ for every $k$ in the set of realized sizes for $(n, s, r)$
(the sizes of Turán $(n, s, r)$-systems), then $b$ is at most the Turán number $T(n, s, r)$.

articles.title: A Turán system has $r < s$
articles.statement:
Let $n$, $s$, $r$ be natural numbers and let $H$ be a
Turán $(n, s, r)$-system. Then $r < s$.

articles.title: Membership in the realized sizes
articles.statement:
For natural numbers $n$, $s$, $r$, $k$, the number $k$
lies in the set of realized sizes for $(n, s, r)$ if and only if some Turán $(n, s, r)$-system
$H$ has exactly $k$ members.

articles.title: Turán systems have positive uniformity
articles.statement:
Let $n$, $s$, $r$ be natural numbers and let $H$
be a Turán system with parameters $n$, $s$, $r$, whose definition includes $0 < r < s \le n$.
Then $0 < r$.

articles.title: Some size of a Turán system is realized
articles.statement:
For natural numbers $n$, $s$, $r$ with
$0 < r < s \le n$, the set of realized sizes for $n$, $s$, $r$ is nonempty: some natural number
$k$ is the number of members of a Turán system with parameters $n$, $s$, $r$.

articles.title: Realized sizes of Turán systems
articles.statement:
For natural numbers $n$, $s$, $r$, the set of realized
sizes is the set of natural numbers $k$ such that some Turán system with parameters $n$, $s$, $r$
on the vertex set $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ has exactly $k$ members.

articles.title: The Turán number is attained
articles.statement:
Let $n$, $s$, $r$ be natural numbers with $0 < r < s \le n$
and let $T(n, s, r)$ denote the Turán number. Then some Turán system with parameters $n$, $s$,
$r$ has exactly $T(n, s, r)$ members.

articles.title: Turán systems are at least as large as the Turán number
articles.statement:
Let $n$, $s$, $r$ be natural
numbers and let $T(n, s, r)$ denote the Turán number. If $H$ is a Turán system with parameters
$n$, $s$, $r$, then $T(n, s, r) \le |H|$.

articles.title: The Turán number is a realized size
articles.statement:
Let $n$, $s$, $r$ be natural numbers with
$0 < r < s \le n$ and let $T(n, s, r)$ denote the Turán number. Then $T(n, s, r)$ belongs to the
set of realized sizes for $n$, $s$, $r$.

articles.title: Turán number
articles.statement:
For natural numbers $n$, $s$, $r$, the Turán number $T(n, s, r)$ is the
least element of the set of realized sizes for $n$, $s$, $r$, that is, the least number of members
of a Turán system with parameters $n$, $s$, $r$, and $T(n, s, r) = 0$ if no such system exists.

articles.title: Turán systems are uniform
articles.statement:
Let $n$, $s$, $r$ be natural numbers. If $H$ is a Turán system
with parameters $n$, $s$, $r$, then $H$ is $r$-uniform: every member of $H$ has exactly $r$
elements.

articles.title: Chvátal's conjecture holds
articles.statement:
For every finite set $X$ and every hereditary family $F$ of
subsets of $X$ (one containing every subset of each of its members) that contains a nonempty set,
there is a point $x \in X$ such that every intersecting subfamily $G \subseteq F$ (one in which
any two distinct members meet) has at most as many members as the star $\{A \in F : x \in A\}$.

Resolved true: Chang, Liu, and Liu (arXiv:2609.19123, 2026) prove Chvátal's conjecture. Ellis,
Filmus, and Friedgut (arXiv:2609.28404) give an independent spectral proof, and Keevash
(arXiv:2609.23595) proves the stronger Kahn flow conjecture. erdosproblems.com/701 lists the
Chang–Liu–Liu proof claim with a Lean formalization by Boon Suan Ho.

## Sources

- Fan Chang, Hong Liu, and Miao Liu, A proof of Chvátal's conjecture via a sharp correlation inequality, arXiv:2609.19123 (2026), https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.19123; David Ellis, Yuval Filmus, and Ehud Friedgut, Chvátal's conjecture: a proof from The Book, arXiv:2609.28404v2 (2026), https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.28404; Peter Keevash, On Kahn's flow conjecture, arXiv:2609.23595 (2026), https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.23595.

articles.title: Chvátal's conjecture
articles.statement:
The statement that for every finite set $X$ and every hereditary
family $F$ of subsets of $X$ that contains a nonempty set, there is a point $x \in X$ such that
every intersecting subfamily $G \subseteq F$ has at most as many members as the star
$\{A \in F : x \in A\}$ of $x$. Here $F$ is hereditary when it contains every subset of each of
its members, and $G$ is intersecting when any two distinct members of $G$ meet.

The point $x$ is fixed for the whole family, and the competing subfamilies $G$ need not be
hereditary.

articles.title: Hereditary families
articles.statement:
A finite family $F$ of finite subsets of $\alpha$ is hereditary (an
independence system) when it contains every subset of each of its members: if $A \in F$ and
$B \subseteq A$, then $B \in F$.

articles.title: Number of comparable pairs
articles.statement:
For $n \in \mathbb{N}$ and a family $F$ of subsets of
$\{0, \dots, n - 1\}$, the number of comparable pairs of $F$ is the number of ordered pairs
$(A, B)$ of members of $F$ with $A \subsetneq B$. It is the number of edges of the comparability
graph $G_F$ on $F$, in which two distinct members are adjacent when one contains the other.

articles.title: Negative answer to Erdős Problem 777, second question
articles.statement:
It is not the case that for every
real $c > 0$ there is a real constant $C$ such that for every $n$ and every family $F$ of subsets
of $\{0, \dots, n - 1\}$ with at least $c |F|^2$ comparable pairs (ordered pairs $(A, B)$ of
members of $F$ with $A \subsetneq B$), we have $|F| \le C \cdot 2^{n/2}$. Equivalently, there is
a real $c > 0$ such that for every real $C$ some $n$ and some family $F$ of subsets of
$\{0, \dots, n - 1\}$ with at least $c |F|^2$ comparable pairs have $|F| > C \cdot 2^{n/2}$.

Alon and Frankl's Example 6.1 with $d = 1$ gives such families: $m \gg n 2^{n/2}$ subsets of an
$n$-element set with at least $2^{-5} \binom{m}{2}$ comparable pairs (erdosproblems.com/777).

## Sources

- T. F. Bloom, Erdős Problems, Problem #777, https://www.erdosproblems.com/777 (status SOLVED); resolution: N. Alon and P. Frankl, The maximum number of disjoint pairs in a family of subsets, Graphs Combin. 1 (1985), 13-21; N. Alon, S. Das, R. Glebov and B. Sudakov, Comparable pairs in families of sets, J. Combin. Theory Ser. B (2015), 164-185, arXiv:1411.4196, Alon-Frankl Theorem 1.4: for every k ≥ 1 there is β(k) > 0 such that for m = 2^{(1/(k+1) + δ)n}, c(n, m) < (1 - 1/k) C(m, 2) + O(m^{2 - β δ^{k+1}}), the case k = 1 conjectured by Daykin and Erdős; Alon-Frankl Section 6, Example 6.1: the sets meeting the second half of [n] in at most d elements or missing at most d elements of the first half form a family of Θ(n^d 2^{n/2}) sets with a constant fraction of comparable pairs, disproving a conjecture of Erdős; erdosproblems.com/777: Alon and Frankl answer the third question in the affirmative and the second in the negative, and an affirmative answer to the first follows from Theorem 1.4 and Corollary 1.5 of Alon, Das, Glebov and Sudakov, https://www.erdosproblems.com/777.

articles.title: Erdős Problem 777, second question
articles.statement:
For every real $c > 0$ there is a real constant $C$
such that for every $n$ and every family $F$ of subsets of $\{0, \dots, n - 1\}$ with at least
$c |F|^2$ comparable pairs (ordered pairs $(A, B)$ of members of $F$ with $A \subsetneq B$), we
have $|F| \le C \cdot 2^{n/2}$.

articles.title: Affirmative answer to Erdős Problem 777, first question
articles.statement:
For every real $\varepsilon > 0$
there is $N$ such that for every $n \ge N$, every family $F$ of subsets of $\{0, \dots, n - 1\}$
with $|F| \le (2 - \varepsilon) 2^{n/2}$ has fewer than $2^n$ comparable pairs, that is, ordered
pairs $(A, B)$ of members of $F$ with $A \subsetneq B$.

The bound is sharp: for even $n$, a family of $m = 2^{n/2 + 1}$ subsets formed by two stacked
subcubes has at least $2^n$ comparable pairs. According to erdosproblems.com/777 the affirmative
answer follows from Theorem 1.4 and Corollary 1.5 of Alon, Das, Glebov and Sudakov.

## Sources

- T. F. Bloom, Erdős Problems, Problem #777, https://www.erdosproblems.com/777 (status SOLVED); resolution: N. Alon and P. Frankl, The maximum number of disjoint pairs in a family of subsets, Graphs Combin. 1 (1985), 13-21; N. Alon, S. Das, R. Glebov and B. Sudakov, Comparable pairs in families of sets, J. Combin. Theory Ser. B (2015), 164-185, arXiv:1411.4196, Alon-Frankl Theorem 1.4: for every k ≥ 1 there is β(k) > 0 such that for m = 2^{(1/(k+1) + δ)n}, c(n, m) < (1 - 1/k) C(m, 2) + O(m^{2 - β δ^{k+1}}), the case k = 1 conjectured by Daykin and Erdős; Alon-Frankl Section 6, Example 6.1: the sets meeting the second half of [n] in at most d elements or missing at most d elements of the first half form a family of Θ(n^d 2^{n/2}) sets with a constant fraction of comparable pairs, disproving a conjecture of Erdős; erdosproblems.com/777: Alon and Frankl answer the third question in the affirmative and the second in the negative, and an affirmative answer to the first follows from Theorem 1.4 and Corollary 1.5 of Alon, Das, Glebov and Sudakov, https://www.erdosproblems.com/777.

articles.title: Erdős Problem 777, first question
articles.statement:
For every real $\varepsilon > 0$ there is $N$ such that
for every $n \ge N$, every family $F$ of subsets of $\{0, \dots, n - 1\}$ with
$|F| \le (2 - \varepsilon) 2^{n/2}$ has fewer than $2^n$ comparable pairs, that is, ordered pairs
$(A, B)$ of members of $F$ with $A \subsetneq B$.

articles.title: Affirmative answer to Erdős Problem 777, third question
articles.statement:
For every real $\varepsilon > 0$
there is a real $\delta > 0$ such that for every $n$, every family $F$ of subsets of
$\{0, \dots, n - 1\}$ with more than $|F|^{2 - \delta}$ comparable pairs (ordered pairs $(A, B)$
of members of $F$ with $A \subsetneq B$) satisfies $|F| < (2 + \varepsilon)^{n/2}$.

According to erdosproblems.com/777 this follows from the case $k = 1$ of Theorem 1.4 of Alon and
Frankl, conjectured by Daykin and Erdős: there is $\beta > 0$ such that for every $\eta > 0$, a
family of $m = 2^{(1/2 + \eta) n}$ subsets of an $n$-element set has $O(m^{2 - \beta \eta^2})$
comparable pairs.

## Sources

- T. F. Bloom, Erdős Problems, Problem #777, https://www.erdosproblems.com/777 (status SOLVED); resolution: N. Alon and P. Frankl, The maximum number of disjoint pairs in a family of subsets, Graphs Combin. 1 (1985), 13-21; N. Alon, S. Das, R. Glebov and B. Sudakov, Comparable pairs in families of sets, J. Combin. Theory Ser. B (2015), 164-185, arXiv:1411.4196, Alon-Frankl Theorem 1.4: for every k ≥ 1 there is β(k) > 0 such that for m = 2^{(1/(k+1) + δ)n}, c(n, m) < (1 - 1/k) C(m, 2) + O(m^{2 - β δ^{k+1}}), the case k = 1 conjectured by Daykin and Erdős; Alon-Frankl Section 6, Example 6.1: the sets meeting the second half of [n] in at most d elements or missing at most d elements of the first half form a family of Θ(n^d 2^{n/2}) sets with a constant fraction of comparable pairs, disproving a conjecture of Erdős; erdosproblems.com/777: Alon and Frankl answer the third question in the affirmative and the second in the negative, and an affirmative answer to the first follows from Theorem 1.4 and Corollary 1.5 of Alon, Das, Glebov and Sudakov, https://www.erdosproblems.com/777.

articles.title: Erdős Problem 777, third question
articles.statement:
For every real $\varepsilon > 0$ there is a real
$\delta > 0$ such that for every $n$, every family $F$ of subsets of $\{0, \dots, n - 1\}$ with
more than $|F|^{2 - \delta}$ comparable pairs (ordered pairs $(A, B)$ of members of $F$ with
$A \subsetneq B$) satisfies $|F| < (2 + \varepsilon)^{n/2}$.

articles.title: $K(d)$-families
articles.statement:
Let $n$, $k$ and $d$ be natural numbers and let
$[n] = \{0, 1, \dots, n - 1\}$. A family $G$ of subsets of $[n]$ is a $K(d)$-family of
$k$-subsets when every member of $G$ has exactly $k$ elements and any $d$ distinct members
$A_1, \dots, A_d$ of $G$ with $|A_1 \cup \dots \cup A_d| \le 2k$ have a common element.

articles.title: Mubayi's Erdős–Ko–Rado conjecture for $K(d)$-families holds
articles.statement:
For all natural numbers $n$, $k$
and $d$ with $3 \le d \le k$ and $n \ge dk/(d - 1)$, every $K(d)$-family $G$ of $k$-subsets of
$[n] = \{0, 1, \dots, n - 1\}$ satisfies $|G| \le \binom{n-1}{k-1}$, and if
$|G| = \binom{n-1}{k-1}$ then some element of $[n]$ lies in every member of $G$.

Currier proved the bound for $2 \le d \le k$, with the equality case for $d \ge 3$.

## Sources

- D. Mubayi, in Combinatorics, Probability and Computing, Oberwolfach Reports 3 (2006), no. 48, p. 2922, Conjecture 3, DOI 10.4171/OWR/2006/48; resolution: G. Currier, On the d-cluster generalization of Erdős-Ko-Rado, J. Combin. Theory Ser. A 182 (2021), 105464, arXiv:1812.11153, abstract and Theorem 2: for 2 ≤ d ≤ k and n ≥ dk/(d - 1), a family of k-subsets of [n] with no d-cluster (d members with empty intersection and union of size at most 2k) has at most C(n - 1, k - 1) members, with equality only for a full star (d ≥ 3); this resolves Mubayi's conjecture, https://arxiv.org/abs/1812.11153.

articles.title: Mubayi's Erdős–Ko–Rado conjecture for $K(d)$-families
articles.statement:
For all natural numbers $n$, $k$
and $d$ with $3 \le d \le k$ and $n \ge dk/(d - 1)$, every $K(d)$-family $G$ of $k$-subsets of
$[n] = \{0, 1, \dots, n - 1\}$ satisfies $|G| \le \binom{n-1}{k-1}$, and if
$|G| = \binom{n-1}{k-1}$ then some element of $[n]$ lies in every member of $G$.

## Sources

- D. Mubayi, Oberwolfach Report 48/2006, Conjecture 3.

articles.title: Frankl's theorem on families with no singleton intersection
articles.statement:
For every $k \ge 4$ and every
sufficiently large $n$ (depending on $k$), every family of more than $\binom{n-2}{k-2}$ subsets of
$\{1, \dots, n\}$, each with exactly $k$ elements, contains two sets $A$ and $B$ with
$|A \cap B| = 1$.

This resolves Erdős Problem 702 of Erdős and Sós; Katona had the case $k = 4$. The hypothesis that
$n$ is large is needed ($k = 4$, $n = 5$).

## Sources

- T. F. Bloom, Erdős Problems, Problem #702, https://www.erdosproblems.com/702 (status PROVED); resolution: P. Frankl, On families of finite sets no two of which intersect in a singleton, Bull. Austral. Math. Soc. 17 (1977), 125-134, P. Keevash, D. Mubayi and R. M. Wilson, Set systems with no singleton intersection, abstract: 'Frankl showed that |F| ≤ C(n-2, k-2) for k ≥ 4 and n sufficiently large, confirming a conjecture of Erdős and Sós'; erdosproblems.com/702: Frankl proved this for all k ≥ 4, https://www.math.cmu.edu/users/mubayi/papers/no-singleton.pdf.

articles.title: Erdős Problem 702 on singleton intersections
articles.statement:
For every $k \ge 4$ and every sufficiently
large $n$ (depending on $k$), every family of more than $\binom{n-2}{k-2}$ subsets of
$\{1, \dots, n\}$, each with exactly $k$ elements, contains two sets $A$ and $B$ with
$|A \cap B| = 1$.

This is Frankl's form of the problem of Erdős and Sós; without the hypothesis that $n$ is large
the statement fails, for instance for $k = 4$ and $n = 5$.

articles.title: Frankl–Rödl forbidden intersection theorem
articles.statement:
For every $\varepsilon > 0$ there is $\delta > 0$
such that for all natural numbers $n$ and $r$ with $\varepsilon n < r < (1/2 - \varepsilon) n$,
every family $\mathcal{F}$ of subsets of $\{1, \dots, n\}$ with $|A \cap B| \ne r$ for all
$A, B \in \mathcal{F}$ (including $A = B$) has $|\mathcal{F}| < (2 - \delta)^n$. This answers the
second question of Erdős Problem 703 in the affirmative.

## Sources

- T. F. Bloom, Erdős Problems, Problem #703, https://www.erdosproblems.com/703 (status PROVED (LEAN)); resolution: P. Frankl and V. Rödl, Forbidden intersections, Trans. Amer. Math. Soc. 300 (1987), 259-286, erdosproblems.com/703: 'The answer to the second question is yes, proved by Frankl and Rödl', https://www.erdosproblems.com/703.

articles.title: Erdős Problem 703: exponential gap for a forbidden intersection size
articles.statement:
The proposition that
for every $\varepsilon > 0$ there is $\delta > 0$ such that for all natural numbers $n$ and $r$ with
$\varepsilon n < r < (1/2 - \varepsilon) n$, every family $\mathcal{F}$ of subsets of
$\{1, \dots, n\}$ with $|A \cap B| \ne r$ for all $A, B \in \mathcal{F}$ (including $A = B$) has
$|\mathcal{F}| < (2 - \delta)^n$. Equivalently, $T(n, r) < (2 - \delta)^n$, where $T(n, r)$ is the
largest size of such a family.

articles.title: Hamming expansion
articles.statement:
Let $\iota$ and $F$ be finite, and view functions $\iota \to F$ as
words with the Hamming distance. For a finite set $A$ of words and $t \in \mathbb{N}$, the
$t$-expansion of $A$ is the set of words at Hamming distance at most $t$ from some element of
$A$, that is, the union over $a \in A$ of the closed Hamming balls of radius $t$ about $a$.

articles.title: Harper's isoperimetric inequality on the Hamming cube
articles.statement:
Let $n$ be a natural number. For
points $x, y \in \{0,1\}^n$, write $d_H(x, y)$ for the Hamming distance between them, the number
of coordinates in which they differ. For a set $S \subseteq \{0,1\}^n$ and a natural number $t$,
write $S_t$ for the set of points $x \in \{0,1\}^n$ with $d_H(x, s) \le t$ for some $s \in S$.
Let $A$ and $B$ be subsets of $\{0,1\}^n$ such that $B$ is a closed Hamming ball, that is,
$B = \{x : d_H(c, x) \le e\}$ for some $c \in \{0,1\}^n$ and some natural number $e$, and such
that $|B| \le |A|$. Then $|B_t| \le |A_t|$ for every natural number $t \ge 1$.

This is only the ball-comparison form of Harper's theorem: it does not assert that a ball
exists at every cardinality and gives no equality cases.

## Sources

- ATLAS ProbabilisticMethodsInCombinatorics, Theorem 9.4.3; the course text cites Harper without proof.
- L. H. Harper, "Optimal numberings and isoperimetric problems on graphs," Journal of Combinatorial Theory 1(3) (1966), 385–393, DOI 10.1016/S0021-9800(66)80059-5.

articles.title: Hamming ball predicate
articles.statement:
Let $\iota$ and $F$ be finite, and view functions $\iota \to F$
as words with the Hamming distance. A set $B$ of words is a Hamming ball if there are a word
$c$ and a radius $e \in \mathbb{N}$ such that $B$ is the closed Hamming ball of radius $e$
about $c$.

articles.title: Bound for 2-intersecting families of half-size sets (Erdős Problem 83)
articles.statement:
For every natural
number $n$, every family $F$ of $2n$-element subsets of $\{0, \dots, 4n-1\}$ such that
$|A \cap B| \ge 2$ for all $A, B \in F$ (including $A = B$) satisfies
$2|F| + \binom{2n}{n}^2 \le \binom{4n}{2n}$, that is,
$|F| \le \frac{1}{2}\left(\binom{4n}{2n} - \binom{2n}{n}^2\right)$.

Ahlswede and Khachatrian proved this as a case of their complete intersection theorem, which
determines the largest $t$-intersecting families of $k$-element subsets of an $m$-element set. The
bound is attained by the $2n$-element sets with at least $n + 1$ elements in $\{0, \dots, 2n-1\}$.

## Sources

- T. F. Bloom, Erdős Problems, Problem #83, https://www.erdosproblems.com/83 (status PROVED (LEAN)); resolution: R. Ahlswede and L. H. Khachatrian, The complete intersection theorem for systems of finite sets, European J. Combin. 18 (1997), 125-136, erdosproblems.com/83: for 2 ≤ t ≤ k ≤ m and r with 1/(r + 1) ≤ (m - 2k + 2t - 2)/((t - 1)(k - t + 1)) < 1/r, the largest family of k-subsets of [m] with pairwise intersections of size at least t consists of the k-sets with at least t + r elements of {1, …, t + 2r}; for m = 4n, k = 2n, t = 2 the ratio is 2/(2n - 1), so r = n - 1 and the family is the 2n-sets with at least n + 1 elements of [2n], https://doi.org/10.1006/eujc.1995.0092.

articles.title: Erdős Problem 83
articles.statement:
The assertion that, for every natural number $n$, every family $F$ of
$2n$-element subsets of $\{0, \dots, 4n-1\}$ such that $|A \cap B| \ge 2$ for all $A, B \in F$
(including $A = B$) satisfies $2|F| + \binom{2n}{n}^2 \le \binom{4n}{2n}$, that is,
$|F| \le \frac{1}{2}\left(\binom{4n}{2n} - \binom{2n}{n}^2\right)$.

articles.title: Macaulay's theorem for monomials
articles.statement:
Let $k \ge 0$ and let $A$ be a finite set of
monomials of degree $k + 1$ in the variables $x_0, x_1, x_2, \dots$, given by their exponent
vectors: finitely supported $a \colon \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ with $\sum_j a_j = k + 1$.
Suppose that $|A| = \sum_{i=0}^{k} \binom{d_i}{i + 1}$ for natural numbers
$d_0 < d_1 < \dots < d_k$. Let the shadow $\partial A$ be the set of exponent vectors obtained
from some $a \in A$ by lowering one positive coordinate $a_j$ by $1$. Then $\partial A$ has at
least $\sum_{0 \le i \le k,\ d_i \ge 1} \binom{d_i - 1}{i}$ elements.

Terms with $d_i = 0$, which can occur only for $i = 0$, contribute nothing to the bound.

Proof: following Ábrego, Fernández-Merchant, and Llano, from a binomial-cascade split
inequality and induction on coordinate slices (their route from Theorem 1 to Theorem M).

## Sources

- Bernardo M. Ábrego, Silvia Fernández-Merchant, and Bernardo Llano, "An Inequality for Macaulay Functions," Journal of Integer Sequences 14 (2011), Theorem M, lines 215–223. Source: <https://cs.uwaterloo.ca/journals/JIS/VOL14/Abrego/abrego2.tex>.

articles.title: Multicolored sunflower
articles.statement:
Let $n$ be a natural number and let $S$ be a finite set of triples
$(x, y, z)$ of vectors in $(\mathbb{Z}/3)^n$. Then $S$ contains a multicolored sunflower if there
are triples $(x_1, y_1, z_1), (x_2, y_2, z_2), (x_3, y_3, z_3) \in S$, not all three equal, with
$x_1 + y_2 + z_3 = 0$.

articles.title: The multicolored sunflower conjecture holds
articles.statement:
There are a real number $\varepsilon > 0$ and a
natural number $n_0$ such that for every $n > n_0$, every finite set $S$ of triples $(x, y, z)$ of
vectors in $(\mathbb{Z}/3)^n$ with $x + y + z = 0$ for every $(x, y, z) \in S$ and with
$|S| \ge 3^{(1 - \varepsilon) n}$ contains a multicolored sunflower: triples
$(x_1, y_1, z_1), (x_2, y_2, z_2), (x_3, y_3, z_3) \in S$, not all three equal, with
$x_1 + y_2 + z_3 = 0$.

This was resolved in the affirmative: a set $S$ as above with no multicolored sunflower is a
tricolored sum-free set ($x_a + y_b + z_c = 0$ only for $a = b = c$), and Blasiak, Church, Cohn,
Grochow, Naslund, Sawin and Umans proved (Theorem A′) that such sets in $(\mathbb{Z}/3)^n$ have at
most $3 \cdot 3^{(1 - \delta/\log 3) n}$ elements, $\delta = 0.0566\ldots$; Alon, Shpilka and Umans
had shown that this tricolored version of the cap set bound disproves the strong USP conjecture.

## Sources

- C. Umans, in Complexity Theory, Oberwolfach Reports 9 (2012), no. 54, p. 3292, Conjecture 7, DOI 10.4171/OWR/2012/54; resolution: J. Blasiak, T. Church, H. Cohn, J. A. Grochow, E. Naslund, W. F. Sawin and C. Umans, On cap sets and the group-theoretic approach to matrix multiplication, Discrete Anal. 2017:3, arXiv:1605.06702, Theorem A′: for H ≅ (ℤ/q)ⁿ, q a prime power, every tricolored sum-free set in H (Definition 3.1) has at most 3 |H|^{1 - δ/log q} elements, δ = 0.0566...; Section 1: Alon, Shpilka and Umans showed that a tricolored version of the cap set bounds would disprove the strong USP conjecture (the source's Theorem 8), and Theorem A disproves it via their result; Kleinberg, Sawin and Speyer, arXiv:1607.00047, abstract, restate the bound as 3 θⁿ, θ ≈ 2.755, https://arxiv.org/abs/1605.06702.

articles.title: Multicolored sunflower conjecture
articles.statement:
There are a real number $\varepsilon > 0$ and a natural
number $n_0$ such that for every $n > n_0$, every finite set $S$ of triples $(x, y, z)$ of vectors
in $(\mathbb{Z}/3)^n$ with $x + y + z = 0$ for every $(x, y, z) \in S$ and with
$|S| \ge 3^{(1 - \varepsilon) n}$ contains a multicolored sunflower: triples
$(x_1, y_1, z_1), (x_2, y_2, z_2), (x_3, y_3, z_3) \in S$, not all three equal, with
$x_1 + y_2 + z_3 = 0$.

The conjecture is due to Alon, Shpilka and Umans (Oberwolfach Report 54/2012, Conjecture 7).

articles.title: Ternary vectors
articles.statement:
For a natural number $n$, the vectors of length $n$ over $\mathbb{Z}/3$,
that is, the functions from $\{0, 1, \dots, n - 1\}$ to $\mathbb{Z}/3$.

articles.title: Sunflower constant
articles.statement:
An unspecified real number $C$, the absolute constant in the
Alweiss–Lovett–Wu–Zhang sunflower bound (Theorem 1.4); it does not depend on $r$ or $w$.

## Sources

- R. Alweiss, S. Lovett, K. Wu, and J. Zhang, `Improved bounds for the sunflower lemma`, Annals of Math, 194 (3) 2021. Statement taken from https://github.com/ImperialCollegeLondon/AnnalsChallenge. Problem `annals_improved_bounds_sunflower_lemma` of the lean-eval benchmark.

articles.title: The Erdős–Szemerédi sunflower bound for $k \ge 4$
articles.statement:
For every natural number $k \ge 4$ there
is a real number $c$ with $0 < c < 2$ such that, for all sufficiently large $n$, every family of
subsets of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ that contains no $k$-sunflower has at most $c^n$ members. Here a
$k$-sunflower in a family is a choice of $k$ distinct members whose pairwise intersections are
all equal.

Resolved true: Proved: Bucić, He and Lee (arXiv:2610.26686, 2026, Theorem 1) show that for every
k >= 3 and n >= 1 a family of subsets of [n] with no k-sunflower has at most 3(2 - 1/(16k^3))^n
members, which gives the formalized bound c^n with c < 2 for each k >= 4 and all large n.
erdosproblems.com/857 (checked 2026-10-22) records this bound as known. The paper states that
the proof of its vector-sunflower bound (Theorem 2) was found by ChatGPT 6 Astra Pro and
verified by the authors. Source: Matija Bucić, Fankang He and Hyunwoo Lee, Proof of the
Erdős-Szemerédi sunflower conjecture, arXiv:2610.26686 (2026), https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.26686;
T. F. Bloom, Erdős Problem #857, erdosproblems.com, https://www.erdosproblems.com/857. Moved
from `OpenConjectures/Combinatorics/ErdosProblem857WeakSunflower`.

articles.title: Erdős–Szemerédi sunflower conjecture for $k \ge 4$
articles.statement:
The proposition asserts that for every
natural number $k \ge 4$ there is a real number $c$ with $0 < c < 2$ such that, for all
sufficiently large $n$, every $k$-sunflower-free family of subsets of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ has at
most $c^n$ members.

The bound is required only for large $n$ because for $2^n < k$ the family of all subsets of
$\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ is $k$-sunflower-free. The case $k = 3$, proved by Naslund and Sawin, is
omitted.

articles.title: Families containing a sunflower
articles.statement:
Let $n$ and $k$ be natural numbers. A family $F$ of
subsets of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ contains a $k$-sunflower if some subfamily $T \subseteq F$ with
exactly $k$ members satisfies $A \cap B = C \cap D$ for all $A, B, C, D \in T$ with $A \ne B$ and
$C \ne D$, that is, all pairwise intersections of distinct members of $T$ are equal.

articles.title: Sunflower-free families
articles.statement:
Let $n$ and $k$ be natural numbers. A family $F$ of subsets of
$\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ is $k$-sunflower-free if it does not contain a $k$-sunflower.

articles.title: Sunflower
articles.statement:
Let $r \in \mathbb{N}$ and let $S$ be a family of subsets of a type $X$. Then
$S$ is an $r$-sunflower if $S$ has exactly $r$ members (its cardinality is taken to be $0$ when
$S$ is infinite) and any two distinct members $A \ne B$ of $S$ satisfy $A \cap B = \bigcap S$,
the intersection of all members of $S$.

## Sources

- R. Alweiss, S. Lovett, K. Wu, and J. Zhang, *Improved bounds for the sunflower lemma*, Annals of Math 194 (3), 2021, Definition 1.1.

articles.title: Bounded-size set systems
articles.statement:
Let $w \in \mathbb{N}$ and let $\mathcal{F}$ be a family of
subsets of a type $X$. Then $\mathcal{F}$ is a $w$-set system if every member $A \in \mathcal{F}$
has at most $w$ elements, where the size of an infinite set is taken to be $0$.

## Sources

- R. Alweiss, S. Lovett, K. Wu, and J. Zhang, *Improved bounds for the sunflower lemma*, Annals of Math 194 (3), 2021, second sentence of the introduction.

articles.title: Sunflower lower bound
articles.statement:
For natural numbers $r$ and $w$ and a real number $C$, the lower
bound is the real number

$$\left(C\, r^3 \log_{1.9} w \, \log_{1.9}(\log_{1.9} w)\right)^w,$$

where $\log_{1.9} x = \ln x / \ln 1.9$, with the convention $\ln 0 = 0$.

Following the authors, logarithms are taken to base $1.9$; see the paragraph directly after
Theorem 1.4 of Alweiss, Lovett, Wu, and Zhang, *Improved bounds for the sunflower lemma*.

articles.title: Alweiss–Lovett–Wu–Zhang sunflower bound
articles.statement:
Let $C$ be the sunflower constant, a real number
not depending on $r$ or $w$. Let $r \ge 3$ and $w \ge 2$ be natural numbers, let $X$ be a finite
type, and let $\mathcal{F}$ be a $w$-set system of subsets of $X$, that is, every member of
$\mathcal{F}$ has at most $w$ elements. If $\mathcal{F}$ has at least

$$\left(C\, r^3 \log_{1.9} w \, \log_{1.9}(\log_{1.9} w)\right)^w$$

members, then some subfamily $S \subseteq \mathcal{F}$ is an $r$-sunflower: $S$ has exactly $r$
members and any two distinct members of $S$ intersect in $\bigcap S$.

This is Theorem 1.4 (main theorem, sunflowers); logarithms are to base $1.9$, as in the paper.
We require $w \ge 2$, as the paper assumes $\log \log w > 0$.

## Sources

- R. Alweiss, S. Lovett, K. Wu, and J. Zhang, `Improved bounds for the sunflower lemma`, Annals of Math, 194 (3) 2021. Statement taken from https://github.com/ImperialCollegeLondon/AnnalsChallenge. Problem `annals_improved_bounds_sunflower_lemma` of the lean-eval benchmark.

articles.title: Binary code of a subset
articles.statement:
For a natural number $n$ and a subset $A$ of
$\{0, 1, \dots, n-1\}$, the binary code of $A$ is the natural number
$b(A) = \sum_{i \in A} 2^i$.

articles.title: String of a family
articles.statement:
For a family $U$ of subsets of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$, the string
$s(U)$ is the list of the sort keys of the nonempty members of $U$, in increasing order.

articles.title: Canonical family
articles.statement:
A family $U$ of subsets of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ is canonical, the
canonical representative of its isomorphism class, if for every permutation $\sigma$ of
$\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ the string $s(U)$ is lexicographically at most the string $s(\sigma(U))$
of the permuted family $\sigma(U)$.

articles.title: Union-closed family
articles.statement:
A family $U$ of subsets of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ is union-closed if
$A \cup B \in U$ for all $A, B \in U$.

articles.title: Prefixes of a sorted canonical family are canonical
articles.statement:
Let $A_1, \dots, A_k$ be nonempty
subsets of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ with $A_i < A_j$ in the set order whenever $i < j$, and suppose
the family $U = \{\emptyset, A_1, \dots, A_k\}$ is canonical. Then for every $m \le k$, including
$m = 0$, the family $\{\emptyset, A_1, \dots, A_m\}$ is canonical.

Neither union closure nor coverage of the universe is needed.

articles.title: Orderly generation of union-closed families
articles.statement:
Let $n$, $k$ and $m$ be natural numbers with
$1 \le m \le k$, and let $A_1, \dots, A_k$ be nonempty subsets of $\Omega_n = \{0, \dots, n-1\}$
with $A_i < A_j$ in the set order whenever $i < j$. Suppose the family
$U = \{\emptyset, A_1, \dots, A_k\}$ is union-closed, every element of $\Omega_n$ lies in some
member of $U$, $U \ne \{\Omega_n, \emptyset\}$, and $U$ is canonical. Then the prefix family
$\{\emptyset, A_1, \dots, A_m\}$ is canonical.

The hypotheses that $U$ is union-closed, covers $\Omega_n$ and differs from
$\{\Omega_n, \emptyset\}$ are not used in the proof. The string of $U$ lists the sort keys of
$A_1, \dots, A_k$ in order, so the string of the prefix family is a prefix of it, and a
permutation that made the prefix family's string smaller would make the string of $U$ smaller.

## Sources

- Gunnar Brinkmann and Robin Deklerck, "Generation of Union-Closed Sets and Moore Families", Journal of Integer Sequences 21 (2018), Article 18.1.7, Theorem `thm:orderly`, source lines 275–281, <https://cs.uwaterloo.ca/journals/JIS/VOL21/Brinkmann/brink6.tex>.

articles.title: Permuted image of a family
articles.statement:
For a permutation $\sigma$ of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ and a
family $U$ of subsets of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$, the permuted image $\sigma(U)$ is the family
$\{\sigma(A) : A \in U\}$, where $\sigma(A) = \{\sigma(a) : a \in A\}$.

articles.title: Sort key of a subset
articles.statement:
For a subset $A$ of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$, the sort key of $A$ is
the natural number $(n - |A|) \cdot 2^n + b(A)$, where $b(A) = \sum_{i \in A} 2^i$ is the
binary code of $A$.

Since $b(A) < 2^n$, comparing sort keys as numbers agrees with the set order: larger sets come
first, and sets of the same size are ordered by binary code.

articles.title: The sort key encodes the set order
articles.statement:
For all subsets $A$ and $B$ of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$,
$A < B$ in the set order if and only if the sort key of $A$ is less than the sort key of $B$.

articles.title: Set order
articles.statement:
For subsets $A$ and $B$ of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$, $A$ precedes $B$ in the set
order, written $A < B$, if $|A| > |B|$, or $|A| = |B|$ and $b(A) < b(B)$, where
$b(A) = \sum_{i \in A} 2^i$ is the binary code of $A$.

articles.title: Union-free family
articles.statement:
A family $F$ of subsets of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ is union-free if there
are no pairwise distinct $A, B, C \in F$ with $A \cup B = C$.

articles.title: Kleitman's bound for union-free families (Erdős Problem 447)
articles.statement:
For every real
$\varepsilon > 0$ and all sufficiently large $n$, the maximum size of a union-free family of
subsets of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ is at most $(1 + \varepsilon)\binom{n}{\lfloor n/2 \rfloor}$; that
is, it is at most $(1 + o(1))\binom{n}{\lfloor n/2 \rfloor}$.

## Sources

- T. F. Bloom, Erdős Problems, Problem #447, https://www.erdosproblems.com/447 (status PROVED (LEAN)); resolution: D. Kleitman, Collections of subsets containing no two sets and their union, Proceedings of the LA Meeting AMS (1971), 153-155, |F| < (1 + o(1)) C(n, ⌊n/2⌋) (erdosproblems.com/447).

articles.title: Erdős Problem 447, second question
articles.statement:
The assertion that, for every real $\varepsilon > 0$
and all sufficiently large $n$, the maximum size of a union-free family of subsets of
$\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ is at most $(1 + \varepsilon)\binom{n}{\lfloor n/2 \rfloor}$; that is, it is
at most $(1 + o(1))\binom{n}{\lfloor n/2 \rfloor}$.

articles.title: Union-free families have vanishing density (Erdős Problem 447)
articles.statement:
The maximum size of a
union-free family of subsets of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ is $o(2^n)$ as $n \to \infty$.

This follows from Kleitman's bound $(1 + o(1))\binom{n}{\lfloor n/2 \rfloor}$; Erdős reported an
earlier unpublished proof by Sárközy and Szemerédi.

## Sources

- T. F. Bloom, Erdős Problems, Problem #447, https://www.erdosproblems.com/447 (status PROVED (LEAN)); resolution: D. Kleitman, Collections of subsets containing no two sets and their union, Proceedings of the LA Meeting AMS (1971), 153-155, |F| < (1 + o(1)) C(n, ⌊n/2⌋) (erdosproblems.com/447).

articles.title: Erdős Problem 447, first question
articles.statement:
The assertion that the maximum size of a union-free
family of subsets of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ is $o(2^n)$ as $n \to \infty$.

articles.title: Maximum size of a union-free family
articles.statement:
For a natural number $n$, the largest size $|F|$ of a
union-free family $F$ of subsets of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$.

articles.title: Families in which no member is a union of other members
articles.statement:
A family $F$ of finite sets
is union-free over its subfamilies if no member $A \in F$ is the union of a nonempty
subfamily of $F$ that does not contain $A$.

articles.title: Characterization of subhypergraph containment
articles.statement:
Let $H$ be a finite family of finite
subsets of a type $V$ and let $m, k \in \mathbb{N}$. Then $H$ contains a subgraph with $m$
vertices and at least $k$ edges if and only if there is a set $S$ of exactly $m$ elements of $V$
such that at least $k$ members of $H$ are subsets of $S$.

articles.title: Subhypergraph containment
articles.statement:
Let $H$ be a finite family of finite subsets of a type $V$,
viewed as a hypergraph with edge set $H$, and let $m, k \in \mathbb{N}$. Then $H$ contains a
subgraph with $m$ vertices and at least $k$ edges when there is a set $S$ of exactly $m$ elements
of $V$ such that at least $k$ edges of $H$ are subsets of $S$.

articles.title: Characterization of intersecting families
articles.statement:
Let $F$ be a finite family of finite subsets
of a type $\alpha$. Then $F$ is intersecting if and only if for all $A, B \in F$ with $A \neq B$,
the intersection $A \cap B$ is nonempty.

articles.title: Intersecting families
articles.statement:
Let $F$ be a finite family of finite subsets of a type $\alpha$.
Then $F$ is intersecting when every two distinct members meet: for all $A, B \in F$ with
$A \neq B$, the intersection $A \cap B$ is nonempty.

The distinctness is load-bearing: the singleton family $\{\emptyset\}$ is intersecting.

articles.title: Characterization of uniform hypergraphs
articles.statement:
Let $H$ be a finite family of finite subsets of
a type $V$ and let $r \in \mathbb{N}$. Then $H$ is $r$-uniform if and only if every member
$e \in H$ has exactly $r$ elements.

articles.title: Uniform hypergraphs
articles.statement:
Let $H$ be a finite family of finite subsets of a type $V$, viewed as
a hypergraph with edge set $H$, and let $r \in \mathbb{N}$. Then $H$ is $r$-uniform when every
edge $e \in H$ has exactly $r$ elements.

articles.title: Anti-palindromic compositions of 6 with four parts
articles.statement:
There are exactly four
anti-palindromic compositions of $6$ with four parts, and exactly one reduced anti-palindromic
composition of $6$ with four parts.

## Sources

- Daniel F. Checa and José L. Ramírez, *Arndt Compositions: A Generating Functions Approach*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A35, Section 2.1 (each class has `2^{⌊ℓ/2⌋}` members).

articles.title: Anti-palindromic compositions of 6 with three parts
articles.statement:
There are exactly eight
anti-palindromic compositions of $6$ with three parts.

## Sources

- Daniel F. Checa and José L. Ramírez, *Arndt Compositions: A Generating Functions Approach*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A35, Section 2.1 (each class has `2^{⌊ℓ/2⌋}` members).

articles.title: Anti-palindromic compositions
articles.statement:
For natural numbers $n$ and $m$, the number of
anti-palindromic compositions of $n$ with $m$ parts: sequences $(c_1, \dots, c_m)$ of positive
integers with $c_1 + \dots + c_m = n$ and $c_i \ne c_{m+1-i}$ for every $i$ with
$2i \ne m + 1$. That is, each part differs from the part in the mirror position, except the
middle part when $m$ is odd.

## Sources

- Daniel F. Checa and José L. Ramírez, *Arndt Compositions: A Generating Functions Approach*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A35, Section 2.1 (definition of anti-palindromic compositions, after Andrews, Just, and Simay).

articles.title: Alternating sum and recurrence for Arndt compositions
articles.statement:
Let $a(n, m)$ be the number of
Arndt compositions of $n$ with $m$ parts, and write $K = n - m - \lfloor m/2 \rfloor$. For all
$n, m \ge 0$: if $m + \lfloor m/2 \rfloor \le n$, then

$$a(n, m) = \sum_{\ell=0}^{K} \binom{m+\ell-1}{\ell} \binom{n-m-\ell-1}{K-\ell} (-1)^{K-\ell},$$

and otherwise $a(n, m) = 0$. Moreover, for all $n \ge 3$ and $m \ge 2$,
$a(n, m) = a(n-1, m) + a(n-2, m) - a(n-3, m) + a(n-3, m-2)$. The binomial coefficients are the
generalized ones, $\binom{r}{k} = r(r-1)\cdots(r-k+1)/k!$ for an integer $r$, so the upper
index $-1$ is allowed and $\binom{-1}{k} = (-1)^k$.

## Sources

- Daniel F. Checa and José L. Ramírez, *Arndt Compositions: A Generating Functions Approach*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A35, Theorem 2.

articles.title: Positive sum for Arndt compositions
articles.statement:
Let $a(n, m)$ be the number of Arndt compositions of
$n$ with $m$ parts, and write $h = \lfloor m/2 \rfloor$. For all $n \ge 0$ and $m \ge 1$: if
$m + h \le n$, then

$$a(n, m) = \sum_{\ell=0}^{\lfloor (n-m-h)/2 \rfloor} \binom{h+\ell-1}{\ell}
\binom{n-2h-2\ell-1}{\lfloor (m-1)/2 \rfloor},$$

and otherwise $a(n, m) = 0$. Here $\binom{-1}{0} = 1$ (this term occurs for $m = 1$).

The paper states it for all $n, m \ge 0$; at $n = m = 0$ it fails ($a(0, 0) = 1$, while the only
term has lower index $\lfloor -1/2 \rfloor = -1$ and vanishes), so the case $m = 0$ is omitted.

## Sources

- Daniel F. Checa and José L. Ramírez, *Arndt Compositions: A Generating Functions Approach*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A35, Theorem 3.

articles.title: Arndt compositions with a given number of parts as a sum of products
articles.statement:
For all natural
numbers $n$ and $\ell$, the number of Arndt compositions of $n$ with $2\ell$ parts is

$$\sum_{(a_1, \dots, a_\ell)} \prod_{i=1}^{\ell} \left\lfloor \frac{a_i - 1}{2} \right\rfloor,$$

the sum running over the $\ell$-tuples of natural numbers with $a_1 + \dots + a_\ell = n$ and
every $a_i \ge 3$; and the number of Arndt compositions of $n$ with $2\ell + 1$ parts is the same
sum of products $\prod_{i=1}^{\ell} \lfloor (a_i - 1)/2 \rfloor$, now running over the
$(\ell + 1)$-tuples $(a_1, \dots, a_{\ell+1})$ of natural numbers with
$a_1 + \dots + a_{\ell+1} = n$, $a_1, \dots, a_\ell \ge 3$ and $a_{\ell+1} \ge 1$.

## Sources

- Mohammed L. Nadji, Moussa Ahmia, Daniel F. Checa, and José L. Ramírez, *Arndt Compositions with Restricted Parts, Palindromes, and Colored Variants*, Journal of Integer Sequences 28 (2025), Article 25.3.6, Theorem 10 (`jis-2025-25.3.6-thm-10`).

articles.title: Holonomic recurrence for Arndt compositions
articles.statement:
Let $a(n, m)$ be the number of Arndt
compositions of $n$ with $m$ parts. For all $n, m \ge 0$,

$$(m - n - 2 + \lfloor m/2 \rfloor)\, a(n+2, m) + (m - \lfloor m/2 \rfloor)\, a(n+1, m) +
n\, a(n, m) = 0.$$

## Sources

- Daniel F. Checa and José L. Ramírez, *Arndt Compositions: A Generating Functions Approach*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A35, Theorem 4.

articles.title: Asymptotics of Arndt compositions with a fixed number of parts
articles.statement:
Let $a(n, m)$ be the
number of Arndt compositions of $n$ with $m$ parts. For every fixed integer $m \ge 1$,

$$a(n, m) \sim \frac{n^{m-1}}{2^{\lfloor m/2 \rfloor} (m-1)!} \quad (n \to \infty).$$

## Sources

- Daniel F. Checa and José L. Ramírez, *Arndt Compositions: A Generating Functions Approach*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A35, Corollary 1.

articles.title: Arndt compositions of 6 with four parts
articles.statement:
There is exactly one Arndt composition of $6$
with four parts.

It is $(2, 1, 2, 1)$.

## Sources

- D. F. Checa and J. L. Ramírez, *Arndt compositions: a generating functions approach*, arXiv:2311.15388, Section 1 (list of the Arndt compositions of `6`).

articles.title: Arndt compositions of 6 with three parts
articles.statement:
There are exactly $4$ Arndt compositions of $6$
with three parts.

They are $(4, 1, 1)$, $(3, 2, 1)$, $(3, 1, 2)$ and $(2, 1, 3)$.

## Sources

- D. F. Checa and J. L. Ramírez, *Arndt compositions: a generating functions approach*, arXiv:2311.15388, Section 1 (list of the Arndt compositions of `6`).

articles.title: Arndt compositions of 6 with two parts
articles.statement:
There are exactly $2$ Arndt compositions of $6$
with two parts.

They are $(5, 1)$ and $(4, 2)$.

## Sources

- D. F. Checa and J. L. Ramírez, *Arndt compositions: a generating functions approach*, arXiv:2311.15388, Section 1 (list of the Arndt compositions of `6`).

articles.title: Number of Arndt compositions with parts in a set
articles.statement:
For a set $S$ of natural numbers and
natural numbers $n$ and $k$, $a_S(n, k)$ is the number of $k$-tuples $(c_1, \dots, c_k)$ of
positive integers such that $c_1 + \dots + c_k = n$, every $c_i$ lies in $S$, and
$c_{2i-1} > c_{2i}$ for every $i$ with $2i \le k$. These tuples are the Arndt compositions of
$n$ with $k$ parts in $S$.

## Sources

- Mohammed L. Nadji, Moussa Ahmia, Daniel F. Checa, and José L. Ramírez, *Arndt Compositions with Restricted Parts, Palindromes, and Colored Variants*, Journal of Integer Sequences 28 (2025), Article 25.3.6, Section 1 (definition of Arndt compositions, after D. F. Checa and J. L. Ramírez, arXiv:2311.15388, Section 1).

articles.title: Expected number of parts of an Arndt composition
articles.statement:
Let $a(n, m)$ be the number of Arndt
compositions of $n$ with $m$ parts, and $F_n$ the $n$-th Fibonacci number ($F_0 = 0$, $F_1 = 1$).
Then

$$\frac{1}{F_n} \sum_{m=0}^{n} m\, a(n, m) \sim \left(\frac{3}{\sqrt 5} - 1\right) n
\quad (n \to \infty).$$

Since there are $F_n$ Arndt compositions of $n$ for $n \ge 1$, the left side is the expected
number of parts of a uniformly random Arndt composition of $n$.

## Sources

- Daniel F. Checa and José L. Ramírez, *Arndt Compositions: A Generating Functions Approach*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A35, Theorem 5.

articles.title: Arndt compositions are counted by Fibonacci numbers
articles.statement:
Let $a(n, m)$ be the number of Arndt
compositions of $n$ with $m$ parts, let $a(n) = \sum_{m=0}^{n} a(n, m)$ be the number of all
Arndt compositions of $n$, and let $F_n$ be the $n$-th Fibonacci number ($F_0 = 0$, $F_1 = 1$).
Then, in $\mathbb{Z}[[x]]$,

$$\Big(\sum_{n \ge 0} a(n) x^n\Big)(1 - x - x^2) = 1 - x^2,$$

and $a(n) = F_n$ for every $n \ge 1$.

## Sources

- Daniel F. Checa and José L. Ramírez, *Arndt Compositions: A Generating Functions Approach*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A35, Corollary 2.

articles.title: The Arndt generating function as a bivariate count series
articles.statement:
For a set $S$ of natural
numbers, let $a_S(n, m)$ be the number of Arndt compositions of $n$ with $m$ parts, all parts in
$S$. Then the Arndt generating function $A_S(x, y)$ equals the bivariate generating function
$\sum_{n \ge 0} \sum_{m=0}^{n} a_S(n, m) x^n y^m$ in $\mathbb{Z}[y][[x]]$.

## Sources

- Daniel F. Checa and José L. Ramírez, *Arndt Compositions: A Generating Functions Approach*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A35, Section 2 (definition of `A(x, y)`).

articles.title: Generating functions of Arndt compositions with even parts and with odd parts
articles.statement:
Let
$A_E(x, y)$ and $A_O(x, y)$ be the formal power series in $x$ over $\mathbb{Z}[y]$ whose
coefficient of $x^n y^k$ is the number of Arndt compositions of $n$ with $k$ parts, all even,
respectively all odd. Then

$$A_E(x, y) \left(1 - x^2 - x^4 + x^6 (1 - y^2)\right) = (1 - x^4)\left(1 - x^2 (1 - y)\right)$$

and

$$A_O(x, y) \left(1 - x^2 + x^6 - x^4 (1 + y^2)\right) = (1 - x^4)(1 - x^2 + x y).$$

## Sources

- Mohammed L. Nadji, Moussa Ahmia, Daniel F. Checa, and José L. Ramírez, *Arndt Compositions with Restricted Parts, Palindromes, and Colored Variants*, Journal of Integer Sequences 28 (2025), Article 25.3.6, Corollary 7 (`jis-2025-25.3.6-cor-7`).

articles.title: Generating function of Arndt compositions with bounded smallest part
articles.statement:
For a natural
number $\ell \ge 1$, let $B(x, y; \ell)$ be the formal power series in $x$ over $\mathbb{Z}[y]$
whose coefficient of $x^n y^k$ is the number of Arndt compositions of $n$ with $k$ parts, all at
least $\ell$. Then

$$B(x, y; \ell) \left(1 - x - x^2 + x^3 - x^{2\ell+1} y^2\right) = (1 - x^2)(1 - x + x^\ell y).$$

## Sources

- Mohammed L. Nadji, Moussa Ahmia, Daniel F. Checa, and José L. Ramírez, *Arndt Compositions with Restricted Parts, Palindromes, and Colored Variants*, Journal of Integer Sequences 28 (2025), Article 25.3.6, Corollary 6 (`jis-2025-25.3.6-cor-6`).

articles.title: Generating function of Arndt compositions with bounded largest part
articles.statement:
For a natural number
$\ell$, let $A(x, y; \ell)$ be the formal power series in $x$ over $\mathbb{Z}[y]$ whose
coefficient of $x^n y^k$ is the number of Arndt compositions of $n$ with $k$ parts, all at most
$\ell$, and let

$$D_\ell(x, y) = 1 - x^{2+2\ell} y^2 + x^{2+\ell} (1 + x) y^2 - x (1 + x + x^2 (y^2 - 1)).$$

Then

$$A(x, y; \ell) \, D_\ell(x, y) = (1 - x^2)\left(1 - x + x (1 - x^\ell) y\right).$$

The paper assumes $\ell \ge 2$; the identity also holds for $\ell = 0, 1$.

## Sources

- Mohammed L. Nadji, Moussa Ahmia, Daniel F. Checa, and José L. Ramírez, *Arndt Compositions with Restricted Parts, Palindromes, and Colored Variants*, Journal of Integer Sequences 28 (2025), Article 25.3.6, Corollary 5 (`jis-2025-25.3.6-cor-5`).

articles.title: Pair decomposition of the Arndt generating function
articles.statement:
Let $S$ be a set of positive
integers and let $A_S(x, y)$ be the generating function of Arndt compositions with parts in $S$:
the formal power series in $x$ over $\mathbb{Z}[y]$ whose coefficient of $x^n y^k$ is the number
of Arndt compositions of $n$ with $k$ parts, all in $S$. Put $P_S(x) = \sum_{i \in S} x^i$ and
$Q_S(x) = \sum_{i, j \in S,\ j < i} x^{i+j}$. Then

$$A_S(x, y) \, (1 - y^2 Q_S(x)) = 1 + y P_S(x).$$

Equivalently, $A_S(x, y) = (1 + y P_S(x)) \sum_{m \ge 0} Q_S(x)^m y^{2m}$.

## Sources

- Mohammed L. Nadji, Moussa Ahmia, Daniel F. Checa, and José L. Ramírez, *Arndt Compositions with Restricted Parts, Palindromes, and Colored Variants*, Journal of Integer Sequences 28 (2025), Article 25.3.6, Theorem 1 (`jis-2025-25.3.6-thm-1`).

articles.title: Generating function of all Arndt compositions
articles.statement:
Let $A(x, y)$ be the formal power series
in $x$ over $\mathbb{Z}[y]$ whose coefficient of $x^n y^k$ is the number of Arndt compositions of
$n$ with $k$ parts. Then

$$A(x, y) \left((1 - x)(1 - x^2) - y^2 x^3\right) = (1 - x + xy)(1 - x^2).$$

Equivalently, $A(x, y) = (1 + xy/(1 - x)) \sum_{m \ge 0} y^{2m} x^{3m} / (x; x)_2^m$ with
$(x; x)_2 = (1 - x)(1 - x^2)$.

## Sources

- Mohammed L. Nadji, Moussa Ahmia, Daniel F. Checa, and José L. Ramírez, *Arndt Compositions with Restricted Parts, Palindromes, and Colored Variants*, Journal of Integer Sequences 28 (2025), Article 25.3.6, Theorem 9 (`jis-2025-25.3.6-thm-9`).

articles.title: Generating function of Arndt compositions with parts in a set
articles.statement:
An Arndt composition is a
finite sequence $(\sigma_1, \dots, \sigma_k)$ of positive integers such that
$\sigma_{2i-1} > \sigma_{2i}$ for every $i$ with $2i \le k$. For a set $S$ of natural numbers, let
$a_S(n, k)$ be the number of Arndt compositions of $n$ with $k$ parts, all in $S$. The bivariate
generating function of these compositions, by weight ($x$) and number of parts ($y$), is the power
series $A_S(x, y) = \sum_{n \ge 0} \left(\sum_{k=0}^{n} a_S(n, k)\, y^k\right) x^n$ in
$\mathbb{Z}[y][[x]]$.

## Sources

- Mohammed L. Nadji, Moussa Ahmia, Daniel F. Checa, and José L. Ramírez, *Arndt Compositions with Restricted Parts, Palindromes, and Colored Variants*, Journal of Integer Sequences 28 (2025), Article 25.3.6, Section 2.

articles.title: Arndt compositions with last part at most or at least $k$
articles.statement:
Let $F_n$ be the $n$-th
Fibonacci number ($F_0 = 0$, $F_1 = 1$) and $b(n, j)$ the number of Arndt compositions of $n$
with last part $j$. For all integers $k \ge 1$ and $n \ge 2k + 2$, the number of Arndt
compositions of $n$ with last part at most $k$ is
$\sum_{j=1}^{k} b(n, j) = F_n - F_{n-k-1} - F_{n-2k-2}$, and the number with last part at least
$k$ is $\sum_{j=k}^{n} b(n, j) = F_{n-k} + F_{n-2k}$.

The paper prints the second count as $F_{n-k} - F_{n-2k}$, which is false: for $k = 1$ and
$n = 4$ all $F_4 = 3$ Arndt compositions of $4$ have last part at least $1$, while
$F_3 - F_2 = 1$. The sign $+$ is the one the paper's own consequence uses ($F_{n-2} + F_{n-4}$
compositions with last part greater than $1$), and it is what subtracting the number with last
part at most $k - 1$ from $F_n$ gives.

## Sources

- Daniel F. Checa and José L. Ramírez, *Arndt Compositions: A Generating Functions Approach*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A35, Corollary 4.

articles.title: Closed formula for Arndt compositions by last part
articles.statement:
Let $F_r$ be the $r$-th Fibonacci
number ($F_0 = 0$, $F_1 = 1$) and $b(n, m)$ the number of Arndt compositions of $n$ with last
part $m$. Define $t_1, t_2 : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ by $t_1(0) = 1$, $t_1(1) = 0$,
$t_1(r) = F_{r-2}$ and $t_2(0) = 0$, $t_2(1) = 1$, $t_2(r) = F_{r-1}$ for $r \ge 2$. Then for all
integers $n \ge 1$ and $m \ge 1$: $b(n, m) = 0$ if $n < m$, $b(n, m) = t_1(n - m)$ if
$m \le n < 2m$, and $b(n, m) = t_1(n - m) + t_2(n - 2m)$ if $n \ge 2m$.

The paper leaves the range of $m$ implicit; at $m = 0$ the printed formula fails ($b(1, 0) = 0$,
while the formula gives $t_1(1) + t_2(1) = 1$), so $m \ge 1$ is assumed.

## Sources

- Daniel F. Checa and José L. Ramírez, *Arndt Compositions: A Generating Functions Approach*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A35, Theorem 9.

articles.title: Asymptotics of Arndt compositions with a fixed last part
articles.statement:
Let $b(n, m)$ be the number of
Arndt compositions of $n$ with last part $m$, and let $\varphi$ be the golden ratio. For every
fixed integer $m \ge 1$,
$b(n, m) \sim \frac{\varphi^{n-m-2}}{\sqrt{5}} \left(1 + \frac{1}{\varphi^{m-1}}\right)$ as
$n \to \infty$.

## Sources

- Daniel F. Checa and José L. Ramírez, *Arndt Compositions: A Generating Functions Approach*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A35, Theorem 10.

articles.title: Arndt compositions of 6 by last part
articles.statement:
Let $b(n, j)$ be the number of Arndt compositions
of $n$ with last part $j$. Then $b(6, 1) = 4$, $b(6, 2) = 2$, $b(6, 3) = 1$ and $b(6, 6) = 1$.

## Sources

- Daniel F. Checa and José L. Ramírez, *Arndt Compositions: A Generating Functions Approach*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A35, Section 3, Table 2.

articles.title: Arndt compositions by last part
articles.statement:
An Arndt composition of $n$ is a composition
$(\sigma_1, \ldots, \sigma_\ell)$ of $n$ into positive parts such that $\sigma_{2i-1} > \sigma_{2i}$
for every $i$ with $2i \le \ell$. For natural numbers $n$ and $j$, $b(n, j)$ is the number of
Arndt compositions of $n$, with any number of parts, whose last part is $j$. The empty
composition of $0$ counts as having last part $0$, so $b(0, 0) = 1$ and $b(0, j) = 0$ for
$j \ge 1$.

## Sources

- Daniel F. Checa and José L. Ramírez, *Arndt Compositions: A Generating Functions Approach*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A35, Section 3 (definition of `b(n, m)` and Table 2).

articles.title: The auxiliary series $\alpha$ for down/up compositions
articles.statement:
In $\mathbb{Q}[[x, y, z]]$ write
$(a; x)_m = \prod_{j=0}^{m-1} (1 - a x^j)$. For a power series $w$ in $\mathbb{Q}[[x, y, z]]$, the
series $\alpha(x, y, w)$ is the coefficientwise convergent sum
$\alpha(x, y, w) = \sum_{n \ge 0} \frac{(-1)^n x^{n^2+n} y^{2n} w^n}{(xw; x)_{2n}}$.

The paper uses it with $w = z$ and with $w = x$.

## Sources

- Mohammed L. Nadji, Moussa Ahmia, Daniel F. Checa, and José L. Ramírez, *Arndt Compositions with Restricted Parts, Palindromes, and Colored Variants*, Journal of Integer Sequences 28 (2025), Article 25.3.6, Theorem 12, equation (5).

articles.title: The auxiliary series $\beta$ for down/up compositions
articles.statement:
In $\mathbb{Q}[[x, y, z]]$ write
$(a; x)_m = \prod_{j=0}^{m-1} (1 - a x^j)$. For a power series $w$ in $\mathbb{Q}[[x, y, z]]$, the
series $\beta(x, y, w)$ is the coefficientwise convergent sum
$\beta(x, y, w) = \sum_{n \ge 1} \frac{(-1)^{n+1} x^{n^2+n} y^{2n} w^n}{(1 - x)(xw; x)_{2n-1}}$.

The paper uses it with $w = z$ and with $w = x$.

## Sources

- Mohammed L. Nadji, Moussa Ahmia, Daniel F. Checa, and José L. Ramírez, *Arndt Compositions with Restricted Parts, Palindromes, and Colored Variants*, Journal of Integer Sequences 28 (2025), Article 25.3.6, Theorem 12, equation (5).

articles.title: Values of the map $U$
articles.statement:
The map $U$ sends $(2, 3)$ to $(1, 1, 1, 2)$, $(1, 4)$ to
$(1, 4)$, $(3, 2)$ to $(5)$, $(1, 1, 1, 2)$ to $(2, 1, 2)$ and $(1, 3, 1)$ to $(4, 1)$.

## Sources

- Brian Hopkins and Aram Tangboonduangjit, *Arndt and De Morgan Compositions*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A64, Table 3.

articles.title: Compositions fixed by $U$ and their Padovan count
articles.statement:
A composition $(c_1, \dots, c_m)$ of
$n$ is fixed by the map $U$ if and only if $c_i = 1$ for every odd $i$ and $c_i$ is even for
every even $i$. Let $c_U(n)$ be the number of compositions of $n$ fixed by $U$. Then
$c_U(n) = c_U(n - 2) + c_U(n - 3)$ for every $n \ge 4$, $c_U(1) = 1$, $c_U(2) = 0$,
$c_U(3) = 1$, and $c_U(n) = P_{n-1}$ for every $n \ge 1$, where $P$ is the shifted Padovan
sequence, given by $P_0 = 1$, $P_1 = 0$, $P_2 = 1$ and $P_{j+3} = P_{j+1} + P_j$.

## Sources

- Brian Hopkins and Aram Tangboonduangjit, *Arndt and De Morgan Compositions*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A64, Proposition 1.

articles.title: The map $U$ on lists
articles.statement:
The map $U$ sends a list $(c_1, c_2, \dots)$ of natural
numbers to the concatenation of the images of its consecutive pairs $(c_1, c_2)$, $(c_3, c_4)$,
and so on, where $1^j$ denotes $j$ parts equal to $1$: a pair $(a, b)$ with $b < a$ goes to
$(1^{a - b - 1}, 2b + 1)$; a pair $(a, b)$ with $b \ge a$ goes to $(1^{a + b - 2k}, 2k)$, where
$k = \lfloor (b - a)/2 \rfloor + 1$ is the integer $k \ge 1$ with $2k - 2 \le b - a < 2k$; and a
final unpaired entry $a$ goes to $1^a$. The empty list goes to itself. The exponent
$a + b - 2k$ is read as $0$ when it is negative, which happens only when $a = 0$.

## Sources

- Brian Hopkins and Aram Tangboonduangjit, *Arndt and De Morgan Compositions*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A64, Theorem 2 and its proof.

articles.title: Values of the map $V$
articles.statement:
The map $V$ sends $(2, 3)$ to $(1, 1, 3)$, $(1, 4)$ to $(5)$,
$(4, 1)$ to $(1, 1, 1, 2)$, $(1, 3, 1)$ to $(1, 3, 1)$ and $(2, 2, 1)$ to $(4, 1)$.

## Sources

- Brian Hopkins and Aram Tangboonduangjit, *Arndt and De Morgan Compositions*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A64, Table 6.

articles.title: Compositions fixed by $V$ and their Fibonacci count
articles.statement:
A composition $(c_1, \dots, c_m)$
of $n$ is fixed by the map $V$ if and only if $c_i = 1$ for every odd $i$ and $c_i$ is odd and
at least $3$ for every even $i$. Let $c_V(n)$ be the number of compositions of $n$ fixed by $V$.
Then $c_V(n) = c_V(n - 2) + c_V(n - 4)$ for every $n \ge 5$, $c_V(1) = c_V(4) = 1$,
$c_V(2) = c_V(3) = 0$, and $c_V(2j) = c_V(2j + 1) = F_{j-1}$ for every $j \ge 1$, where $F$ is
the Fibonacci sequence with $F_0 = 0$ and $F_1 = 1$.

## Sources

- Brian Hopkins and Aram Tangboonduangjit, *Arndt and De Morgan Compositions*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A64, Proposition 2.

articles.title: The map $V$ on lists
articles.statement:
The map $V$ sends a list $(c_1, c_2, \dots)$ of natural
numbers to the concatenation of the images of its consecutive pairs $(c_1, c_2)$, $(c_3, c_4)$,
and so on, where $1^j$ denotes $j$ parts equal to $1$: a pair $(a, b)$ with $b \le a$ goes to
$(1^{a - b}, 2b)$; a pair $(a, b)$ with $b > a$ goes to $(1^{a + b - 2k - 1}, 2k + 1)$, where
$k = \lfloor (b - a + 1)/2 \rfloor$ is the integer $k \ge 1$ with $2k - 1 \le b - a < 2k + 1$;
and a final unpaired entry $a$ goes to $1^a$. The empty list goes to itself. The exponent
$a + b - 2k - 1$ is read as $0$ when it is negative, which happens only when $a = 0$.

## Sources

- Brian Hopkins and Aram Tangboonduangjit, *Arndt and De Morgan Compositions*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A64, Theorem 3 and its proof.

articles.title: Generating function of anti-palindromic compositions
articles.statement:
Let $ap(n, m)$ be the number of
anti-palindromic compositions of $n$ with $m$ parts, and let
$Ap(x, y) = \sum_{n \ge 0} \sum_{m=0}^{n} ap(n, m)\, x^n y^m \in \mathbb{Z}[y][[x]]$. Then
$Ap(x, y)\,(1 - x - x^2 + x^3 - 2x^3y^2) = 1 - x - x^2 + x^3 + xy - x^3y$, that is,
$Ap(x, y) = (1 - x - x^2 + x^3 + xy - x^3y)/(1 - x - x^2 + x^3 - 2x^3y^2)$.

## Sources

- Daniel F. Checa and José L. Ramírez, *Arndt Compositions: A Generating Functions Approach*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A35, Theorem 6.

articles.title: Generating function of Arndt compositions by last part
articles.statement:
Let $b(n, m)$ be the number of
Arndt compositions of $n$ with last part $m$, where the empty composition of $0$ counts as
having last part $0$ (so $b(0, 0) = 1$), and let
$B(x, y) = \sum_{n \ge 0} \sum_{m=0}^{n} b(n, m)\, x^n y^m \in \mathbb{Z}[y][[x]]$. Then
$B(x, y)\,(1 - x - x^2)(1 - xy)(1 - x^2y) =
1 - x - x^2 - x^2y + 2x^3y + 2x^4y - x^5y - x^4y^2$.

## Sources

- Daniel F. Checa and José L. Ramírez, *Arndt Compositions: A Generating Functions Approach*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A35, Theorem 8.

articles.title: Generating function of block Arndt compositions
articles.statement:
Let $k \ge 1$, let $a^{(k)}(n, m)$ be
the number of $k$-block Arndt compositions of $n$ with $m$ parts, and let
$A^{(k)}(x, y) = \sum_{n \ge 0} \sum_{m=0}^{n} a^{(k)}(n, m)\, x^n y^m \in \mathbb{Z}[y][[x]]$.
Then
$A^{(k)}(x, y) \bigl(\prod_{\ell=1}^{k} (1 - x^\ell) - x^{\binom{k+1}{2}} y^k\bigr) =
\sum_{j=0}^{k-1} x^{\binom{j+1}{2}} y^j \prod_{\ell=j+1}^{k} (1 - x^\ell)$.
Equivalently, with $J_j(x, y) = x^{\binom{j+1}{2}} y^j \prod_{\ell=1}^{j} (1 - x^\ell)^{-1}$,
$A^{(k)}(x, y) = \bigl(\sum_{j=0}^{k-1} J_j(x, y)\bigr) / (1 - J_k(x, y))$.

## Sources

- Daniel F. Checa and José L. Ramírez, *Arndt Compositions: A Generating Functions Approach*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A35, Theorem 12.

articles.title: Generating function of $k$-Arndt compositions for negative $k$
articles.statement:
Let $k' \ge 1$ and
$k = -k'$, let $a_k(n, m)$ be the number of $k$-Arndt compositions of $n$ with $m$ parts, and
let $A_k(x, y) = \sum_{n \ge 0} \sum_{m=0}^{n} a_k(n, m)\, x^n y^m \in \mathbb{Z}[y][[x]]$. Then
