$F_B(x) = (2 - 3x - 3x^2 + (x - 2)\sqrt{1 - 2x - 3x^2}) / (2x^2(1 + x))$ with the denominator
cleared, $s$ standing for $\sqrt{1 - 2x - 3x^2}$.

## Sources

- Toufik Mansour, *Inversion Sequences Avoiding a Set of Length-3 Patterns*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A76, Theorem 22.

articles.title: Generating function of inversion sequences avoiding a set of patterns
articles.statement:
For a set $B$ of
length-3 patterns, $F_B(x) = \sum_{n \ge 1} |I_n(B)| x^n$ is the formal power series in
$\mathbb{Q}[[x]]$ with constant coefficient $0$ whose coefficient of $x^n$, for $n \ge 1$, is the
number $|I_n(B)|$ of inversion sequences of length $n$ that avoid every pattern in $B$.

## Sources

- Toufik Mansour, *Inversion Sequences Avoiding a Set of Length-3 Patterns*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A76, Section 2.

articles.title: Containment of a length-3 pattern
articles.statement:
A sequence $e = e_0 e_1 \cdots e_{n-1}$ of natural
numbers contains the length-3 pattern $p = p_0 p_1 p_2$ of natural numbers when there are
positions $i_0 < i_1 < i_2$ in $\{0, \dots, n - 1\}$ such that, for all $a, b \in \{0, 1, 2\}$,
$e_{i_a} < e_{i_b}$ if and only if $p_a < p_b$; that is, the subsequence $e_{i_0} e_{i_1} e_{i_2}$
is order-isomorphic to $p$.

## Sources

- Toufik Mansour, *Inversion Sequences Avoiding a Set of Length-3 Patterns*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A76, Introduction.

articles.title: Reducible sets of length-3 patterns for inversion sequences
I-Wilf equivalence of $\{000, 010, 100, 101, 120\}$ and $\{000, 010, 100, 110, 120\}$
articles.statement:
Write length-3 patterns as digit strings ($101$ is the pattern $(1, 0, 1)$) and let $|I_n(B)|$ be
the number of inversion sequences of length $n$ that avoid every pattern in the set $B$. Then for
every $n \ge 0$, $|I_n(\{000, 010, 100, 101, 120\})| = |I_n(\{000, 010, 100, 110, 120\})|$.

## Sources

- Toufik Mansour, *Inversion Sequences Avoiding a Set of Length-3 Patterns*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A76, Theorem 4.

articles.title: Three I-Wilf-equivalent sets of five patterns containing $000$, $010$ and $120$
articles.statement:
Write
length-3 patterns as digit strings ($101$ is the pattern $(1, 0, 1)$) and let $|I_n(B)|$ be the
number of inversion sequences of length $n$ that avoid every pattern in the set $B$. For
$B_1 = \{000, 010, 101, 120, 201\}$, $B_2 = \{000, 010, 101, 120, 210\}$ and
$B_3 = \{000, 010, 110, 120, 210\}$, and for every $n \ge 0$,
$|I_n(B_1)| = |I_n(B_2)| = |I_n(B_3)|$.

## Sources

- Toufik Mansour, *Inversion Sequences Avoiding a Set of Length-3 Patterns*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A76, Theorem 5.

articles.title: Five I-Wilf-equivalent sets of six patterns containing $000$, $010$ and $120$
articles.statement:
Write
length-3 patterns as digit strings ($101$ is the pattern $(1, 0, 1)$) and let $|I_n(B)|$ be the
number of inversion sequences of length $n$ that avoid every pattern in the set $B$. For a pattern
$\tau$ let $A_\tau = \{000, 010, 100, 101, 120, \tau\}$ and $B_\tau = \{000, 010, 100, 110, 120,
\tau\}$, and let $C = \{000, 010, 101, 110, 120, 201\}$. Then for every $n \ge 0$,
$|I_n(A_{201})| = |I_n(A_{210})| = |I_n(B_{201})| = |I_n(B_{210})| = |I_n(C)|$.

## Sources

- Toufik Mansour, *Inversion Sequences Avoiding a Set of Length-3 Patterns*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A76, Theorem 13.

articles.title: Two I-Wilf equivalences exchanging $201$ and $210$ in five-pattern sets
articles.statement:
Write
length-3 patterns as digit strings ($101$ is the pattern $(1, 0, 1)$) and let $|I_n(B)|$ be the
number of inversion sequences of length $n$ that avoid every pattern in the set $B$. For a pattern
$\tau$ let $A_\tau = \{000, 100, 101, 120, \tau\}$ and $B_\tau = \{000, 100, 110, 120, \tau\}$.
Then for every $n \ge 0$, $|I_n(A_{201})| = |I_n(A_{210})|$ and $|I_n(B_{201})| = |I_n(B_{210})|$.

## Sources

- Toufik Mansour, *Inversion Sequences Avoiding a Set of Length-3 Patterns*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A76, Theorem 8.

articles.title: Three I-Wilf-equivalent sets of five patterns containing $000$, $102$ and $120$
articles.statement:
Write
length-3 patterns as digit strings ($101$ is the pattern $(1, 0, 1)$) and let $|I_n(B)|$ be the
number of inversion sequences of length $n$ that avoid every pattern in the set $B$. For
$B_1 = \{000, 101, 102, 120, 201\}$, $B_2 = \{000, 101, 102, 120, 210\}$ and
$B_3 = \{000, 102, 110, 120, 210\}$, and for every $n \ge 0$,
$|I_n(B_1)| = |I_n(B_2)| = |I_n(B_3)|$.

## Sources

- Toufik Mansour, *Inversion Sequences Avoiding a Set of Length-3 Patterns*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A76, Theorem 7.

articles.title: Exchanging $201$ and $210$ in $\{010, 100, 101, 102, 120, 201\}$
articles.statement:
Write length-3
patterns as digit strings ($101$ is the pattern $(1, 0, 1)$) and let $|I_n(B)|$ be the number of
inversion sequences of length $n$ that avoid every pattern in the set $B$. For a pattern $\tau$
let $A_\tau = \{010, 100, 101, 102, 120, \tau\}$. Then for every $n \ge 0$,
$|I_n(A_{201})| = |I_n(A_{210})|$.

The source further claims $|I_n(A_{210})| = |I_n(B)| = |I_n(C)|$ for all $n$, with
$B = \{010, 100, 110, 102, 120, 201\}$ and $C = \{010, 101, 110, 102, 120, 210\}$; these claims are
false as printed ($|I_7| = 538, 537, 539$ for $A_{210}$, $B$, $C$) and are omitted.

- Toufik Mansour, *Inversion Sequences Avoiding a Set of Length-3 Patterns*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A76, Theorem 15.

articles.title: I-Wilf equivalence of $\{010, 100, 101, 120, 201\}$ and $\{010, 100, 101, 120, 210\}$
articles.statement:
Write length-3 patterns as digit strings ($101$ is the pattern $(1, 0, 1)$) and let $|I_n(B)|$ be
the number of inversion sequences of length $n$ that avoid every pattern in the set $B$. Then for
every $n \ge 0$, $|I_n(\{010, 100, 101, 120, 201\})| = |I_n(\{010, 100, 101, 120, 210\})|$.

- Toufik Mansour, *Inversion Sequences Avoiding a Set of Length-3 Patterns*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A76, Theorem 11.

articles.title: I-Wilf equivalences among five-pattern sets containing $010$, $102$ and $120$
articles.statement:
Write
length-3 patterns as digit strings ($101$ is the pattern $(1, 0, 1)$) and let $|I_n(B)|$ be the
number of inversion sequences of length $n$ that avoid every pattern in the set $B$. For a pattern
$\tau$ let $A_\tau = \{010, \tau, 102, 120, 201\}$ and $A'_\tau = \{010, \tau, 102, 120, 210\}$,
and let $B = \{010, 101, 102, 120, 201\}$. Then for every $n \ge 0$,
$|I_n(A_{100})| = |I_n(A_{110})|$ and
$|I_n(A'_{100})| = |I_n(A'_{101})| = |I_n(A'_{110})| = |I_n(B)|$.

- Toufik Mansour, *Inversion Sequences Avoiding a Set of Length-3 Patterns*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A76, Theorem 9.

articles.title: I-Wilf-equivalence of 101 and 110 alongside 010, 120, 201, 210
articles.statement:
Write a length-3 pattern
as the word of its values, so $101$ is the pattern $(1, 0, 1)$, and for a set $B$ of patterns let
$|I_n(B)|$ be the number of inversion sequences of length $n$ that avoid every pattern in $B$.
For every $n \ge 0$,

$$|I_n(\{010, 101, 120, 201, 210\})| = |I_n(\{010, 110, 120, 201, 210\})|.$$

The paper's Theorem 12 also claims this equality for $\{100, 101, 120, 201, 210\}$ and
$\{100, 110, 120, 201, 210\}$; that claim is false, since for $n = 5$ the two counts are $79$
and $81$.

## Sources

- Toufik Mansour, *Inversion Sequences Avoiding a Set of Length-3 Patterns*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A76, Theorem 12.

articles.title: Three I-Wilf-equivalent six-pattern sets containing 102 and 110
articles.statement:
Write a length-3 pattern
as the word of its values, so $101$ is the pattern $(1, 0, 1)$, and for a set $B$ of patterns let
$|I_n(B)|$ be the number of inversion sequences of length $n$ that avoid every pattern in $B$.
Let $A_\tau = \{011, 101, 102, 110, 120, \tau\}$ and $C = \{011, 021, 102, 110, 201, 210\}$.
Then $|I_n(A_{201})| = |I_n(A_{210})| = |I_n(C)|$ for every $n \ge 0$.

## Sources

- Toufik Mansour, *Inversion Sequences Avoiding a Set of Length-3 Patterns*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A76, Theorem 14.

articles.title: I-Wilf-equivalence of 101 and 110 alongside 102, 120, 210
articles.statement:
Write a length-3 pattern as the
word of its values, so $101$ is the pattern $(1, 0, 1)$, and for a set $S$ of patterns let
$|I_n(S)|$ be the number of inversion sequences of length $n$ that avoid every pattern in $S$.
Let $B_\tau = \{100, \tau, 102, 120, 210\}$ and $C_\tau = \{\tau, 102, 120, 201, 210\}$. Then for
every $n \ge 0$, $|I_n(B_{101})| = |I_n(B_{110})|$ and $|I_n(C_{101})| = |I_n(C_{110})|$.

The paper's Theorem 10 also claims $|I_n(A_{101})| = |I_n(A_{110})|$ for all $n$, where
$A_\tau = \{100, \tau, 102, 120, 201\}$; that claim is false, since for $n = 6$ the two counts
are $206$ and $205$.

- Toufik Mansour, *Inversion Sequences Avoiding a Set of Length-3 Patterns*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A76, Theorem 10.

articles.title: Number of I-Wilf classes of sets of length-3 patterns
articles.statement:
Let $P$ be the set of the thirteen
length-3 patterns $000, 001, 010, 011, 012, 021, 100, 101, 102, 110, 120, 201, 210$, each written
as the word of its values. For $B \subseteq P$ let $|I_n(B)|$ be the number of inversion sequences
of length $n$ that avoid every pattern in $B$, and let $w_d$ be the number of distinct sequences
$(|I_n(B)|)_{n \ge 0}$ as $B$ ranges over the $d$-element subsets of $P$ (the number of
I-Wilf-equivalence classes of such sets). Then $w_5 = 219$, $w_6 = 167$, $w_7 = 105$, $w_8 = 61$,
$w_9 = 35$, $w_{10} = 21$, $w_{11} = 10$, $w_{12} = 4$ and $w_{13} = 1$.

## Sources

- Toufik Mansour, *Inversion Sequences Avoiding a Set of Length-3 Patterns*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A76, Theorem 1.

articles.title: Eight-pattern sets differing in 201 and 210: equivalence and generating function
articles.statement:
Write a
length-3 pattern as the word of its values, so $101$ is the pattern $(1, 0, 1)$. For a set $B$ of
patterns let $|I_n(B)|$ be the number of inversion sequences of length $n$ that avoid every
pattern in $B$, and let $F_B(x) = \sum_{n \ge 1} |I_n(B)| x^n \in \mathbb{Q}[[x]]$. Let
$B_\tau = \{000, 010, 100, 101, 102, 110, 120, \tau\}$. Then $|I_n(B_{201})| = |I_n(B_{210})|$
for every $n \ge 0$, and for every power series $s \in \mathbb{Q}[[x]]$ with constant term $1$
and $s^2 = 1 - 2x - 3x^2$,

$$
2x^3 (1 + x)(x^2 + 2x + 2) F_{B_{201}}(x) =
1 - x^2 - 4x^3 - 7x^4 - 5x^5 - 2x^6 - (1 + x + 2x^2 + 2x^3 + x^4) s.
$$

This is the paper's closed form for $F_{B_{201}}$ with the denominator cleared, where $s$ plays
the role of $\sqrt{1 - 2x - 3x^2}$.

## Sources

- Toufik Mansour, *Inversion Sequences Avoiding a Set of Length-3 Patterns*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A76, Theorem 17.

articles.title: Short sequences contain no length-3 pattern
articles.statement:
If $n < 3$, then no sequence
$e_0 e_1 \cdots e_{n-1}$ of natural numbers contains a length-3 pattern $p$.

## Sources

- Toufik Mansour, *Inversion Sequences Avoiding a Set of Length-3 Patterns*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A76, Introduction.

articles.title: Eight signed-pattern triples with (n + 1)! avoiders (Lemma 8)
articles.statement:
Write a length-2 signed
pattern as $\tau_1\tau_2$, where $00$, $01$ and $10$ record whether $|\tau_1|$ is equal to, smaller
than or larger than $|\tau_2|$ and a bar marks a barred letter, and write $|\bar I_n(B)|$ for the
number of signed inversion sequences of length $n$ avoiding every pattern of a set $B$ of such
patterns. For every $n \ge 0$ and each of the eight sets
$B = \lbrace \bar 1\bar 0, \bar 0\bar 1, \bar 0\bar 0 \rbrace$,

or larger than $|\tau_2|$ and a bar marks a barred letter, and write $|\bar I_n(A)|$ for the
number of signed inversion sequences of length $n$ avoiding every pattern of a set $A$ of such
patterns. For every $n \ge 1$ and each of the three sets

articles.title: Signed inversion sequences of length one
articles.statement:
The signed inversion sequences of length $1$ are
$0$ and $\bar 0$, and neither contains a length-2 signed pattern, so for every finite set $B$ of
length-2 signed patterns the number $|\bar I_1(B)|$ of signed inversion sequences of length $1$
avoiding every pattern of $B$ is $2$.

articles.title: Signed inversion sequences of length zero
articles.statement:
The empty sequence is the only signed inversion
sequence of length $0$, and it contains no pattern, so for every finite set $B$ of length-2 signed
patterns the number $|\bar I_0(B)|$ of signed inversion sequences of length $0$ avoiding every
pattern of $B$ is $1$.

articles.title: Number of signed inversion sequences avoiding a set of patterns
articles.statement:
A signed inversion
sequence of length $n$ is a word $e_1 \cdots e_n$ in which each entry $e_i$ is a natural number
$|e_i| \le i - 1$, either barred or not; that is, $e_i \in \lbrace 0, \bar 0, 1, \bar 1, \dots,
i - 1, \overline{i - 1} \rbrace$. For a finite set $B$ of length-2 signed patterns and $n \ge 0$,
$|\bar I_n(B)|$ is the number of signed inversion sequences of length $n$ that contain no pattern
of $B$.

articles.title: Generating function of signed inversion sequences avoiding a set of patterns
articles.statement:
For a finite
set $B$ of length-2 signed patterns, $F_B(x) = \sum_{n \ge 0} |\bar I_n(B)| x^n$ is the formal
power series with rational coefficients whose coefficient of $x^n$ is the number $|\bar I_n(B)|$
of signed inversion sequences of length $n$ avoiding every pattern of $B$.

articles.title: Containment of a length-2 signed pattern
articles.statement:
Let $e = e_1 \cdots e_n$ be a sequence whose
entries are natural numbers $|e_i|$, each barred or not, and let $\tau_1\tau_2$ be a length-2
signed pattern. Then $e$ contains $\tau_1\tau_2$ if there are positions $i < j$ such that $|e_i|$
is equal to, smaller than or larger than $|e_j|$ exactly as $|\tau_1|$ is equal to, smaller than
or larger than $|\tau_2|$, and $e_i$ and $e_j$ are barred exactly when $\tau_1$ and $\tau_2$ are.

of length-2 signed patterns (a bar marks a barred letter), let $|\bar I_n(B)|$ be the number of
signed inversion sequences of length $n$ avoiding every pattern of $B$, and let
$F_B(x) = \sum_{n \ge 0} |\bar I_n(B)| x^n \in \mathbb{Q}[[x]]$. Let
$B = \{\bar1\bar0, \bar0\bar1, 0\bar1, 01\}$ and $C = \{\bar10, \bar0\bar1, 0\bar1, 01\}$. Then
$|\bar I_n(B)| = |\bar I_n(C)|$ for every $n \ge 0$, and $(1 - 3x + x^2) F_B(x) = 1 - x$, that is,
$F_B(x) = (1 - x)/(1 - 3x + x^2)$.

## Sources

- Toufik Mansour and Amir Safadi, *Signed Inversion Sequences Avoiding a Set of Length-2 Signed Patterns*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A74, Theorem 3 (C38).

articles.title: Signed inversion sequences avoiding $\{\bar1\bar0, \bar0\bar1, 01\}$
articles.statement:
For a set $B$ of
length-2 signed patterns (a bar marks a barred letter), let $|\bar I_n(B)|$ be the number of signed
inversion sequences of length $n$ avoiding every pattern of $B$, and let
$F_B(x) = \sum_{n \ge 0} |\bar I_n(B)| x^n \in \mathbb{Q}[[x]]$. Let
$B = \{\bar1\bar0, \bar0\bar1, 01\}$ and $C = \{\bar10, \bar0\bar1, 01\}$. Then
$|\bar I_n(B)| = |\bar I_n(C)|$ for every $n \ge 0$, and

$$
(1 - 2x)(1 - 3x + x^2)(1 - x)^2 F_B(x) = (1 - 2x)(1 - 3x + x^2)(1 - x)^2 + x(1 - x)^4 +
x(1 - x + x^2)(1 - 3x + x^2),
$$

that is,
$F_B(x) = 1 + \frac{x(1 - x)^2}{(1 - 2x)(1 - 3x + x^2)} + \frac{x(1 - x + x^2)}{(1 - 2x)(1 - x)^2}$.

## Sources

- Toufik Mansour and Amir Safadi, *Signed Inversion Sequences Avoiding a Set of Length-2 Signed Patterns*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A74, Lemma 5.

articles.title: Signed inversion sequences avoiding $\{\bar1\bar0, \bar0\bar1, \bar00, 00\}$
articles.statement:
For a set $B$
of length-2 signed patterns (a bar marks a barred letter), let $|\bar I_n(B)|$ be the number of
signed inversion sequences of length $n$ avoiding every pattern of $B$, and let
$F_B(x) = \sum_{n \ge 0} |\bar I_n(B)| x^n \in \mathbb{Q}[[x]]$. Let
$B_1 = \{\bar1\bar0, \bar0\bar1, \bar00, 00\}$, $B_2 = \{\bar1\bar0, \bar0\bar1, 0\bar0, 00\}$ and
$B_3 = \{\bar10, \bar0\bar1, 0\bar0, 00\}$. Then
$|\bar I_n(B_1)| = |\bar I_n(B_2)| = |\bar I_n(B_3)|$ for every $n \ge 0$, and for every $n \ge 0$
the coefficient of $x^n$ in $F_{B_1}(x)$ equals the coefficient of $x^n$ in

$$
\frac{1}{1 - x} + \frac{1}{1 - x} \sum_{j=1}^{n} \frac{x^j (1 - jx)}{\prod_{i=1}^{j+1} (1 - ix)}.
$$

The terms with $j > n$ are divisible by $x^{n+1}$, so this says
$F_{B_1}(x) = \frac{1}{1 - x}\Bigl(1 + \sum_{j \ge 1} x^j (1 - jx) /
\prod_{i=1}^{j+1} (1 - ix)\Bigr)$.

articles.title: Mansour–Safadi Theorem 12: four Wilf-equivalences of five-pattern sets
articles.statement:
Length-2 signed
patterns are written as in the paper, a bar marking a barred letter, and $B \sim C$ means that
for every $n \ge 0$ the number $|\bar I_n(B)|$ of signed inversion sequences of length $n$
avoiding every pattern of $B$ equals $|\bar I_n(C)|$. Then
$\{\bar1\bar0, \bar0\bar1, \bar00, \bar01, 0\bar0\} \sim
\{\bar1\bar0, \bar0\bar1, \bar0\bar0, \bar01, 0\bar0\}$,
$\{\bar1\bar0, \bar10, \bar0\bar1, \bar00, 0\bar0\} \sim
\{\bar1\bar0, \bar10, \bar0\bar1, \bar0\bar0, 0\bar0\}$,
$\{\bar1\bar0, \bar0\bar1, \bar0\bar0, \bar00, 1\bar0\} \sim
\{\bar1\bar0, \bar0\bar1, \bar00, 0\bar0, 1\bar0\}$ and
$\{\bar1\bar0, \bar10, \bar0\bar1, \bar00, 00\} \sim
\{\bar1\bar0, \bar10, \bar0\bar1, 0\bar0, 00\}$.

The paper prints a third set in the first equivalence,
$\{\bar1\bar0, \bar0\bar1, \bar01, 0\bar0, 1\bar0\}$; it is left out here because it has
$|\bar I_2| = 5$, against $4$ for the first two sets.

articles.title: Length-2 signed pattern
articles.statement:
A length-2 signed pattern is a word $\tau_1\tau_2$ whose
underlying word $|\tau_1||\tau_2|$ is $00$, $01$ or $10$ and each of whose letters may be barred,
for example $\bar10$ or $0\bar1$. It is given by the comparison of $|\tau_1|$ with $|\tau_2|$
(equal for $00$, less for $01$, greater for $10$) together with whether $\tau_1$ is barred and
whether $\tau_2$ is barred.

## Sources

- Toufik Mansour and Amir Safadi, *Signed Inversion Sequences Avoiding a Set of Length-2 Signed Patterns*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A74, Introduction.

articles.statement:

Wilf-equivalence classes among the sets of $k$ length-2 signed patterns, that is, the number of
distinct counting functions $n \mapsto |\bar{I}_n(B)|$ (for $n \ge 0$) over all sets $B$ of exactly

articles.title: Ascent sequences avoiding a set of patterns
articles.statement:
For a finite set $P$ of patterns (words over
$\mathbb{N}$) and $n \in \mathbb{N}$, $A_n(P)$ is the set of ascent sequences of length $n$ that

articles.title: Number of Wilf classes of ascent sequences avoiding four length-3 patterns
articles.statement:
For a set $P$
of patterns, let $A_n(P)$ be the set of ascent sequences of length $n$ avoiding every pattern in
$P$. As $P$ ranges over the $4$-element subsets of the thirteen patterns of length three, the
counting sequences $n \mapsto |A_n(P)|$ take exactly $74$ distinct values. Equivalently, there are

articles.title: The word $00203413$ contains $011$
articles.statement:

articles.title: Pattern containment in words
articles.statement:
A word $w$ over $\mathbb{N}$ contains a pattern $p$ (another
word over $\mathbb{N}$) if $w$ has a subsequence $s$, not necessarily contiguous, of the same
length as $p$ that is order-isomorphic to $p$: for all positions $i$ and $j$, $s_i < s_j$ if and
only if $p_i < p_j$.

## Sources

- David Callan and Toufik Mansour, *Ascent Sequences and Weak Ascent Sequences Avoiding a Quadruple of Length-3 Patterns*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A80, Section 1.

articles.title: Big entries of $00203413$
articles.statement:
In the word $w = 00203413$, with positions numbered from $1$,
the entries $w_3 = 2$ and $w_6 = 4$ are big entries and the entry $w_7 = 1$ is not.

articles.title: Successors of big entries in $W_n$
articles.statement:
Let $W_n$ be the set of weak ascent sequences of length
$n$ avoiding the patterns $011$, $100$, $201$ and $210$, and let $w = w_1 \cdots w_n \in W_n$. If
$2 \le k \le n - 1$ and $w_k$ is a big entry of $w$, then either $w_{k+1}$ is a big entry, or
$w_{k+1} < w_k$ and $w_j$ is a big entry for every $j$ with $k + 2 \le j \le n$.

## Sources

- David Callan and Toufik Mansour, *Ascent Sequences and Weak Ascent Sequences Avoiding a Quadruple of Length-3 Patterns*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A80, Lemma 1.

articles.title: Big entry
articles.statement:
Let $w = w_1 \cdots w_n$ be a word over $\mathbb{N}$ and $2 \le k \le n$. The
entry $w_k$ is a big entry of $w$ if it equals $1$ plus the number of weak ascents of
$w_1 \cdots w_{k-1}$, that is, of positions $j < k - 1$ with $w_j \le w_{j+1}$. In a weak ascent
sequence this is the largest value allowed at position $k$. The entry $w_k$ is referred to by its
zero-based index $i = k - 1$, so the index ranges over $1 \le i < n$.

## Sources

- David Callan and Toufik Mansour, *Ascent Sequences and Weak Ascent Sequences Avoiding a Quadruple of Length-3 Patterns*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A80, Section 4.3 (definition of big entry).

articles.title: The weak ascent sequence $00203413$

articles.title: Weak ascent sequence
articles.statement:
A word $a_1 a_2 \cdots a_n$ over $\mathbb{N}$ is a weak ascent
sequence if either $n = 0$, or $a_1 = 0$ and $a_i \le 1 + \operatorname{wasc}(a_1 \cdots a_{i-1})$
for every $2 \le i \le n$, where $\operatorname{wasc}(u)$ is the number of weak ascents of $u$,
that is, of positions $j$ with $u_j \le u_{j+1}$.

## Sources

- David Callan and Toufik Mansour, *Ascent Sequences and Weak Ascent Sequences Avoiding a Quadruple of Length-3 Patterns*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A80, Section 1.

articles.title: Examples of the last descent top
articles.statement:
Each of the sequences $0010$, $0020$, $0021$ and
$0120$ has its last descent top at position $3$, and the sequence $012$, which has no
descent, has last descent top position $0$.

articles.title: Position of the last descent top
articles.statement:
For a finite sequence $w = w_1 w_2 \cdots w_m$ of
natural numbers, a descent of $w$ is an index $1 \le i < m$ with $w_i > w_{i+1}$, and $w_i$ is
its descent top. The position of the last descent top of $w$ is the largest index $i$ with
$w_i > w_{i+1}$ (positions counted from $1$), and it is $0$ if $w$ has no descent.

## Sources

- David Callan and Toufik Mansour, *Ascent Sequences and Weak Ascent Sequences Avoiding a Quadruple of Length-3 Patterns*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A80, Section 4.3 (definition of `W_{n,k}`).

articles.title: The thirteen patterns of length three
articles.statement:
The set of patterns of length three consists of
the thirteen words $000$, $001$, $010$, $011$, $012$, $021$, $100$, $101$, $102$, $110$, $120$,
$201$ and $210$.

## Sources

- David Callan and Toufik Mansour, *Ascent Sequences and Weak Ascent Sequences Avoiding a Quadruple of Length-3 Patterns*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A80, Section 1.

articles.title: Sum formulas for $|U_{n,1}|$ and $|V_{n,1}|$ (Proposition 2)
articles.statement:
For every natural number
$n$ let $f(n, a) = \min(n - 3 - a, \lfloor (a - 1)/2 \rfloor)$ and

$$
S(n) = \sum_{a=2}^{n-4} \sum_{k=1}^{f(n,a)} \left( \binom{a-2}{2k} 2^{a-2k-2} +
\binom{a-2}{2k-1} 2^{a-2k-1} \right) (n - k - a - 2).
$$

Then for every $n \ge 1$

$$
|U_{n,1}| = \sum_{k=1}^{\lfloor n/3 \rfloor - 1} \left( \binom{n-k-4}{2k} 2^{n-3k-4} +
\binom{n-k-4}{2k-1} 2^{n-3k-3} \right)
$$

and

$$
|V_{n,1}| = \sum_{a=2}^{n-4} 2^{a-2} (n - a - 3) + S(n),
$$

and for every $n \ge 4$

$$
|V_{n,1}| = 2^{n-4} - n + 3 + S(n).
$$

A sum whose upper limit is below its lower limit is empty, and an exponent such as
$n - 3k - 4$ is negative only where the binomial coefficient multiplying it is $0$; such a
term is $0$. The last formula is stated only for $n \ge 4$: at $n = 3$ the expression
$2^{n-4} - n + 3$ equals $1/2$, while $\sum_{a=2}^{n-4} 2^{a-2} (n - a - 3)$ is $0$.

## Sources

- David Callan and Toufik Mansour, *Ascent Sequences and Weak Ascent Sequences Avoiding a Quadruple of Length-3 Patterns*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A80, Proposition 2.

articles.title: Recurrence for $|U_{n,1}|$ and $|V_{n,1}|$ (Lemma 2)
articles.statement:
Let $f$ be either of the
sequences $u_n = |U_{n,1}|$ and $v_n = |V_{n,1}|$. Then $f_j = 0$ for every $j \le 5$,
$f_6 = 1$, and $f_n = 5 f_{n-1} - 7 f_{n-2} + 2 f_{n-3}$ for every $n \ge 7$.

## Sources

- David Callan and Toufik Mansour, *Ascent Sequences and Weak Ascent Sequences Avoiding a Quadruple of Length-3 Patterns*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A80, Lemma 2.

articles.title: $U_{0,j}$ is empty

articles.title: The sets $U_{n,j}$
articles.statement:
Let $W_n = WA_n(011, 100, 201, 210)$ be the set of weak ascent
sequences of length $n$ that avoid each of the patterns $011$, $100$, $201$ and $210$. For
natural numbers $n$ and $j$, $U_{n,j}$ is the set of sequences $w = w_1 w_2 \cdots w_n$ in
$W_n$ such that the last descent top of $w$ is at position $n - 1$, $w$ has a big entry, the
first $n - 2$ entries of $w$ are not all $0$, $w_{n-1} \ne n - 2$, and $w_{n-1} = w_n + j$.

articles.title: The sets $V_{n,j}$
articles.statement:
Let $W_n = WA_n(011, 100, 201, 210)$ be the set of weak ascent
sequences of length $n$ that avoid each of the patterns $011$, $100$, $201$ and $210$. For
natural numbers $n$ and $j$, $V_{n,j}$ is the set of sequences $w = w_1 w_2 \cdots w_n$ in
$W_n$ such that the last descent top of $w$ is at position $n - 2$, $w_n \le n - 3$,

articles.title: Reducible pattern sets (Theorem 3)
Fibonacci closed form of a binomial sum with powers of two
articles.statement:
Let $F_m$ denote the
Fibonacci numbers, with $F_0 = 0$ and $F_1 = 1$. For every natural number $n \ge 4$,

$$\sum_{k=1}^{\lfloor n/3 \rfloor - 1} \left( \binom{n-k-4}{2k} 2^{n-3k-4} +
\binom{n-k-4}{2k-1} 2^{n-3k-3} \right) + 2^{n-4} = F_{2n-7}.$$

The sum is empty for $n < 6$. When $3$ divides $n$, the last index $k = n/3 - 1$ gives the
exponent $n - 3k - 4 = -1$, but there $\binom{n-k-4}{2k} = 0$, and the product
$\binom{n-k-4}{2k} 2^{n-3k-4}$ is read as $0$; the other product in that summand is $1$.

The source states this as the sum being $F_{2n-7} - 2^{n-4}$. The summand is reconstructed from
an extracted display of the source's Proposition 2(i), as the full text was not available; exact
computation confirms the identity for $4 \le n \le 500$.

## Sources

- David Callan and Toufik Mansour, *Ascent Sequences and Weak Ascent Sequences Avoiding a Quadruple of Length-3 Patterns*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A80, Proposition 3, with the sum of Proposition 2(i).

articles.title: Weak ascent sequences avoiding a set of patterns
articles.statement:
For a finite set $P$ of patterns
(words over $\mathbb{N}$) and a natural number $n$, $\mathrm{WA}_n(P)$ is the set of weak ascent
sequences of length $n$ that contain none of the patterns in $P$.

## Sources

- David Callan and Toufik Mansour, *Ascent Sequences and Weak Ascent Sequences Avoiding a Quadruple of Length-3 Patterns*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A80, Section 1.

articles.title: Motzkin counts for weak ascent sequences in Class 86
articles.statement:
Let $M_n$ denote the Motzkin
numbers. For every natural number $n \ge 3$, the number of weak ascent sequences of length $n$
avoiding every pattern in $\{000, 021, 101, 120\}$, the number avoiding every pattern in
$\{000, 021, 101, 102\}$ and the number avoiding every pattern in $\{000, 021, 110, 120\}$ are
each equal to $M_n + M_{n-2}$.

## Sources

- David Callan and Toufik Mansour, *Ascent Sequences and Weak Ascent Sequences Avoiding a Quadruple of Length-3 Patterns*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A80, Theorem 4.

articles.title: Generating function for weak ascent sequences avoiding 101, 102, 110 and 201
articles.statement:
Let $a_n$
be the number of weak ascent sequences of length $n$ that avoid each of the patterns $101$,
$102$, $110$ and $201$, and let $F = \sum_{n \ge 0} a_n X^n$ in $\mathbb{Q}[[X]]$. For every
power series $S \in \mathbb{Q}[[X]]$ with $S^2 = 1 - 4X$ and constant term $1$,

$$F \cdot 2(1 - X)(1 - 4X - X^2) = (2 - 3X - X^2) S - X - X^2.$$

Such an $S$ is the power series $\sqrt{1 - 4X}$, and $1 - X$ and $1 - 4X - X^2$ are invertible,
so this is the formula
$F = \frac{(2 - 3X - X^2)\sqrt{1 - 4X} - X - X^2}{2(1 - X)(1 - 4X - X^2)}$ with the denominator
cleared.

## Sources

- David Callan and Toufik Mansour, *Ascent Sequences and Weak Ascent Sequences Avoiding a Quadruple of Length-3 Patterns*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A80, Theorem 12.

articles.title: Weakly increasing weak ascent sequences: Catalan and Motzkin counts
articles.statement:
Let $C_n$ denote the
Catalan numbers and $M_n$ the Motzkin numbers. For every natural number $n$, (i) the number of
weakly increasing weak ascent sequences of length $n$ is $C_n$, and (ii) the number of weakly
increasing weak ascent sequences of length $n$ that avoid the pattern $000$ is $M_n$.

At $n = 0$ both counts are $1$, from the empty sequence.

## Sources

- David Callan and Toufik Mansour, *Ascent Sequences and Weak Ascent Sequences Avoiding a Quadruple of Length-3 Patterns*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A80, Proposition 1.

articles.title: Weak-ascent Wilf equivalence in Class 61
articles.statement:
For every natural number $n$, the number of
weak ascent sequences of length $n$ avoiding every pattern in $\{010, 011, 102, 201\}$ equals the
number avoiding every pattern in $\{010, 011, 120, 201\}$.

That is, the two sets are WA-Wilf equivalent.

## Sources

- David Callan and Toufik Mansour, *Ascent Sequences and Weak Ascent Sequences Avoiding a Quadruple of Length-3 Patterns*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A80, Theorem 6.

articles.title: Weak ascent Wilf equivalence and generating function, class 93
articles.statement:
Write $\mathrm{WA}_n(P)$
for the set of weak ascent sequences of length $n$ avoiding every pattern in $P$, with patterns
written as words (for example $011$). The pattern sets $P = \{011, 102, 120, 201\}$ and
$\{011, 102, 120, 210\}$ are WA-Wilf equivalent, that is,
$|\mathrm{WA}_n(P)| = |\mathrm{WA}_n(\{011, 102, 120, 210\})|$ for every $n \ge 0$. Moreover, the
formal power series $F(x) = \sum_{n \ge 1} |\mathrm{WA}_n(P)| \, x^n$ in $\mathbb{Z}[[x]]$
(without the $n = 0$ term) satisfies $F(x) \, (1 - 2x)(1 - x)^2 = x(2x^2 - 2x + 1)$, that is,
$F(x) = \frac{x(2x^2 - 2x + 1)}{(1 - 2x)(1 - x)^2}$.

## Sources

- David Callan and Toufik Mansour, *Ascent Sequences and Weak Ascent Sequences Avoiding a Quadruple of Length-3 Patterns*, INTEGERS 25 (2025), Article A80, Theorem 7.

articles.title: Weak ascent Wilf equivalence, class 99
articles.statement:
Write $\mathrm{WA}_n(P)$ for the set of weak
ascent sequences of length $n$ avoiding every pattern in $P$, with patterns written as words (for
example $011$). The pattern sets $\{011, 100, 102, 201\}$ and $\{011, 100, 120, 201\}$ are WA-Wilf
equivalent: for every $n \ge 0$,
$|\mathrm{WA}_n(\{011, 100, 102, 201\})| = |\mathrm{WA}_n(\{011, 100, 120, 201\})|$.

articles.title: WA-Wilf classes of pattern quadruples
articles.statement:
Write $\mathrm{WA}_n(P)$ for the set of weak ascent
sequences of length $n$ avoiding every pattern in $P$, and call two sets of patterns $P$ and $Q$
WA-Wilf equivalent when $|\mathrm{WA}_n(P)| = |\mathrm{WA}_n(Q)|$ for every $n \ge 0$. As $P$

articles.title: Number of weak ascents of a word
articles.statement:
For a word $a_1 a_2 \cdots a_m$ of natural numbers,
$\mathrm{wasc}(a_1 \cdots a_m)$ is the number of weak ascents, that is, of positions $j$ with
$1 \le j < m$ and $a_j \le a_{j+1}$; in particular the empty word and every word of length one
have no weak ascents.

articles.title: Ascents and descents over permutations avoiding $123$ and $132$
articles.statement:
Let

$$G = \sum_{n \ge 0} \sum_{\sigma} x^n p^{\mathrm{asc}(\sigma)} q^{\mathrm{des}(\sigma)},$$

where $\sigma$ runs over the permutations of $\{0, 1, \dots, n-1\}$ that avoid both patterns
$123$ and $132$, and $\mathrm{asc}(\sigma)$ and $\mathrm{des}(\sigma)$ are the numbers of ascents
and descents of $\sigma$; $G$ is a formal power series in $x$ with coefficients in
$\mathbb{Q}[p, q]$. Then

$$(1 - 2qx - pqx^2 + q^2x^2)\, G = 1 + x - 2qx + px^2 - qx^2 - pqx^2 + q^2x^2.$$

## Sources

- Han, *Joint Distributions of 10 Classical Statistics over Permutations Avoiding Two Patterns of Length 3*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A18, Corollary 1.

articles.title: Ascents and descents over permutations avoiding $132$ and $321$
articles.statement:
Let

$$G = \sum_{n \ge 0} \sum_{\sigma} x^n p^{\mathrm{asc}(\sigma)} q^{\mathrm{des}(\sigma)},$$

where $\sigma$ runs over the permutations of $\{0, 1, \dots, n-1\}$ that avoid both patterns
$132$ and $321$, and $\mathrm{asc}(\sigma)$ and $\mathrm{des}(\sigma)$ are the numbers of ascents
and descents of $\sigma$; $G$ is a formal power series in $x$ with coefficients in
$\mathbb{Q}[p, q]$. Then

$$(1 - px)^3\, G = 1 + x - 3px - 2px^2 + 3p^2x^2 + qx^2 + p^2x^3 - p^3x^3.$$

## Sources

- Han, *Joint Distributions of 10 Classical Statistics over Permutations Avoiding Two Patterns of Length 3*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A18, Corollary 2.

articles.title: Ascents and descents over permutations avoiding $213$ and $231$
articles.statement:
Let

$$G = \sum_{n \ge 0} \sum_{\sigma} x^n p^{\mathrm{asc}(\sigma)} q^{\mathrm{des}(\sigma)},$$

where $\sigma$ runs over the permutations of $\{0, 1, \dots, n-1\}$ that avoid both patterns
$213$ and $231$, and $\mathrm{asc}(\sigma)$ and $\mathrm{des}(\sigma)$ are the numbers of ascents
and descents of $\sigma$; $G$ is a formal power series in $x$ with coefficients in
$\mathbb{Q}[p, q]$. Then

$$(1 - px - qx)\, G = 1 + x - px - qx.$$

The lead-in of the source's Corollary 4 names the permutations avoiding $213$ and $312$ instead;
both classes have this distribution of ascents and descents.

## Sources

- Han, *Joint Distributions of 10 Classical Statistics over Permutations Avoiding Two Patterns of Length 3*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A18, Corollary 4.

articles.title: Ascent–descent generating function of a pair of patterns
articles.statement:
For permutations $\tau$ and
$\rho$ of $\{0, 1, 2\}$, let $S_n(\tau, \rho)$ be the set of permutations of
$\{0, 1, \dots, n-1\}$ that contain neither $\tau$ nor $\rho$ as a classical pattern. The
ascent–descent generating function of $(\tau, \rho)$ is the formal power series

$$\sum_{n \ge 0} \sum_{\sigma \in S_n(\tau, \rho)}
x^n p^{\mathrm{asc}(\sigma)} q^{\mathrm{des}(\sigma)}$$

in $x$ with coefficients in the polynomial ring $\mathbb{Q}[p, q]$, where $\mathrm{asc}(\sigma)$
and $\mathrm{des}(\sigma)$ are the numbers of ascents and descents of $\sigma$. The empty
permutation ($n = 0$) contributes the constant term $1$.

## Sources

- Han, *Joint Distributions of 10 Classical Statistics over Permutations Avoiding Two Patterns of Length 3*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A18, Section 1 (`asc`, `des`).

articles.title: Ten classical statistics over permutations avoiding $123$ and $132$
articles.statement:
Let $F$ be the
joint generating function of the ten classical statistics over the permutations avoiding both
patterns $123$ and $132$: a formal power series in $x$ over
$\mathbb{Q}[p, q, u, v, s, t, y, z, \ell, m]$ in which $x$ marks the length and
$p, q, u, v, s, t, y, z, \ell, m$ mark the numbers of ascents, descents, left-to-right maxima,
right-to-left maxima, left-to-right minima, right-to-left minima, double ascents, double
descents, peaks and valleys, respectively. Then

$$
(1 - \ell m p q s v x^2 - q s x z - q s v x z + q^2 s^2 v x^2 z^2)\, F = 1 +
s x \bigl(t u v + p t^2 u^2 v x - q(\ell m p v x + z + v z)\bigr) +
q^2 s^3 t u v^2 x^3 \bigl(\ell p u x (m - z) + z(-1 - m p t u x + z + p t u x z)\bigr) +
q s^2 v x^2 \bigl(q z^2 + p t^2 u x \bigl(m(u + v) - u(1 + v) z\bigr) +
t u \bigl(-z - v(-1 + \ell p (m - u) x + z)\bigr)\bigr).
$$

## Sources

- Han, *Joint Distributions of 10 Classical Statistics over Permutations Avoiding Two Patterns of Length 3*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A18, Theorem 2.

articles.title: Ten classical statistics over permutations avoiding $132$ and $321$
articles.statement:
Let $F$ be the
joint generating function of the ten classical statistics over the permutations avoiding both
patterns $132$ and $321$: a formal power series in $x$ over
$\mathbb{Q}[p, q, u, v, s, t, y, z, \ell, m]$ in which $x$ marks the length and
$p, q, u, v, s, t, y, z, \ell, m$ mark the numbers of ascents, descents, left-to-right maxima,
right-to-left maxima, left-to-right minima, right-to-left minima, double ascents, double
descents, peaks and valleys, respectively. Then $(1 - ptxy)(1 - puxy)(1 - ptuxy)\, F$ equals

$$
1 + stuvx + pst^2u^2vx^2 + qs^2tuv^2x^2 + mpqs^2t^2u^2vx^3 + mpqs^2t^2uv^2x^3 +
\ell pqs^2tu^2v^2x^3 + \ell mp^2qs^2t^2u^3vx^4 + \ell mp^2qs^2t^2u^2v^2x^4 - ptxy - puxy -
pqs^2tu^2v^2x^3y - pst^2uvx^2y - pstu^2vx^2y - pst^2u^2vx^2y - p^2st^3u^2vx^3y -
p^2st^2u^3vx^3y - pqs^2t^2uv^2x^3y - ptuxy - pqs^2t^2u^2v^2x^3y - mp^2qs^2t^2u^3vx^4y -
\ell p^2qs^2t^2u^2v^2x^4y - mp^2qs^2t^2u^2v^2x^4y - mp^2qs^2t^3u^2v^2x^4y -

p^2tu^2x^2y^2 + p^2st^2u^2vx^3y^2 + p^2st^3u^2vx^3y^2 + p^2st^2u^3vx^3y^2 +
p^3st^3u^3vx^4y^2 + p^2qs^2t^2u^2v^2x^4y^2 + p^2qs^2t^3u^2v^2x^4y^2 +
p^2qs^2t^2u^3v^2x^4y^2 + \ell p^3qs^2t^3u^3v^2x^5y^2 + mp^3qs^2t^3u^3v^2x^5y^2 -
p^3t^2u^2x^3y^3 - p^3st^3u^3vx^4y^3 - p^3qs^2t^3u^3v^2x^5y^3.
$$

## Sources

articles.title: Ten classical statistics over permutations avoiding $213$ and $231$
articles.statement:
Let $F$ be the
joint generating function of the ten classical statistics over the permutations avoiding both
patterns $213$ and $231$: a formal power series in $x$ over
$\mathbb{Q}[p, q, u, v, s, t, y, z, \ell, m]$ in which $x$ marks the length and

t\bigl(u(1 - qvxz)(1 + pqxyz) + pqxz(\ell mqvx + y - qvxyz)\bigr) -
pt^2ux\bigl(-\ell quvx - u(y - 1)(qvxz - 1) + (1 + pqxyz)(\ell mqvx + y - qvxyz)\bigr)\Bigr) -
qs^2tuv^2x^2\Bigl(mptx(ptuxy - 1)\bigl(1 + (\ell - 1)qvxz\bigr) -
(ptxy - 1)\bigl((1 - z)(qvxz - 1) +
ptux\bigl(z(1 + \ell qvx - qvxz) + y(z - 1)(qvxz - 1)\bigr)\bigr)\Bigr) +

articles.title: Generating function of ten classical statistics over a pair of patterns
articles.statement:
For
permutations $\tau$ and $\rho$ of $\{0, 1, 2\}$, let $S_n(\tau, \rho)$ be the set of permutations
of $\{0, 1, \dots, n-1\}$ that contain neither $\tau$ nor $\rho$ as a classical pattern. The
generating function $F_{(\tau, \rho)}$ is the formal power series

$$F_{(\tau, \rho)} = \sum_{n \ge 0} \sum_{\sigma \in S_n(\tau, \rho)} x^n
p^{\mathrm{asc}(\sigma)} q^{\mathrm{des}(\sigma)} u^{\mathrm{lrmax}(\sigma)}
v^{\mathrm{rlmax}(\sigma)} s^{\mathrm{lrmin}(\sigma)} t^{\mathrm{rlmin}(\sigma)}
y^{\mathrm{dasc}(\sigma)} z^{\mathrm{ddes}(\sigma)} \ell^{\mathrm{pk}(\sigma)}
m^{\mathrm{vl}(\sigma)}$$

in $x$ with coefficients in the polynomial ring $\mathbb{Q}[p, q, u, v, s, t, y, z, \ell, m]$.
Here $\mathrm{asc}$ and $\mathrm{des}$ count ascents and descents, $\mathrm{lrmax}$ and
$\mathrm{rlmax}$ left-to-right and right-to-left maxima, $\mathrm{lrmin}$ and $\mathrm{rlmin}$
left-to-right and right-to-left minima, $\mathrm{dasc}$ and $\mathrm{ddes}$ double ascents and
double descents, and $\mathrm{pk}$ and $\mathrm{vl}$ peaks and valleys. The empty permutation
($n = 0$) contributes the constant term $1$.

## Sources

- Han, *Joint Distributions of 10 Classical Statistics over Permutations Avoiding Two Patterns of Length 3*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A18, Section 1 (the g.f. `F_(τ,ρ)`).

articles.title: Double ascents and double descents over permutations avoiding $231$ and $312$
articles.statement:
Let

$$H = \sum_{n \ge 0} \sum_{\sigma} x^n y^{\mathrm{dasc}(\sigma)} z^{\mathrm{ddes}(\sigma)},$$

where $\sigma$ runs over the permutations of $\{0, 1, \dots, n-1\}$ that avoid both patterns
$231$ and $312$, and $\mathrm{dasc}(\sigma)$ and $\mathrm{ddes}(\sigma)$ are the numbers of
double ascents and double descents of $\sigma$; $H$ is a formal power series in $x$ with
coefficients in $\mathbb{Q}[y, z]$. Then

$$(1 - x(y + z) - x^2(1 - yz))\, H = 1 + x^2(1 + x)(1 - y)(1 - z) + x(1 - y - z).$$

The source's Corollary 3 also gives an identity (22) for ascents and descents, marked by $p$
and $q$, and an identity (24) for peaks and valleys, marked by $\ell$ and $m$, over this class;
both are false as printed (at $p = 2$, $q = 1$ the coefficient of $x^5$ in (22) is $75$, the true
value $81$; at $\ell = 2$, $m = 1$ the coefficient of $x^5$ in (24) is $28$, the true value
$29$).

- Han, *Joint Distributions of 10 Classical Statistics over Permutations Avoiding Two Patterns of Length 3*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A18, Corollary 3.

For
permutations $\tau$ and $\rho$ of $\{0, 1, 2\}$, let $S_n(\tau, \rho)$ be the set of permutations

articles.title: Length-three pattern from one-line values
articles.statement:
Given a bijection $v$ from $\{0, 1, 2\}$ to
itself, this is the permutation of $\{0, 1, 2\}$ that sends $i$ to $v(i)$. The values are listed
zero-based, so $v = (0, 2, 1)$ gives the pattern $132$ in the usual one-based one-line notation.

## Sources

- Han, *Joint Distributions of 10 Classical Statistics over Permutations Avoiding Two Patterns of Length 3*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A18, Section 1.

articles.title: Ascents and descents of $123$ and $132$
articles.statement:
Writing permutations of $\{0, 1, 2\}$ in
one-based one-line notation, the identity $123$ has two ascents and no descents,
$\operatorname{asc}(123) = 2$ and $\operatorname{des}(123) = 0$, and $132$ has one of each,
$\operatorname{asc}(132) = \operatorname{des}(132) = 1$.

## Sources

- Han, *Joint Distributions of 10 Classical Statistics over Permutations Avoiding Two Patterns of Length 3*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A18, Section 1 (`asc`, `des`).

articles.title: Ascent number of a permutation
articles.statement:
For a permutation $\sigma$ of $\{0, 1, \dots, n - 1\}$,
$\operatorname{asc}(\sigma)$ is the number of positions $i$ with $i + 1 < n$ and
$\sigma(i) < \sigma(i + 1)$.

## Sources

- Han, *Joint Distributions of 10 Classical Statistics over Permutations Avoiding Two Patterns of Length 3*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A18, Section 1 (`asc`, `des`).

articles.title: Descent number of a permutation
articles.statement:
For a permutation $\sigma$ of $\{0, 1, \dots, n - 1\}$,
$\operatorname{des}(\sigma)$ is the number of positions $i$ with $i + 1 < n$ and
$\sigma(i + 1) < \sigma(i)$.

## Sources

- Han, *Joint Distributions of 10 Classical Statistics over Permutations Avoiding Two Patterns of Length 3*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A18, Section 1 (`asc`, `des`).

articles.title: Double ascents, double descents, peaks and valleys in length three
articles.statement:
Writing permutations
of $\{0, 1, 2\}$ in one-based one-line notation, and $\operatorname{dasc}$,
$\operatorname{ddes}$, $\operatorname{pk}$ and $\operatorname{vl}$ for the numbers of double
ascents, double descents, peaks and valleys, $\operatorname{dasc}(123) = 1$,
$\operatorname{ddes}(321) = 1$, $\operatorname{dasc}(132) = \operatorname{ddes}(132) = 0$,
$\operatorname{pk}(132) = 1$, $\operatorname{vl}(132) = 0$, $\operatorname{pk}(213) = 0$ and
$\operatorname{vl}(213) = 1$.

## Sources

- Han, *Joint Distributions of 10 Classical Statistics over Permutations Avoiding Two Patterns of Length 3*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A18, Section 1 (`dasc`, `ddes`, `pk`, `vl`).

articles.title: Left-to-right and right-to-left extrema of $132$ and $213$
articles.statement:
Writing permutations of
$\{0, 1, 2\}$ in one-based one-line notation, $132$ has $2$ left-to-right maxima, $2$
right-to-left maxima, $1$ left-to-right minimum and $2$ right-to-left minima, and $213$ has $2$
left-to-right maxima, $1$ right-to-left maximum, $2$ left-to-right minima and $2$ right-to-left
minima.

## Sources

- Han, *Joint Distributions of 10 Classical Statistics over Permutations Avoiding Two Patterns of Length 3*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A18, Section 1 (`lrmax`, `rlmax`, `lrmin`, `rlmin`).

articles.title: Permutations of length four avoiding $132$ and $321$
articles.statement:
Exactly $7$ permutations of
$\{0, 1, 2, 3\}$ avoid both patterns $132$ and $321$, that is,
$A_4(132, 321) = 7 = 1 + \binom{4}{2}$.

## Sources

- Han, *Joint Distributions of 10 Classical Statistics over Permutations Avoiding Two Patterns of Length 3*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A18, Theorem 1.

articles.title: Simion–Schmidt enumeration of permutations avoiding two patterns of length three
Permutations of length three avoiding $123$ and $132$
articles.statement:
Exactly $4$ permutations of
$\{0, 1, 2\}$ avoid both patterns $123$ and $132$, that is, $A_3(123, 132) = 4$: of the six
permutations of length $3$, only $123$ and $132$ themselves are excluded.

## Sources

- Han, *Joint Distributions of 10 Classical Statistics over Permutations Avoiding Two Patterns of Length 3*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A18, Theorem 1.

articles.title: Number of permutations avoiding two patterns of length three
articles.statement:
For a natural number $n$
and permutations $\tau$ and $\rho$ of $\{0, 1, 2\}$, $A_n(\tau, \rho)$ is the number of
permutations of $\{0, 1, \dots, n - 1\}$ that contain neither $\tau$ nor $\rho$ as a classical
pattern.

## Sources

- Han, *Joint Distributions of 10 Classical Statistics over Permutations Avoiding Two Patterns of Length 3*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A18, Theorem 1.

articles.title: Position of the smallest entry in $(231, 3124)$-avoiding permutations
articles.statement:
For a natural
number $m$, write $S_m(231, 3124)$ for the set of permutations of $\{0, 1, \dots, m-1\}$ that
avoid both patterns $231$ and $3124$, that is, contain neither of them. Let $n \ge 1$ and let
$j$ be a position with $j + 1 < n$. Then the number of permutations $\sigma \in S_n(231, 3124)$
with $\sigma(j) = 0$ equals $(j + 1) \cdot |S_{n-j-1}(231, 3124)|$.

In the source, positions and values start at $1$: with $k = j + 1$, the number of such
permutations with $\sigma(k) = 1$ is $k \cdot |S_{n-k}(231, 3124)|$ for $1 \le k < n$.

## Sources

- Juan B. Gil, Felix H. Xu, and William Y. Zhu, "Odd-Indexed Fibonacci Numbers via Pattern-Avoiding Permutations", Proposition 11.

articles.title: $(231, 3124)$-avoiding permutations are counted by odd-indexed Fibonacci numbers
articles.statement:
For
every $n \ge 1$, the number of permutations of $\{0, 1, \dots, n-1\}$ that avoid both patterns
$231$ and $3124$, that is, contain neither of them, is the Fibonacci number $F_{2n-1}$, where
$F_0 = 0$ and $F_1 = 1$.

## Sources

- Juan B. Gil, Felix H. Xu, and William Y. Zhu, "Odd-Indexed Fibonacci Numbers via Pattern-Avoiding Permutations", Proposition 10.

articles.title: Smallest entry in the first two positions of $(321, 3412)$-avoiding permutations
articles.statement:
Let
$n \ge 2$. Among the permutations $\sigma$ of $\{0, 1, \dots, n-1\}$ that avoid both patterns
$321$ and $3412$, that is, contain neither of them, the number with $\sigma(0) = 0$ and the
number with $\sigma(1) = 0$ are both equal to the Fibonacci number $F_{2n-3}$, where $F_0 = 0$
and $F_1 = 1$.

In the source's indexing from $1$, these are the permutations with $\sigma(1) = 1$ and with
$\sigma(2) = 1$.

## Sources

- Juan B. Gil, Felix H. Xu, and William Y. Zhu, "Odd-Indexed Fibonacci Numbers via Pattern-Avoiding Permutations", Proposition 8.

articles.statement:
For
every $n \ge 1$, the number of permutations of $\{0, 1, \dots, n-1\}$ that avoid both patterns

articles.statement:
For a natural
number $m$, write $S_m(321, 4123)$ for the set of permutations of $\{0, 1, \dots, m-1\}$ that

articles.title: Classical pattern containment in a permutation
articles.statement:
Let $\sigma$ be a permutation of
$\{0, 1, \dots, n-1\}$ and let $\pi$ be a map from $\{0, 1, \dots, k-1\}$ to itself. Then
$\sigma$ contains the pattern $\pi$ if there are positions $e_0 < e_1 < \dots < e_{k-1}$ in
$\{0, 1, \dots, n-1\}$ such that for all $i, j < k$, $\sigma(e_i) < \sigma(e_j)$ holds exactly
when $\pi(i) < \pi(j)$.

articles.title: The pattern $231$
articles.statement:
The pattern $231$ written with values $0, 1, 2$: the map from
$\{0, 1, 2\}$ to itself sending $0 \mapsto 1$, $1 \mapsto 2$ and $2 \mapsto 0$.

articles.title: The pattern $321$
articles.statement:
The pattern $321$ written with values $0, 1, 2$: the map from
$\{0, 1, 2\}$ to itself sending $0 \mapsto 2$, $1 \mapsto 1$ and $2 \mapsto 0$.

articles.title: The pattern $3124$
articles.statement:
The pattern $3124$ written with values $0, 1, 2, 3$: the map from
$\{0, 1, 2, 3\}$ to itself sending $0 \mapsto 2$, $1 \mapsto 0$, $2 \mapsto 1$ and $3 \mapsto 3$.

articles.title: The permutation pattern $3412$
articles.statement:
The pattern $3412$ with its values shifted down by
one: the map $\{0, 1, 2, 3\} \to \{0, 1, 2, 3\}$ sending $0, 1, 2, 3$ to $2, 3, 0, 1$
respectively.

articles.title: The permutation pattern $4123$
articles.statement:
The pattern $4123$ with its values shifted down by
one: the map $\{0, 1, 2, 3\} \to \{0, 1, 2, 3\}$ sending $0, 1, 2, 3$ to $3, 0, 1, 2$
respectively.

articles.title: Number of positions with two successors
articles.statement:
For every natural number $n$, exactly $n - 2$ of
the positions $i \in \{0, 1, \dots, n-1\}$ satisfy $i + 2 < n$, where $n - 2$ is truncated
subtraction (it is $0$ when $n < 2$).

These are the positions at which a permutation of $\{0, 1, \dots, n-1\}$ can have a double
ascent, a double descent, a peak or a valley.

## Sources

- Han, *Joint Distributions of 10 Classical Statistics over Permutations Avoiding Two Patterns of Length 3*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A18, Section 1.

articles.title: Double ascent of a permutation
articles.statement:
Let $\sigma$ be a permutation of $\{0, 1, \dots, n-1\}$.
A position $i$ is a double ascent of $\sigma$ if $i + 2 < n$ and
$\sigma(i) < \sigma(i+1) < \sigma(i+2)$.

## Sources

- Han, *Joint Distributions of 10 Classical Statistics over Permutations Avoiding Two Patterns of Length 3*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A18, Section 1 (`dasc`).

articles.title: Double descent of a permutation
articles.statement:
Let $\sigma$ be a permutation of $\{0, 1, \dots, n-1\}$.
A position $i$ is a double descent of $\sigma$ if $i + 2 < n$ and
$\sigma(i) > \sigma(i+1) > \sigma(i+2)$.

## Sources

- Han, *Joint Distributions of 10 Classical Statistics over Permutations Avoiding Two Patterns of Length 3*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A18, Section 1 (`ddes`).

articles.title: Peak of a permutation
articles.statement:
Let $\sigma$ be a permutation of $\{0, 1, \dots, n-1\}$.
A position $i$ is a peak of $\sigma$ if $i + 2 < n$ and $\sigma(i) < \sigma(i+1) > \sigma(i+2)$.
Thus the peak entry is $\sigma(i+1)$, and the position recorded is $i$, that of the first of
the three entries.

## Sources

- Han, *Joint Distributions of 10 Classical Statistics over Permutations Avoiding Two Patterns of Length 3*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A18, Section 1 (`pk`).

articles.title: Valley of a permutation
articles.statement:
Let $\sigma$ be a permutation of $\{0, 1, \dots, n-1\}$.
A position $i$ is a valley of $\sigma$ if $i + 2 < n$ and
$\sigma(i) > \sigma(i+1) < \sigma(i+2)$. Thus the valley entry is $\sigma(i+1)$, and the
position recorded is $i$, that of the first of the three entries.

## Sources

- Han, *Joint Distributions of 10 Classical Statistics over Permutations Avoiding Two Patterns of Length 3*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A18, Section 1 (`vl`).

articles.title: Local shape of a position in a permutation
articles.statement:
Let $\sigma$ be a permutation of
$\{0, 1, \dots, n-1\}$ and let $i$ be a position. If $i + 2 < n$, then $i$ is exactly one of a
double ascent, a double descent, a peak or a valley of $\sigma$; otherwise $i$ is none of them.
That is, the number of these four properties that $i$ has is $1$ when $i + 2 < n$ and $0$
otherwise.

## Sources

- Han, *Joint Distributions of 10 Classical Statistics over Permutations Avoiding Two Patterns of Length 3*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A18, Section 1.

articles.title: Sum of the four local statistics of a permutation
articles.statement:
Let $\sigma$ be a permutation of
$\{0, 1, \dots, n-1\}$, and write $\mathrm{dasc}(\sigma)$, $\mathrm{ddes}(\sigma)$,
$\mathrm{pk}(\sigma)$ and $\mathrm{vl}(\sigma)$ for its numbers of double ascents, double
descents, peaks and valleys. Then
$\mathrm{dasc}(\sigma) + \mathrm{ddes}(\sigma) + \mathrm{pk}(\sigma) + \mathrm{vl}(\sigma) = n - 2$,
where $n - 2$ is truncated subtraction (it is $0$ when $n < 2$).

## Sources

- Han, *Joint Distributions of 10 Classical Statistics over Permutations Avoiding Two Patterns of Length 3*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A18, Section 1.

articles.title: Number of double ascents
articles.statement:
For a permutation $\sigma$ of $\{0, 1, \dots, n-1\}$,
$\mathrm{dasc}(\sigma)$ is the number of positions $i$ that are double ascents of $\sigma$.

## Sources

- Han, *Joint Distributions of 10 Classical Statistics over Permutations Avoiding Two Patterns of Length 3*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A18, Section 1 (`dasc`).

articles.title: Number of double descents
articles.statement:
For a permutation $\sigma$ of $\{0, 1, \dots, n-1\}$,
$\mathrm{ddes}(\sigma)$ is the number of positions $i$ that are double descents of $\sigma$.

## Sources

- Han, *Joint Distributions of 10 Classical Statistics over Permutations Avoiding Two Patterns of Length 3*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A18, Section 1 (`ddes`).

articles.title: Number of left-to-right maxima
articles.statement:
For a permutation $\sigma$ of $\{0, 1, \dots, n-1\}$,
$\mathrm{lmax}(\sigma)$ is the number of positions $i$ such that $\sigma(j) < \sigma(i)$ for
every position $j < i$, that is, the number of entries larger than every entry to their left.

## Sources

- Dan Li and Sergey Kitaev, *King Permutations and Partially Ordered Patterns*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A59, Section 1 (statistics).

articles.title: Number of left-to-right minima
articles.statement:
For a permutation $\sigma$ of $\{0, 1, \dots, n - 1\}$
written in one-line notation, $\operatorname{lmin}(\sigma)$ is the number of positions $i$ such
that $\sigma(i) < \sigma(j)$ for every position $j < i$, that is, the number of entries smaller
than every entry to their left.

## Sources

- Dan Li and Sergey Kitaev, *King Permutations and Partially Ordered Patterns*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A59, Section 1 (statistics).

articles.title: Number of peaks of a permutation
articles.statement:
For a permutation $\sigma$ of $\{0, 1, \dots, n - 1\}$
written in one-line notation, $\operatorname{pk}(\sigma)$ is the number of positions $i$ with
$i + 2 < n$ and $\sigma(i) < \sigma(i + 1) > \sigma(i + 2)$, that is, the number of peaks of
$\sigma$.

## Sources

- Han, *Joint Distributions of 10 Classical Statistics over Permutations Avoiding Two Patterns of Length 3*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A18, Section 1 (`pk`).

articles.title: Number of right-to-left maxima
articles.statement:
For a permutation $\sigma$ of $\{0, 1, \dots, n - 1\}$
written in one-line notation, $\operatorname{rmax}(\sigma)$ is the number of positions $i$ such
that $\sigma(j) < \sigma(i)$ for every position $j > i$, that is, the number of entries larger
than every entry to their right.

## Sources

- Dan Li and Sergey Kitaev, *King Permutations and Partially Ordered Patterns*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A59, Section 1 (statistics).

articles.title: Number of right-to-left minima
articles.statement:
For a permutation $\sigma$ of $\{0, 1, \dots, n - 1\}$
written in one-line notation, $\operatorname{rmin}(\sigma)$ is the number of positions $i$ such
that $\sigma(i) < \sigma(j)$ for every position $j > i$, that is, the number of entries smaller
than every entry to their right.

## Sources

- Dan Li and Sergey Kitaev, *King Permutations and Partially Ordered Patterns*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A59, Section 1 (statistics).

articles.title: Number of valleys of a permutation
articles.statement:
For a permutation $\sigma$ of
$\{0, 1, \dots, n - 1\}$ written in one-line notation, $\operatorname{vl}(\sigma)$ is the number
of positions $i$ with $i + 2 < n$ and $\sigma(i) > \sigma(i + 1) < \sigma(i + 2)$, that is, the
number of valleys of $\sigma$.

## Sources

- Han, *Joint Distributions of 10 Classical Statistics over Permutations Avoiding Two Patterns of Length 3*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A18, Section 1 (`vl`).

articles.title: Pain's signed factorial-ratio identity for fixed points
articles.statement:
Let $n$ and $k$ be natural
numbers with $n \ge 2$ and $k \ge 1$. For a permutation $\sigma$ of
$\lbrace 0, 1, \dots, n-1 \rbrace$, write $\operatorname{sgn}(\sigma)$ for its sign and
$\operatorname{fix}(\sigma)$ for its number of fixed points. Then, summing over all permutations
$\sigma$ of this set,

$$\sum_{\sigma} \operatorname{sgn}(\sigma)
\frac{\operatorname{fix}(\sigma)!}{(\operatorname{fix}(\sigma) + k)!} =
\frac{(-1)^{n+1} \left(n^2 + (k-1)n - (k-1)\right)}{(k-1)! (n+k-1)(n+k)}.$$

## Sources

- Jean-Christophe Pain, "Identities for Permutations with Fixed Points", Theorem 3.

articles.title: Pain's signed falling-factorial identity for fixed points
articles.statement:
Let $n$ and $k$ be natural
numbers with $n \ge 2$, $k \ge 1$ and $k + 1 \le n$, and let $x$ be a real number. For a
permutation $\sigma$ of $\lbrace 0, 1, \dots, n-1 \rbrace$, write $\operatorname{sgn}(\sigma)$ for
its sign and $\operatorname{fix}(\sigma)$ for its number of fixed points, and for a natural number
$m$ write $(m)_k = m(m-1)\cdots(m-k+1)$ for the falling factorial. Then, summing over all
permutations $\sigma$ of this set,

$$\sum_{\sigma} \operatorname{sgn}(\sigma) (\operatorname{fix}(\sigma))_k
x^{\operatorname{fix}(\sigma) - k} = \frac{n!}{(n-k)!} (x-1)^{n-k-1} (x + n - k - 1),$$

where a term with $\operatorname{fix}(\sigma) < k$ is $0$ because then
$(\operatorname{fix}(\sigma))_k = 0$.

The left side is the $k$-th derivative in $x$ of
$\sum_{\sigma} \operatorname{sgn}(\sigma) x^{\operatorname{fix}(\sigma)}$.

## Sources

- Jean-Christophe Pain, "Identities for Permutations with Fixed Points", Theorem 2.

articles.title: Central limit theorem for polynomials with nonpositive real zeros
articles.statement:
Let $(Q_n)_{n \ge 0}$
be real polynomials such that every $Q_n$ has only real zeros and all of them are $\le 0$. Put
$\mu_n = Q_n'(1) / Q_n(1)$ and $\sigma_n^2 = Q_n'(1) / Q_n(1) + Q_n''(1) / Q_n(1) - \mu_n^2$, and
let $\sigma_n = \sqrt{\sigma_n^2}$. If $\sigma_n^2 \to \infty$ as $n \to \infty$, then for every
real $x$, the sum of the coefficients of $X^j$ in $Q_n$ over the indices $0 \le j \le \deg Q_n$
with $(j - \mu_n) / \sigma_n \le x$, divided by $Q_n(1)$, tends to $\Phi(x)$ as $n \to \infty$,
where $\Phi$ is the distribution function of the standard normal distribution.

The source asks for negative zeros; zeros at $0$ are also allowed here, since $Q_n = X^m R_n$ only
shifts the coefficient distribution by $m$ and leaves $\sigma_n^2$ unchanged. The local limit
theorem that accompanies this result in the source is not stated.

## Sources

- Moussa Benoumhani, *The Distribution of the Number of Fixed Points in k-Permutations*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A54, Theorem 5.

articles.title: Real-rootedness of the derangement cycle polynomial
articles.statement:
Write $a(m, k, j)$ for the number of
permutations of an $m$-element set with exactly $k$ cycles (fixed points counted as cycles of
length one) and exactly $j$ fixed points, so that $d(m, k) = a(m, k, 0)$ is the number of
derangements of an $m$-element set with $k$ cycles. For every $n \ge 2$, the real polynomial
$D_n(x) = \sum_{k=1}^{n} d(n + k, k) x^{k-1}$ has only real zeros.

The terms with $k > n$ vanish, so the upper summation limit $n$ loses nothing.

## Sources

- Moussa Benoumhani, *The Distribution of the Number of Fixed Points in k-Permutations*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A54, Theorem 3.

articles.title: Fixed points split off a derangement
articles.statement:
Write $a(n, k, j)$ for the number of permutations of
an $n$-element set with exactly $k$ cycles (fixed points counted as cycles of length one) and
exactly $j$ fixed points, and $d(m, i) = a(m, i, 0)$ for the number of derangements of an
$m$-element set with $i$ cycles. For all natural numbers $n$, $k$ and $j$ with $j \le k$,
$a(n, k, j) = \binom{n}{j} \, d(n - j, k - j)$, where $n - j$ is read as $0$ when $j > n$.

The paper assumes $n \ge k \ge 1$; the identity holds for all $n$ and all $k \ge j$.

## Sources

- Moussa Benoumhani, *The Distribution of the Number of Fixed Points in k-Permutations*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A54, Proposition 3 (i).

articles.title: A permutation has at most as many fixed points as cycles
articles.statement:
Write $a(n, k, j)$ for the number
of permutations of an $n$-element set with exactly $k$ cycles (fixed points counted as cycles of
length one) and exactly $j$ fixed points. If $k < j$, then $a(n, k, j) = 0$.

## Sources

- Moussa Benoumhani, *The Distribution of the Number of Fixed Points in k-Permutations*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A54, Proposition 3 (range `0 ≤ j ≤ k` of `a(n, k, j)`).

articles.title: Unimodality of fixed-point counts for permutations with a given number of cycles
articles.statement:
Write
$a(n, k, j)$ for the number of permutations of an $n$-element set with exactly $k$ cycles (fixed
points counted as cycles of length one) and exactly $j$ fixed points. If $k \le n$, then there is
an $m \le k$ such that $j \mapsto a(n, k, j)$ is weakly increasing on $\{0, \dots, m\}$ and weakly
decreasing on $\{m, \dots, k\}$, and every $i \le k$ with $a(n, k, i) = a(n, k, m)$ is $m$ or
$m + 1$.

The paper's "SLC" conclusion is not stated (the abbreviation is not defined in the extracted
statement).

## Sources

- Moussa Benoumhani, *The Distribution of the Number of Fixed Points in k-Permutations*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A54, Corollary 2.

articles.title: Counting the empty permutation
articles.statement:
Write $a(n, k, j)$ for the number of permutations of an
$n$-element set with exactly $k$ cycles (fixed points counted as cycles of length one) and exactly
$j$ fixed points. Then $a(0, 0, 0) = 1$: the empty permutation is the only permutation of the
empty set, and it has no cycles and no fixed points.

## Sources

- Moussa Benoumhani, *The Distribution of the Number of Fixed Points in k-Permutations*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A54, Proposition 3 (definition of `a(n, k, j)`, value at `n = k = j = 0`).

articles.title: Permutations counted by cycles and fixed points
articles.statement:
For natural numbers $n$, $k$ and $j$,
$a(n, k, j)$ is the number of permutations of $\{0, 1, \dots, n - 1\}$ with exactly $k$ cycles
(fixed points counted as cycles of length one) and exactly $j$ fixed points.

## Sources

- Moussa Benoumhani, *The Distribution of the Number of Fixed Points in k-Permutations*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A54, Proposition 3 (definition of `a(n, k, j)`).

articles.title: Real zeros of the fixed-point polynomial
articles.statement:
Write $a(n, k, j)$ for the number of permutations
of an $n$-element set with exactly $k$ cycles (fixed points counted as cycles of length one) and
exactly $j$ fixed points. If $1 \le k \le n$, then the real polynomial
$P(x) = \sum_{j=0}^{k} a(n, k, j) x^j$ has only real zeros.

## Sources

- Moussa Benoumhani, *The Distribution of the Number of Fixed Points in k-Permutations*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A54, Theorem 4.

articles.title: Variance of the number of fixed points of a permutation with a given number of cycles
articles.statement:
Write $a(n, k, j)$ for the number of permutations of an $n$-element set with exactly $k$ cycles
(fixed points counted as cycles of length one) and exactly $j$ fixed points, $c(n, k)$ for the
unsigned Stirling number of the first kind (the number of permutations of an $n$-element set
with $k$ cycles), and $\mu_{n,k} = n \, c(n - 1, k - 1) / c(n, k)$. If $2 \le k \le n$, then
$\frac{1}{c(n, k)} \sum_{j=0}^{k} j^2 \, a(n, k, j) - \mu_{n,k}^2 =
\mu_{n,k} (1 + \mu_{n-1,k-1} - \mu_{n,k})$.

Here $\mu_{n,k}$ is the mean number of fixed points of a uniformly random permutation of an
$n$-element set with $k$ cycles, so the left side is the variance of that number.

## Sources

- Moussa Benoumhani, *The Distribution of the Number of Fixed Points in k-Permutations*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A54, Proposition 4.

articles.title: Recurrence for permutations counted by cycles and fixed points
articles.statement:
Write $a(n, k, j)$ for the
number of permutations of an $n$-element set with exactly $k$ cycles (fixed points counted as
cycles of length one) and exactly $j$ fixed points. For all natural numbers $n$, $k$ and $j$
with $1 \le j \le k$, $j \, a(n, k, j) = n \, a(n - 1, k - 1, j - 1)$, where $n - 1$ is read as
$0$ when $n = 0$.

The paper assumes $n \ge k \ge 1$; the identity holds for all $n$.

## Sources

- Moussa Benoumhani, *The Distribution of the Number of Fixed Points in k-Permutations*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A54, Proposition 3 (iii).

articles.title: Newton's inequalities
articles.statement:
Let $p(x) = \sum_{j=0}^{n} a_j x^j$ be a real polynomial of degree
$n \ge 2$ that splits over $\mathbb{R}$, that is, all $n$ of its zeros, counted with
multiplicity, are real. Then for every $j$ with $1 \le j \le n - 1$,

$$a_j^2 \ge \frac{j + 1}{j} \cdot \frac{n - j + 1}{n - j} \, a_{j-1} a_{j+1}.$$

## Sources

- Moussa Benoumhani, *The Distribution of the Number of Fixed Points in k-Permutations*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A54, Theorem 1.

articles.title: Schur's composition theorem for real-rooted polynomials
articles.statement:
Let $f = \sum_k a_k x^k$ and
$g = \sum_k c_k x^k$ be real polynomials that split over $\mathbb{R}$, and suppose that the zeros
of $g$ are either all $\le 0$ or all $\ge 0$. Let $d = \min(\deg f, \deg g)$, where the zero
polynomial is given degree $0$. Then the polynomial $\sum_{k=0}^{d} k!\, a_k c_k x^k$ also splits
over $\mathbb{R}$.

The paper asks that the zeros of one of the two polynomials lie on the same side of the origin;
by symmetry this is taken to be $g$, and zeros at $0$ are allowed.

## Sources

- Moussa Benoumhani, *The Distribution of the Number of Fixed Points in k-Permutations*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A54, Theorem 2 (Schur).

articles.title: Stirling numbers from fixed-point counts
articles.statement:
For natural numbers $n$, $k$ and $j$, let
$a(n, k, j)$ be the number of permutations of an $n$-element set with exactly $k$ cycles (fixed
points counted as cycles of length one) and exactly $j$ fixed points. Then for all natural
numbers $n$ and $k$,

$$\sum_{j=0}^{k} a(n, k, j) = c(n, k),$$

where $c(n, k)$ is the unsigned Stirling number of the first kind.

The paper assumes $n \ge k \ge 1$; the identity is stated for all $n$ and $k$.

## Sources

- Moussa Benoumhani, *The Distribution of the Number of Fixed Points in k-Permutations*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A54, Proposition 3 (iv).

articles.title: Total number of fixed points of permutations with a given number of cycles
articles.statement:
For natural
numbers $n$, $k$ and $j$, let $a(n, k, j)$ be the number of permutations of an $n$-element set
with exactly $k$ cycles (fixed points counted as cycles of length one) and exactly $j$ fixed
points, and let $c(n, k)$ be the unsigned Stirling number of the first kind. Then for every
natural number $n$ and every $k \ge 1$,

$$\sum_{j=0}^{k} j \, a(n, k, j) = n \, c(n - 1, k - 1),$$

where the right-hand side is read as $0$ when $n = 0$.

Dividing by $c(n, k)$, the number of permutations of an $n$-element set with $k$ cycles, gives the
mean $\mu_{n,k} = n \, c(n - 1, k - 1) / c(n, k)$ of the number of fixed points of a uniformly
random such permutation when $n \ge k$.

## Sources

- Moussa Benoumhani, *The Distribution of the Number of Fixed Points in k-Permutations*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A54, Proposition 4.

articles.title: Positive sequences satisfying Newton's inequalities are unimodal
articles.statement:
Let $n$ be a natural
number and let $(a_j)_{j \ge 0}$ be a sequence of real numbers with $a_j > 0$ for every $j \le n$,
such that

$$a_j^2 \ge \frac{j + 1}{j} \cdot \frac{n - j + 1}{n - j} \, a_{j-1} a_{j+1}$$

for every $j$ with $1 \le j \le n - 1$. Then there is an $m \le n$ such that $(a_j)$ is strictly
increasing on $\{0, \dots, m\}$, and either $(a_j)$ is strictly decreasing on $\{m, \dots, n\}$,
or $m < n$, $a_m = a_{m+1}$ and $(a_j)$ is strictly decreasing on $\{m + 1, \dots, n\}$.

The paper's "SLC" conclusion is not stated (the abbreviation is not defined in the extracted
statement).

## Sources

- Moussa Benoumhani, *The Distribution of the Number of Fixed Points in k-Permutations*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A54, Corollary 1.

articles.title: Adler labels lie in $\{1, \dots, n\}$
articles.statement:
For every natural number $n$ and every set
partition $P$ of $\{-n, \dots, n\}$, every Adler block label $p$ of $P$ is an integer with
$1 \le p \le n$.

## Sources

- Buck, Elder, Figueroa, Harris, Harry, Simpson, *Flattened Stirling Permutations*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A104, Notation 2.3.

articles.title: Adler block labels
articles.statement:
Let $n$ be a natural number and $P$ a set partition of the integer
interval $\{-n, \dots, n\}$; for $x$ in this interval write $P(x)$ for the block of $P$
containing $x$. The Adler block labels of $P$ are the integers $p$ with $1 \le p \le n$ such
that $p \le q$ for every positive $q \in P(p)$ and $p < -q$ for every negative $q \in P(p)$;
that is, $p$ is the least positive element of its block and is smaller than the absolute value
of every negative element of that block.

For a type $B$ set partition the block containing $0$ is never labelled, and from each pair of
blocks $\beta \ne -\beta$ exactly the block containing the element of least absolute value as a
positive element is labelled, by its least positive element; sorting the labels orders these
kept blocks as $\beta_1, \dots, \beta_m$.

## Sources

- Buck, Elder, Figueroa, Harris, Harry, Simpson, *Flattened Stirling Permutations*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A104, Notation 2.3 (arXiv:2306.13034).

articles.title: The map $\varphi$ is a bijection from type $B$ set partitions onto flattened Stirling permutations
articles.statement:
**The map $\varphi$ is a bijection from type $B$ set partitions onto flattened Stirling
permutations.** For a natural number $n$, let $\varphi$ be the map of Buck et al.
(Proposition 1) that sends a set partition $P$ of $\{-n, \dots, n\}$ to a word of length
$2(n + 1)$ over the natural numbers, built from the zero block of $P$ and its Adler-labelled
blocks with each element $i$ replaced by $|i| + 1$. Then $\varphi$ sends the set of type $B$
set partitions of $\{-n, \dots, n\}$ bijectively onto the set of flattened Stirling
permutations of order $n + 1$: $\varphi$ is injective on type $B$ set partitions, sends each
of them to a flattened Stirling permutation of order $n + 1$, and every flattened Stirling
permutation of order $n + 1$ is $\varphi(\pi)$ for some type $B$ set partition $\pi$ of
$\{-n, \dots, n\}$.

## Sources

- Buck, Elder, Figueroa, Harris, Harry, Simpson, *Flattened Stirling Permutations*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A104, Theorem 3.

articles.title: The doubled word of a singleton
articles.statement:
For every natural number $s$, the doubled word of the
singleton $\{s\}$ is $f(\{s\}) = s\,s$, the word of length two whose letters are both $s$.

## Sources

- Buck, Elder, Figueroa, Harris, Harry, Simpson, *Flattened Stirling Permutations*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A104, Lemma 3 (the map `f`).

articles.title: Doubled word
articles.statement:
For a finite set $S = \{s_1 < s_2 < \dots < s_k\}$ of natural numbers, the
doubled word of $S$ is $f(S) = s_1 s_1 s_2 s_2 \cdots s_k s_k$, which lists the elements of $S$
in increasing order with each one written twice; $f(\emptyset)$ is the empty word.

## Sources

- Buck, Elder, Figueroa, Harris, Harry, Simpson, *Flattened Stirling Permutations*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A104, Lemma 3 (the map `f`).

articles.title: A binomial–Stirling formula for the Dowling numbers
articles.statement:
Let $W_{2,1,1}(n, k)$ be the
$(q, r)$-Whitney numbers of the second kind with $m = 2$, $r = 1$ and $q = 1$, and let
$D_n = \sum_{k=0}^{n} W_{2,1,1}(n, k)$ be the associated Dowling numbers. For every $n \ge 1$,

$$
D_n = \sum_{i=0}^{n} \binom{n}{i} \sum_{k=0}^{n-i} 2^{n-i-k} S(n-i, k),
$$

where $S(a, k)$ are the Stirling numbers of the second kind, with $S(0, 0) = 1$.

## Sources

- Buck, Elder, Figueroa, Harris, Harry, Simpson, *Flattened Stirling Permutations*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A104, Corollary 3, formula.

articles.title: Recursion for flattened partitions by number of runs
articles.statement:
Let $f_{n,k}$ be the number of
flattened partitions of length $n$ with exactly $k$ runs. For all $n \ge 1$ and $k \ge 2$,

$$
f_{n,k} = \sum_{m=1}^{n-2} \left( \binom{n-1}{m} - 1 \right) f_{m,k-1},
$$

where the sum is empty when $n \le 2$. Moreover $f_{n,1} = 1$ for every $n \ge 1$, and
$f_{n,k} = 0$ whenever $2 \le n \le k$.

This is the recursion of Nabawanda, Rakotondrajao, and Bamunoba as quoted in the paper.

## Sources

- Buck, Elder, Figueroa, Harris, Harry, Simpson, *Flattened Stirling Permutations*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A104, Theorem 1 (quoting Nabawanda et al., Theorem 1).

articles.title: Flattened partitions counted by runs
articles.statement:
For natural numbers $n$ and $k$, $f_{n,k}$ is the
number of permutations $\sigma$ of $\{0, 1, \dots, n - 1\}$ such that the word
$\sigma(0) \sigma(1) \cdots \sigma(n - 1)$ is flattened (the leading letters of its runs, read
left to right, are weakly increasing) and has exactly $k$ runs, where a run is a maximal
contiguous weakly increasing subword. These are the flattened partitions of length $n$ of
Nabawanda, Rakotondrajao, and Bamunoba, with letters $0, \dots, n - 1$ in place of
$1, \dots, n$.

## Sources

- Buck, Elder, Figueroa, Harris, Harry, Simpson, *Flattened Stirling Permutations*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A104, Section 1 (flattened partitions, after Nabawanda, Rakotondrajao, and Bamunoba).

articles.title: Flattened Stirling permutations are counted by Dowling numbers
articles.statement:
For every $n \ge 1$, the
number $|\mathrm{flat}(Q_{n+1})|$ of flattened Stirling permutations of order $n + 1$ equals the
Dowling number $D_n = \sum_{k=0}^{n} W_{2,1,1}(n, k)$, where $W_{2,1,1}(n, k)$ are the
$(q, r)$-Whitney numbers of the second kind with $m = 2$, $r = 1$ and $q = 1$.

## Sources

- Buck, Elder, Figueroa, Harris, Harry, Simpson, *Flattened Stirling Permutations*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A104, Corollary 1.

articles.title: A binomial–Stirling formula for flattened Stirling permutations
articles.statement:
For every natural number
$n$, the number of flattened Stirling permutations of order $n + 1$ is

$$
|\mathrm{flat}(Q_{n+1})| = \sum_{i=0}^{n} \binom{n}{i} \sum_{k=0}^{n-i} 2^{n-i-k} S(n-i, k),
$$

where $S(a, k)$ are the Stirling numbers of the second kind, with $S(0, 0) = 1$.

## Sources

- Buck, Elder, Figueroa, Harris, Harry, Simpson, *Flattened Stirling Permutations*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A104, Theorem 4.

articles.title: Number of flattened Stirling permutations
articles.statement:
For a natural number $n$,
$|\mathrm{flat}(Q_n)|$ is the number of flattened Stirling permutations of order $n$: words
$w_1 w_2 \cdots w_{2n}$ of natural numbers that are Stirling permutations of order $n$ and whose
runs (maximal contiguous weakly increasing subwords) have weakly increasing leading letters,
read from left to right.

## Sources

- Buck, Elder, Figueroa, Harris, Harry, Simpson, *Flattened Stirling Permutations*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A104, Section 1.

articles.title: Exactly one flattened Stirling permutation has one run
articles.statement:
For every natural number
$n \ge 1$, exactly one flattened Stirling permutation of order $n$ has exactly one run.

## Sources

- Buck, Elder, Figueroa, Harris, Harry, Simpson, *Flattened Stirling Permutations*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A104, Proposition 2, part 1.

articles.title: Closed form for flattened Stirling permutations with two runs
articles.statement:
For every natural number
$n \ge 1$, the number $|\mathrm{flat}_2(Q_{n+1})|$ of flattened Stirling permutations of order
$n + 1$ with exactly two runs equals $3(2^n - 1) - 2n$.

## Sources

- Buck, Elder, Figueroa, Harris, Harry, Simpson, *Flattened Stirling Permutations*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A104, Corollary 2.

articles.title: Recursion for flattened Stirling permutations with two runs
articles.statement:
Write
$|\mathrm{flat}_2(Q_n)|$ for the number of flattened Stirling permutations of order $n$ with
exactly two runs. Then $|\mathrm{flat}_2(Q_1)| = 0$, and for every natural number $n \ge 1$,
$|\mathrm{flat}_2(Q_{n+1})| = 2\,|\mathrm{flat}_2(Q_n)| + 2n - 1$.

## Sources

- Buck, Elder, Figueroa, Harris, Harry, Simpson, *Flattened Stirling Permutations*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A104, Proposition 2, part 2.

articles.title: Counting flattened Stirling permutations by runs
articles.statement:
For natural numbers $n$ and $k$,
$|\mathrm{flat}_k(Q_n)|$ is the number of flattened Stirling permutations of order $n$ with
exactly $k$ runs, where a run is a maximal contiguous weakly increasing subword.

## Sources

- Buck, Elder, Figueroa, Harris, Harry, Simpson, *Flattened Stirling Permutations*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A104, Section 1.

articles.title: Exponential generating function of the Dowling numbers
articles.statement:
For $n \ge 0$ let $D_n$ be the
$n$-th Dowling number of the group of order $2$, that is, the $(q, r)$-Dowling number
$D_n = \sum_{k=0}^{n} W_{2,1,1}(n, k)$ built from the $(q, r)$-Whitney numbers of the second
kind with $m = 2$, $r = 1$, $q = 1$. Then for every complex number $x$ the series
$\sum_{n \ge 0} D_n x^n / n!$ is summable with sum $\exp\bigl(x + (e^{2x} - 1)/2\bigr)$.

## Sources

- Buck, Elder, Figueroa, Harris, Harry, Simpson, *Flattened Stirling Permutations*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A104, Corollary 3, generating function.

articles.title: A flattened word with four runs
articles.statement:
The word
$w = 1\,1\,2\,2\,9\,9\,3\,8\,8\,3\,4\,6\,6\,7\,7\,4\,5\,5$ of length $18$ is flattened (the
leading letters of its runs, read left to right, are weakly increasing), and it has exactly
$4$ runs, where a run is a maximal contiguous weakly increasing subword.

## Sources

- Buck, Elder, Figueroa, Harris, Harry, Simpson, *Flattened Stirling Permutations*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A104, Section 1 (example).

articles.title: Flattened words
articles.statement:
A word $w = w_1 w_2 \cdots w_m$ of natural numbers is flattened when
the leading letters of its runs, read left to right, are weakly increasing. Here a run is a
maximal contiguous weakly increasing subword, so position $i$ starts a run when $i = 1$ or
$w_{i-1} > w_i$; the condition is that $w_i \le w_j$ whenever $i < j$ and both positions
start runs.

## Sources

- Buck, Elder, Figueroa, Harris, Harry, Simpson, *Flattened Stirling Permutations*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A104, Section 1 (flattened).

articles.title: Maximum number of runs of a flattened Stirling permutation
articles.statement:
For every natural number
$n \ge 1$, some flattened Stirling permutation of order $n$ has exactly
$\lceil 2n/3 \rceil$ runs, and no flattened Stirling permutation of order $n$ has more.

## Sources

- Buck, Elder, Figueroa, Harris, Harry, Simpson, *Flattened Stirling Permutations*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A104, Lemma 5.

articles.title: The one-block partition is of type B
articles.statement:
For every natural number $n$, the partition of
the integer interval $[-n, n] = \{-n, \dots, n\}$ into a single block is a type $B$ set
partition: its only block is closed under negation, so it is the unique block equal to its own
negative (the zero-block).

## Sources

- Buck, Elder, Figueroa, Harris, Harry, Simpson, *Flattened Stirling Permutations*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A104, Definition 1; characteristic check of `IsTypeBSetPartition`.

articles.title: Type $B$ set partitions
articles.statement:
